articleTitle: Optimization of Reliability in ACP100 Automatic Depressurization System Squib Valve Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To address the issue of excessively high probability of failure on demand (PFD) in the squib valve control system of the ACP100 automatic depressurization system, which arises from the inability to effectively identify failures in the latching module constructed using relays and hardware threshold comparison modules, an analysis of the squib valve control system's functionality was conducted. Based on reliability modeling, a sensitivity analysis of PFD was performed to identify the components that have the most significant impact on the PFD of the squib valve control function. Optimization strategies were proposed from a system-wide perspective, aimed at reducing the undiagnosable dangerous failure rate of the latching module or mitigating its effects. Three reliability enhancement approaches were investigated: shortening the periodic test interval, implementing redundant latching modules, and incorporating diagnostic latching logic. The optimized schemes result in a reduction of the PFD average (PFDavg) to less than 1/60 of the original design at most. Notably, the optimization scheme of latching logic diagnosis based on software implementation does not add additional hardware equipment, system design complexity and maintenance complexity.

articleTitle: Probability Evaluation Method for Thermal Fatigue Life of Surface Mount Components Based on Physis of Failure Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The nuclear instrument control systems contains tens of thousands of surface mount components. The evaluation of thermal fatigue life in the design stage is helpful to ensure the continuous and stable operation of the operation stage. When analyzing the thermal fatigue life of surface mount components, there are many uncertain factors, including random and interval uncertain variables. The thermal fatigue life without considering the fusion of multiple uncertainties may lead to the unreliability of the evaluation results. In this paper, a probabilistic evaluation method of thermal fatigue life based on physis of failure simulation is proposed. The interval variables are transformed into random variables to complete the characteristic parameter sampling based on the probability sampling method. Then, the uncertainty propagation is realized by random physis of failure simulation, and the thermal fatigue life is probabilistically quantified. A patch resistance case is used to verify the method proposed in this paper. The results show that the method can effectively fuse the random and interval uncertainty variables and obtain the thermal fatigue life probability results of the device.

articleTitle: Assessment of Tapered Roller Bearing Assembly Status with Friction Torque Based on Stacked Deep Autoencoder and BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The magnitude of rolling bearing frictional torque is an important performance parameter that affects bearing power consumption and life. In this paper, the tapered roller bearing in transmission device is investigated as the research object, and the assembly test is designed to study the influence law of bearing assembly tolerance, temperature, speed, radial load and preload force on the friction torque of tapered roller bearing. Firstly, the monitoring signals are processed by a stacked deep autoencoder to automatically extract the critical features. Secondly, a back propagation (BP) neural network model is employed to learn the mapping connection between the parameter information and the friction torque. And then the prediction of the tapered roller bearings friction torque is realized. It is verified that the relative errors of the predicted friction torque under three different working conditions are ≤ 0.1, which satisfies the requirements of engineering applications.

articleTitle: LBTCN with Self-Attention for Bearing's Remaining Useful Life Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Bearings are the core components of mechanical equipment, making it crucial to monitor their performance during operation. Currently, deep learning-based methods for predicting remaining useful life (RUL) provide a data-driven approach to assess bearing performance. Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) are one such architecture capable of parallel computation of sequence data, strictly adhering to causality. While TCNs prevent future data leakage, they overlook the value of nearby and past data in offline modeling. This study proposes an LBTCN architecture that utilizes bidirectional information within local windows while maintaining global causality, enhanced by a self-attention mechanism to highlight valuable information. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher prediction accuracy compared to typical prediction networks.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Useful Life and Health Management for Optical Fiber Links in Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Optical cables serve as the foundation of communication network, carrying the vast majority of data flow, especially bulk data services in data centers. When optical fiber links fail, it would severely impact information communication. This paper analyzes the failure mechanisms of optical fiber links, summarizes the main factors influencing the useful life of optical fiber links, and establishes a multi-stress degradation model to further clarify the relationship between them. Building on that, reasonable suggestions for health management of optical fiber links are proposed, aiming to enhance the reliability and stability of information transmission and extend their useful life.

articleTitle: Design of Power System Platform for Testability Demonstration
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: As aircraft power systems continue to evolve, this paper introduces a power system platform tailored for the testability demonstration of airborne products. The platform addresses the varied power needs of these products and their associated equipment, including specialized injection of power failure. This highly integrated platform supports multiple power systems and diverse outputs, addressing both power supply and needs of testability demonstration for airborne products. The successful design and development of this platform significantly enhance the speed of establishing airborne product testing environments and the efficiency of testability demonstration.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Application of Train Air Brake Systems Under Strong Noise using Enhanced Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In high-speed train, the intricate nature of air brake systems coupled with fluctuating operating environments often leads to raw data being heavily contaminated with noise, presenting substantial challenges for current deep learning-based fault diagnosis methods. To address these issues, this paper introduces a noise-resilient optimized residual network. This approach is composed of three main components: the Inverted Residual Block (IRB), Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), and a soft thresholding function (ST-func). The IRB establishes signal correlations, enhances inductive bias capability, and extracts richer local feature information by varying the input channel dimensions. ECA serves as side paths for residual basic blocks, improving the model's perception of relationships between different channels in the input signal features, thereby increasing attention to critical channels. Finally, features learned from the Global Average Pooling and ECA modules are input into the ST-func to eliminate irrelevant features. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to existing mainstream deep learning fault diagnosis methods, the proposed approach offers significant advantages in terms of lightweight design and robustness in handling noisy fault diagnosis tasks.

articleTitle: Tool-Workpiece Contact Detection Using Adaptive Kalman Filtering and Spectral Flux
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Detection of tool-workpiece contact is crucial for ensuring the machining accuracy and health management of CNC machines. However, traditional detection methods require complex geometric modeling or multiple sensors, leading to high costs and poor real-time performance. To address these issues, a tool-workpiece contact detection approach utilizing adaptive Kalman filtering and spectral flux is proposed. The adaptive Kalman filter is employed to denoise the raw signals, thereby improving signal quality. Subsequently, the most impactful frequency band is extracted from the denoised signal, and its spectral flux is calculated to achieve real-time detection of the tool-workpiece contact state. Furthermore, actual engineering data is analyzed to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The results show that this method offers significant advantages in terms of noise resistance, detection accuracy and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Study on Communication System Fault Prediction Based on Multivariate Grey Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Considering the characteristics of communication systems, such as complex structure, high integration, working principle and fault mechanism, this paper proposes to use the Multivariate Growth Model (MGM) for fault prediction based on the data, utilizing the Grey System Theory. The proposed model covers multiple characteristic variables causing communication system faults, monitors and predicts the characteristic variables in the operation of the communication system based on time series, and takes the predicted values as the basis for fault prediction. The comparative analysis shows that the proposed MGM method has good prediction accuracy, and provides a feasible solution for predicting the critical faults of complex communication systems.

articleTitle: A Low Resource Fault Diagnosis Model Based on CDAN Domain Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Facing the problem of insufficient labeled data, which is common in the field of fault diagnosis, this study proposes an approach based on the CDAN domain adaptation model. The performance of the fault diagnosis model is improved by fusing data from different fault types. Experiments conducted on the Case Western Reserve University sliding bearing dataset validate the effectiveness of this method compared to traditional model training and direct data augmentation strategies, which achieves higher data utilization and fault diagnosis accuracy. Feature space visualization analysis further confirms the effectiveness of feature alignment between source and target domains.

articleTitle: Research on Performance Degradation Prediction of Power Driver Considering Multiple Stresses
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Power driver is one of the key components in electronic system, its performance degradation and function failure will affect the normal operation of the whole system. Therefore, it is important to study the performance degradation prediction of power driver. In this paper., the multi-stress accelerated degradation test of power drive device is designed., performance degradation parameters are collected., data are preprocessed by mean filtering., and a performance degradation prediction model of power drive device based on PSO-BP neural network is constructed., and the model is trained and tested by the test data. The results show that the root mean square error of PSO-BP neural network prediction is 4.3e-4., the prediction accuracy is high., and the prediction trend fits well with the test data., indicating that the prediction model is suitable for the accelerated degradation performance prediction of power drive devices., and provides a method for the health state prediction of electronic system.

articleTitle: Assessment of Machine Learning Techniques for Identifying Demagnetization Stress in PMSG Using Flux and Current Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This study focuses on the detection of faults in wind turbine operations to ensure reliability, safety, and cost efficiency. It introduces a machine learning-based diagnostic approach for identifying various faults, including eccentricity faults, stator short circuits, and both damaged and aging magnets in a 25 kW Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG). A 2D simulation model utilizing the Finite Element Method (FEM) to analyze the output monitoring signals and assess the performance of the machine learning algorithms. Moreover, the study uses stator current and leakage flux signals, applying the Matching Pursuit (MP) for feature extraction. Furthermore, the performance of 17 sub-classifiers across three core machine learning classifiers-Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), and Ensemble techniques-is evaluated for diagnosing demagnetization faults in PMSG. The results reveal that when leakage flux signals are used as the output, seven out of the seventeen classifiers achieved 100% accuracy in classifying all faults in PMSG. In contrast, only four classifiers reached the same level of accuracy using current signals. This indicates that leakage flux signals provide a more reliable basis for diagnosing multiple demagnetization faults in PMSG, making any of the seven successful machine learning sub-classifiers a viable choice for this task.

articleTitle: A Reliability Analysis Model based on Time Alignment of Multi-source Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Prognostic and health management (PHM) technology improves the effectiveness of system maintenance and protection, enabling the implementation of preventative maintenance and self-maintenance. Nevertheless, the current research on the PHM solely concentrates on the development of the model and neglects the processing of degradation data. There is currently a lack of study on PHM technology from a systems viewpoint, as well as a lack of research on the design of systems from the standpoint of real-world challenges. To address these issues, this paper utilizes degraded data processing as its foundation, achieves multi-sensor data alignment through time alignment, further constructs the degraded model, and implements reliability estimation. Finally, the validity of the proposed model is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Construction of Bearing HI Based on Digital Twin and KOA-CNN-LSTM RUL Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: traditional remaining useful life (RUL) prediction techniques for rolling bearings are affected by complex operating conditions, noise interference, and weak vibration signals, leading to poor prediction accuracy and limited generalization in practical applications. To address this issue, a digital twin-assisted KOA-CNN-LSTM method for bearing RUL prediction is proposed. Firstly, establish a dynamic simulation model of rolling bearings using digital twin technology. This model is based on a bearing dynamics model combined with measured signals to estimate the evolution of bearing defects, and uses the least squares method to match the root mean square (RMS) value of vibration signals with the corresponding relationship between defect size. Import the excitation of evolutionary defects into the bearing simulation model, create a simulation model that reflects the degradation process of the bearing, generate simulated vibration signals for the entire life cycle of the bearing, and use the generated simulation data to construct the bearing health factor. Next, a KOA-optimized CNN-LSTM model for bearing RUL prediction is proposed. The processed simulated signals are used as input to the model, where the CNN extracts local information from the vibration signals and mines deep features. The features extracted by the CNN are then fed into the LSTM layer to capture the long-term and short-term dependencies of the time series. The best hyperparameters obtained from the KOA-optimized CNN-LSTM model are used to train the model and generate prediction results. Experimental results indicate that the predicted outcomes of the proposed method exhibit a favorable monotonic trend and can closely approximate the actual life values.

articleTitle: Interpretable Pipeline Burst Pressure Prediction Model Based on PCA-HHO-Xgboost
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Pipeline transportation plays a crucial role in long-distance oil and gas transport today, which could pose a threat to the lives and properties of local residents if damage occurs. Thus being able to accurately predict the burst pressure of corroded pipelines has a vital role to play in the life-cycle operational management of pipelines. This paper proposes an interpretable model for predicting pipeline burst pressure. Firstly, the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is used to reduce the dimensions of the original features, obtaining new features that are more informative. Subsequently, Xgboost is employed to predict the pipeline burst pressure, with the Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) then utilized to optimize the hyperparameters of Xgboost. Finally, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) is utilized to interpret the prediction outcomes of PCA-HHO-Xgboost, clarifying the impact of each feature on the pipeline burst pressure.

articleTitle: Determination of Reliability Improvement Objects Based on Aircraft MTBUR Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Based on the operational reliability data of a certain type of regional aircraft, this study identifies the equipment that need to be carried out reliability improvement by calculating and analyzing the aircraft-level MTBUR (Mean Time Between Unscheduled Removals), ATA system-level MTBUR, and equipment MTBUR on a step-by-step basis. In this process, the cost and the maintenance time of removed equipment are also taken into consideration to finally identify the equipment. The research results show that this method can well identify the key items which affect aircraft reliability indexes and effectively reduce the cost and time for product reliability improvement.

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling and Estimation for Electromechanical System Under Periodic Varying Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Using motor current signals for reliability modeling and estimation can minimize the damage to the mechanical transmission mechanism in electromechanical systems and save costs. In some cases, the transmission system suffered from varying loads, which may lead to a substantial difference in the amplitude of current signals across the entire life. For instance, joint reducers in industrial robots are subjected to varying loads at different stages in a single task, with the amplitude of the current have distinguishing differences; therefore, we cannot predefine one failure threshold for the reliability estimation of such systems. In this paper, we propose a periodic multistage task modeling approach based on the Wiener process, which considers varying loads and failure thresholds at different stages of a periodic task. A closed-form reliability function is derived when the stages are independent. The developed method is verified by a periodic varying load test on an industrial robot's harmonic reducer. Results show that the developed model is more accurate and reasonable for systems under periodic varying loads.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Parameter Study of High Performance Zinc Oxide Piezoelectric Films for Flexible Surface Acoustic Wave Biosensors
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Current methods for assessing chronic wounds are quite limited, and traditional examination techniques may cause secondary damage to the wound. To address this issue, researchers have proposed biosensors for real-time monitoring of wound conditions. Flexible Surface Acoustic Wave (FSA W) sensors, with their advantages of high biocompatibility, high sensitivity, miniaturization, and mass manufacturability, have emerged as an ideal choice for wound monitoring. These sensors consist of a flexible substrate, piezoelectric film, interdigital transducers (IDT), and a sensitive layer. However, the fabrication of high-quality piezoelectric films presents several challenges, including material selection, crystal quality, deposition rate, and process stability. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the fabrication techniques for high-performance piezoelectric films in FSA W biosensors, focusing on preparation methods and optimization strategies under various process conditions.

articleTitle: A Rolling Bearing Condition Assessment Method Driven by Data-Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Rolling bearings are critical components in the operation of machinery, and their performance directly affects the safety and stability of the entire system. However, the challenge lies in the difficulty of accurately capturing the wear process of rolling bearings, making it hard for traditional models to predict their actual operating conditions accurately. To overcome this problem, this study introduces a new data-model driven approach to assess the health of rolling element bearings. This new method first utilizes deep learning technology to build an advanced network model aimed at deeply analyzing and extracting key information during the bearing degradation process. By effectively integrating this key information, this paper construct an index system that accurately reflects the degradation trend of the bearings. Subsequently, the method employs stochastic process theory to establish a mathematical model of rolling bearing degradation, providing a detailed description of the degradation process. Finally, the previously constructed degradation indicators are input into this model to predict the remaining useful life of the bearings and assess their overall operating condition. This innovative assessment method allows for more precise monitoring and management of the health status of rolling bearings, providing strong technical support for equipment maintenance and fault prevention.

articleTitle: Integrated Multimodal Fault Diagnosis of Industrial Gearboxes Using Vibration Signals and Infrared Thermal Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the increasing demand for precision in fault diagnosis of gearboxes in complex systems, diagnostic methods based solely on vibration signal characteristics have shown limitations. Therefore, multimodal information fusion technology has become a new trend in the field of gearbox fault diagnosis. This article innovatively proposes a multimodal diagnostic method that combines vibration signals with thermal images, aiming to use thermal imaging technology to intuitively capture the thermal changes during gearbox operation and integrate vibration signals to comprehensively reflect fault characteristics. By introducing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for feature depth extraction, this method effectively improves the parsing ability of fault information, thereby enhancing the accuracy and reliability of fault diagnosis. Experimental data confirms that compared to diagnostic methods using a single signal source, the method proposed in this paper performs well in fault detection of helical gearboxes, significantly improving diagnostic accuracy and precision.

articleTitle: Fault Prediction in Elevator Door System Using Motor Motion Control Information
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The door system is an important part of an elevator, and faults within this system can affect the overall operation of the elevator and potentially cause harm to passengers. Therefore, fault prediction is an invaluable tool for accident prevention. This paper aims to develop a practical and effective method for detecting and recognizing early signs of impending faults in the elevator door system. The proposed method is based on motor motion control information, from which relevant feature variables are extracted using statistical analysis and spatial path similarity analysis techniques. The prediction of early fault symptoms in the elevator door system is performed using the Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). The proposed method is validated using real data obtain from an experimental test bench, and its performance is compared with other methods on same datasets. The results show the superiority of the ANFIS classifier.

articleTitle: Research on Flight Dynamics Modeling and Simulation Technology of Large Transport Fixed-Wing UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The aerodynamic structure of large transport fixed-wing UAV is mainly composed of fuselage, wing, horizontal stabilizer, vertical stabilizer, engine, landing gear and so on. The aerodynamic interference between various aerodynamic structures presents different states with the change of speed. The flight dynamics model parameters must be modified according to the different speeds of the UAV in order to obtain a mathematical model with high confidence. In addition, it is necessary to adjust the control law strategy at different speeds to achieve stable and controllable flight within entire speed envelope which ensures the conformance with flight quality requirements of the UAV. Therefore, the flight dynamics model of large transport fixed wing is established based on wind tunnel data. In order to improve the confidence of the mathematical simulation model, the model was modified using flight test data. At each trim point, the nonlinear dynamics model is linearized to obtain the open-loop aero-dynamic characteristics of the UAV. On this basis, the stability enhancement loop is designed and the simulation verification is conducted. The results show that the reliability of the nonlinear aerodynamic model is high, and the trim results of the mathematical model are basically consistent with the wind tunnel test data. The distribution of the feature roots of the high-order and low-order linear models can maintain a good consistency. The mathematical model for 5-ton large transport fixed-wing UAV is established successfully, and the stability augmentation control strategy is proved to have good stability and maneuverability within the required flight envelope.

articleTitle: Enhanced Phase Demodulation for Vibration-Based Fault Detection of Wind Turbine Drivetrain
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Vibration-based fault detection plays a vital role in monitoring rotary machinery systems such as aircraft Propulsion systems and wind turbines. Detecting their failures early is crucial for ensuring their safety and reliability. One of the main challenges is identifying system faults using non-stationary vibration measurements caused by variable-speed operation. In many cases operating speed has high fluctuations (>±10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) that limit the fault detection performance. In this paper, we introduce an improved method for extracting speed profile from a vibration signal utilizing a geometric feature within a rotating machinery system such as gearboxes, actuators and ball-screws. The performance of the enhanced method has been successfully validated using international benchmarking datasets for wind turbine gearboxes.

articleTitle: Imbalanced Inter Shaft Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on SAGAN-DANN
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the actual operation of aircraft engines, the early fault diagnosis of inter shaft bearings is extremely challenging due to their complex and variable working conditions and the difficulty in collecting sufficient vibration signals in advance. To address this issue, a cross-domain fault diagnosis model for inter shaft bearings based on small samples is proposed. This model first utilizes the Self-Attention Generative Adversarial Network (SAGAN) to augment limited vibration signals, capturing complex temporal patterns and structures through the self-attention mechanism. Secondly, it employs the Domain Adversarial Neural Network (DANN) to extract domain-invariant features through adversarial training. Finally, an intelligent diagnostic network is used to identify the health status of inter shaft bearings with unknown labels under variable working conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately and effectively achieve cross-domain inter shaft bearing fault diagnosis with limited available samples, and performs excellently in cases of imbalanced source domain samples. This provides a new approach for early fault identification in aircraft engines.

articleTitle: Research on the FPGA Reconfiguration Technology Based on RS Code for Nuclear Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) is now widely used in nuclear safety Instrumentation and Control (I&C) systems and operates core features like communication, signal capturing and processing, peripheral controlling etc. Those features are crucial to the entire system, which means the state of the FPGA is vital to the system as well. In nuclear I&C industry, single event effect (SEE) is a common hazard faced by the nuclear facilities which are exposed to the high radiation environment, because it may cause register upsets on static random-access memory (SRAM) devices and interfere the well-functioning of them. One popular method to solve this issue is fault diagnose, while this method only finds out the errors, not corrects them. To improve the solution, forward error correction technology, which is widely used in communication industry, is proposed to combine with the FPGA reconfiguration to check and rectify the upsets. Reed-Solomon (RS) Code is chosen to reinforce the core configuration data and to correct the faults by reconfiguration when diagnose problems occurs. Experiment was taken on the demo board to verify the viability of this strategy. The results indicate that this strategy can improve the FPGA against single event upset (SEU), thereby increase the system reliability in this aspect.

articleTitle: The Impact of Embedding Four Different Kinds of FBGs on the Strength of the Carbon Fiber Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This study embeds four types of fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs)-SM-FBG, M-FBG, PI-FBG, and Normal-FBG-into composite structures and assesses their embedding feasibility through tensile and compression tests on carbon fiber specimens. Results show that M-FBG has the highest survival rate, followed by SM-FBG, while Normal-FBG has the lowest due to coating carbonization during curing. Embedding FBGs affects the tensile Young's modulus by less than 10%, and the compressive modulus by up to 17.7%. With SM-FBG achieving the highest compressive strength and the minimal impact on carbon fiber modulus. The relative difference in compressive modulus for SM-FBG is 8.2 %, with a relative difference in tensile modulus of 7.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> at 0 degrees and 0.8% at 90 degrees. Therefore, the FBGs used in this experiment are all capable of strain sensing, with SM-FBG being more suitable as a strain sensor for carbon fiber structural components.

articleTitle: Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis Method Based on DBO-VMD-TCN
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In response to the complex working environment of rolling bearings and the issue of low fault identification due to noise interference in vibration signals, a rolling bearing fault diagnosis method based on DBO-VMD-TCN is proposed. Firstly, the parameters of VMD are optimized using DBO to decompose into k Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). Secondly, the IMFs that contain rich fault information are selected through evaluation indicators, and nine features including mean, variance, peak value, kurtosis, effective value, peak factor, impulse factor, waveform factor, and margin factor are calculated. Finally, the TCN model processes these attributes for training and forecasting, culminating in a precise fault diagnosis rate. Employing vibration signals from the Case Western Reserve University's rolling bearings, the method's effectiveness is confirmed. It adeptly captures fault-related traits and accurately pinpoints the bearings' fault status. The results underscore the method's high diagnostic precision and its substantial potential for practical implementation.

articleTitle: Research for Civil Aircraft Operational Safety Scenario Design and Risk Assessment Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Safety assessment of civil aircraft is crucial to the entire development and airworthiness certification process. As aircraft systems become increasingly integrated, complex, and automated, pilots are often underprepared for emergency situations during operation, which can lead to operational errors and unintended consequences. Therefore, a comprehensive safety analysis of delivered aircraft must account for various operational scenarios. In this paper, we construct a multi-dimensional matrix of aircraft operational safety scenarios, allowing for the organic overlay of these scenarios. The overlaid operational scenarios are then used to conduct risk assessments, thereby identifying high-risk scenarios and providing strategies for the formulation of risk mitigation measures.

articleTitle: Dynamic Performance and Structural Integrity Monitoring of Bogie Based on Digital Twin Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: A frame structure of bogie digital twin construction is proposed, which can realize the real-time dynamic display and feedback design of key technical indexes of dynamics and structural strength. The four key technologies and technical routes of bogie twin modeling are described. The simulation methods and detailed steps of bogie dynamics twin model and structural strength twin model are given. Some simulation test design schemes are compared and analyzed and an optimal proposal scheme is proposed. A technical route of agent model based on deep learning neural network is proposed, and the effectiveness and accuracy of the model are verified by the cases of wheel rail force prediction and wheel-set stress prediction. The results of this study can be used to guide the development of the core module of digital twin engineering application of bogie and deploy it on the ground center.

articleTitle: Research on Enhancing the Reliability of Priority Logic Selection Module Based on Sneak circuit Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In order to further enhance the reliability of the priority logic selection module, this study utilizes sneak circuit analysis technology to analyze the module from the perspective of non-component failure, thereby increasing the dimensions and content of module reliability analysis. The analysis results serve as input for optimizing the module design and improving its reliability. The analysis results of priority logic selection module indicate that there are sneak circuit in the module. The triggering of these sneak circuit not only affects the reliability of the module itself, but also leads to faults in the nuclear safety classification DCS system or abnormalities in the dedicated drive, directly threatening the reliability of the nuclear safety classification DCS system. Therefore, eliminating the influence of sneak circuit can improve the reliability of the priority logic selection module.

articleTitle: Welding Defect and Robot Fault Prediction Methods Based on Historical Knowledge
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Failures of different components of the welding robot system may cause the same welding defects, which will waste time and personnel energy in troubleshooting the causes of welding defects. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a method to predict robot equipment failure based on welding defects based on knowledge graph theory. This method first uses statistical ideas to preprocess manually recorded historical data to obtain the proportion of different robot component failures in each type of welding defect. Then the knowledge graph method is used to establish a relationship model between welding defects and robot equipment failures, and analyze the correspondence between welding defects and robot equipment failures. Finally, the welding defects produced during the robot welding process are input into the established relational model to predict the location of the robot equipment failure. Moreover, welding defects and robot equipment failures that occur again in actual production are allowed to be input into the established model, and new welding defects and equipment failures are also allowed to continue to be input into the established model. The established model can be continuously iteratively optimized through newly input welding defect and equipment failure data to continuously improve the completeness and accuracy of the relationship model. The practicality of the established relationship model is verified through the manually recorded welding defect and robot failure history data in actual production. The research results can be used to guide robot equipment failures caused by welding defects during the robot welding process.

articleTitle: Allocation of Testability Indicators for Aircraft Electromechanical Systems Based on Improved AHP
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Due to the increasing degree of system integration of the new generation of aircraft, and the lack of data in the early stage of engineering development, the testability allocation method for complex systems such as electromechanical systems is obviously insufficient. In order to solve this dilemma, an improved Analytic Hierarchy Process(AHP) based testability indicators allocation method is adopted. Qualitative and quantitative analysis methods are combined, and evaluation criteria such as failure rate, failure impact, mean time to repair, cost and demand of fault detection and isolation are introduced. By determining weight coefficients, the testability allocation indicators for each subsystem are finally given. By comparing the results of indicator allocation with other scaling methods, it is demonstrated that the improved allocation method is more accurate and reasonable.

articleTitle: Structural Crack Imaging Under Temperature Variation Based on Gaussian Mixture Model and Guided Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The environment and operation conditions (EOCs) of aircraft structures pose a significant challenge for advancing structural health monitoring from laboratory to practical applications. To address this problem, a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and guided wave (GW) based imaging method is presented here for effective crack monitoring in aircraft metal structures under the influence of EOCs. In this method, in order to suppress the EOCs introduced uncertain influence and to generate EOCs independent feature signal, which is solely influenced by structural damages, the GMM is adopted. During the monitoring process, utilizing the derived EOCs independent feature signals enables the execution of GW imaging, yielding a damage map that facilitates accurate damage localization. The method is validated on a perforated aluminum plate from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-50{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, confirming reliable damage imaging and localization.

articleTitle: Cross-Material Adversarial Neural Network Tool Wear Monitoring for Drilling Aerospace Stacks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the aerospace sector, multi-material stacks are widely used. However, it is harder for monitoring tool wear in drilling the stacks, due to the non-uniformed properties of materials leading data distribution shifts for the models. To address the inconsistent feature distribution, this work proposed a cross-domain adaption network to examinate tool wear in drilling CFRP/AI stacks. The adversarial-based adaptation is established and incorporated channel attention mechanism to promote learning domain invariant features. It adapts to data distribution shifts, offering a robust tool condition monitoring for the complete drilling process. The experiment validated the performance of network, showing the improvements in tool wear monitoring accuracy. The cross-material adversarial neural network contributes to improving tool wear monitoring for multi-material stacks.

articleTitle: Storage Reliability Prediction of a MEMS Gyroscope Based on Accelerated Degradation Test
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The degradation mechanism of MEMS gyroscopes is complex, characterized by volatility and nonlinearity. Accurate storage reliability prediction for highly reliable and long-lifetime MEMS gyroscopes is challenging. This study predicts the storage reliability and lifespan of the sensor by conducting accelerated degradation tests on MEMS gyroscopes and utilizing performance degradation data. Firstly, a constant stress accelerated degradation test based on temperature stress was designed, and the failure data were obtained Then, the constraint relationship between the Wiener process drift parameter and diffusion parameter is derived from the test data. Combining with the Arrhenius model, the acceleration models of the drift parameter and diffusion parameter are derived. Thus, the storage reliability and reliable life of the MEMS gyroscopes under normal storage conditions are obtained.

articleTitle: Damage Detection Based on Modal Shapes of Wing
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the current aircraft maintenance process, non-destructive testing is mainly used for damage detection, which has the advantages of simple operation and direct results. However, there are also shortcomings such as low detection efficiency and intermittent damage detection, making it difficult to continuously monitor the health status of the structure. Good research results have been achieved in identifying modal parameters of structures in existing studies, but there is relatively few research on modal parameter identification and damage detection of wing structures. This paper presents NExT-ERA method to identify the modal parameters of wing structures, and the identification results are in good agreement with the theoretical results; Simultaneously, the change rate of curvature modal shape is used as an identification indicator to detect structural damage. The method presented in the paper is based on structural modal shapes for damage identification, which can help to construct an aircraft structural health monitoring (SHM) system.

Author Keywords: change rate of curvature modal shape

articleTitle: AI-Driven Parameters Optimization of Smooth Vertical Sidewall Trench in DRIE Process Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Deep Reactive Ion Etching (DRIE) is a critical process in the fabrication of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) and other advanced semiconductor devices. Achieving the desired trench profile with minimal defects remains a significant challenge due to the complex interplay of various process parameters. This paper focuses on optimizing parameters such as etching cycle time and passivation cycle time in the DRIE process. An improved central composite design method was employed to design 18 sets of etching recipe experiments. Actual etching profile data collection was conducted, resulting in 1800 sets of etching profile data, which serve as the foundation for subsequent AI algorithm optimization. Through real data experiments, effective etching recipes for high-precision smooth vertical sidewalls were identified. It was found that an etching/passivation ratio in the range of 1.09 to 1.4 could achieve 90-degree sidewalls, while a ratio between 1.09 and 1.5 could achieve scallop heights below 90 nm. Furthermore, based on convolutional neural networks and data-driven models, the predictive models are proposed for etching profile angles and scallop smoothness. The results demonstrated a high prediction accuracy, with only a 5.5% error in the etching profile angle prediction. The optimized etching results and recipes identified in this study achieve highly smooth sidewalls. This work not only enhances the quality of etching processes but also contributes significantly to the advancement of AI applications in semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: Lifetime Prediction and Spares Quantity Optimization for Non-Similar Standby Systems Based on Spares Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: A standby system is a vital means to extend system operational time, and enhance fault tolerance and reliability. Modern industrial processes are complex and coupled, requiring the design of standby systems with different types of operating components in series or parallel to achieve specific functions. This paper addresses the scenario where spare parts experience random performance degradation during storage, focusing on non-similar standby systems. It establishes degradation models for various types of operating components and spare parts, deriving the life probability density functions (PDFs) for different standby subsystems. By leveraging the logical relationships among the standby subsystems, the paper derives the life formula for the non-similar standby system. Furthermore, with the operational time of the non-similar standby system as the objective function, the paper constructs an optimization function to determine the optimal inventory quantities for different types of spare parts within a given budget.

articleTitle: Arrangement of Signal Measuring Points of Planetary Gear Transmission Based on Dynamics Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Planetary gear box has complex structure and high failure rate. How to effectively reveal the fault characteristics of the key components in the planetary gear box and find and solve the fault in time is the focus and difficulty of current research. This paper takes the planetary gear meshing system as the research object, combines multi-body dynamics and finite element analysis, considers the transmission path of vibration signals, establishes a rigid-flexible coupling model, analyzes the characteristics and causes of the vibration signals obtained by simulation, seeks the best measuring point position of the vibration acceleration sensor, and verifies the effectiveness of the simulation model through the measured signals.

articleTitle: Fast Spectral Kurtosis Technique and its Application for Gearbox Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Because of the complexity of the motion of the gearbox, the vibration signal components are complex, and the amplitude and frequency modulation are very serious. However, the early fault characteristics are covered up or affected by the vibration response of other movements because they are very weak. Therefore, it is very difficult to separate the fault characteristic information directly from the original signal. To solve this problem, the fast spectral kurtosis technique introduced in this paper can enhance the weak signal and identify the early fault.

articleTitle: Condition identification and health assessment of electromechanical equipment based on similarity hierarchical clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the context of intelligent manufacturing and industrial automation, this paper addresses the problem of difficulty in establishing a fixed baseline for health assessment due to changes in operating conditions and environmental variations during the operation of electromechanical equipment. A hierarchical clustering method based on Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) distance is proposed. This method calculates the DTW distances between pairwise signals and constructs a weighted matrix using key feature parameters for clustering, enabling effective categorization of the equipment's operating conditions. By constructing health baselines under different operating conditions, this approach facilitates the classification and evaluation of various parameter features of the electromechanical equipment. The overall health status of the equipment is obtained through weighting, and the method has been validated on an industrial robot, with results demonstrating its strong practicality.

articleTitle: A Domain Generalization Network via Meta-Learning for Motor Fault Diagnosis Under Unseen Working Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Intelligent motor fault diagnosis has emerged as an effective tool to ensure reliability and safety of industrial equipment. However, as motors always work under varying conditions, intelligent fault diagnosis methods may fail when facing an unseen working condition. To tackle this problem and improve the generalization ability of model, a domain generalization network based on meta-learning is constructed for motor fault diagnosis. A synthetic testing domain is split from source domains, and meta-train and meta-test are performed on the training and testing domains, respectively. The meta-learning process aims to ensure that the model has good generalization on unseen domains. Experiments on multiple cross-condition motor fault diagnosis tasks verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Development of Integrated Vibration-Temperature Sensor for Bearing Fault Diagnosis and Safety Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper presents a high-range, compact, high-resonance frequency vibration-temperature integrated sensor designed for the application requirements of fault diagnosis and safety monitoring of tail rotor joystick bearings. The specific dimensions of the sensitive structure were simulated and optimized based on the FEA software of COMSOL. The sensor uses platinum resistance and piezoelectric ceramics to detect temperature and vibration, respectively. The sensor elements are then integrated with the sensor structure, completing the fabrication of the integrated vibration and temperature sensor. Finally, the main performance indicators of the sensor, including sensitivity, sensitivity error, and resonance frequency, were tested and found to meet the development requirements.

articleTitle: Research on Joint Reliability Test Methods for Software-Intensive Avionics Products Based on Scenario Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Software-intensive systems play a critical role in complex airborne products, where the system-level failure mechanisms are closely related to the interaction between software and hardware. These failures not only impact the reliability and safety of the system but also the integrity of its functionality. These systems typically have high functional requirements and complex failure mechanisms, with physical redundancy in resources. Therefore, thorough validation during the design phase is crucial to ensure comprehensive and sufficient testing. Standards such as DO178 and DO254 provide guidance in the reliability validation of such systems. However, existing research shows that the scenarios used in software-hardware joint reliability test designs do not sufficiently cover all possible operational conditions and environments. This shortfall may lead to undetected software-hardware integration issues, compromising the comprehensiveness and accuracy of reliability assessments. Moreover, there is a lack of research on software-intensive systems. This paper conducts an indepth analysis of scenario models, integrating the design and development characteristics of commercial aircraft avionics systems, and focusing on the mission scenarios and capability requirements of software-hardware intensive systems. It proposes a novel method for constructing software-hardware joint reliability test profiles based on scenario models. This approach comprehensively captures the requirements for reliability integration testing, conducting system-level and component-level reliability integration testing based on model-based techniques, and serving as a primary basis for reliability validation.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Approach for Predicting the Remaining Useful Life of Aircraft Brake Disc
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The aircraft brake system is responsible for maintaining the static weight of the aircraft, absorbing the impact of dynamic loads and dissipating the kinetic energy of the aircraft during landing. Aircraft brake disc is one of the most critical parts of the aircraft to achieve braking and ensure safe flight. Once the brake disc wear exceeds the threshold, it will lead to reduction of braking efficiency, and in serious cases, the aircraft will run off the runway. Therefore, we conduct five commonly used data-driven prognostic approaches to estimate the remaining useful life of aircraft brake discs. Firstly, the wear dataset of aircraft brake discs is presented. Following that, five commonly used remaining useful life prediction methods are introduced briefly. At last, the methods are applied to the same dataset respectively, and the experimental results are compared and analyzed.

articleTitle: A Detection Tool Damage Framework Based on Improved GMM and Cross-Correlation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: As the core structure of the machine tool, cutting tools' health status monitoring has the vital meaning for machining process of advanced CNC. Besides of the tool cutting process, workpiece replacement and other processes are also interspersed in the process of automatic machining. However, traditional signal processing methods only can be used for continuous signals. When facing the actual signal, it is not possible to adaptively lock the effective processing. The redundancy of acquisition signal limits the application of intelligent diagnosis method in machine tools. In this paper, a tool damage monitoring method based on improved Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and cross-correlation algorithm is proposed. Firstly, an improved Gaussian mixture model is used to adaptively intercept the effective machining process, then, the cross-correlation method is used to determine the consistency between machining processes and to determine the health state of the tool. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is verified by real engineering data, and the tool state health monitoring is realized.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Rotating Machinery RUL Prediction Based on Reptile Framework and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of rotating machinery is important in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) of industrial equipment. Traditional RUL prediction methods rely on large amounts of labeled data, making it challenging to meet the prediction needs in data-scarce situations. This paper proposes a Transformer-based meta-learning algorithm for few-shot RUL prediction of rotating machinery. The method constructs a meta-learner based on Transformer and conducts meta-training under the Reptile framework, enabling the model to learn general knowledge across multiple tasks and rapidly adapt to new tasks with limited samples. Experiments on the CMAPSS dataset demonstrate that this method performs well under few-shot conditions.

articleTitle: Fault Prediction of Landing Gear Actuator Based on Attention-GRU Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The landing gear system operates in a complex environment with heavy impact loads, leading to a high failure rate and extensive maintenance tasks. This paper focuses on a specific civilian aircraft's landing gear retractable system. A hydraulic simulation model is built to simulate normal operations, and by adjusting model parameters, two typical faults caused by component degradation are simulated, providing data support for subsequent fault prediction. This paper proposes a fault prediction method for typical failure modes of landing gear retractable actuators using the Attention mechanism and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU). By assigning corresponding weights to different features of fault data through the Attention mechanism, the GRU model adequately learns crucial data and reduces the loss of long sequence data. This enhances fault prediction accuracy compared to GRU, Support Vector Regression (SVR), Long Short-term Memory (LSTM), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), and Attention-LSTM methods. Mean Absolute Error and Mean Squared Error are chosen as evaluation metrics. Experimental results demonstrate the higher prediction accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis with Noise-Resistant Multi-Dimensional Integrated Convolutional Residual Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: A novel three-dimensional six-branch optimised convolutional neural network (MS-MD-CNN) is proposed to address the multimodal characteristics in rolling bearing input signals. The model combines a residual network (ResNet) and a self-attention mechanism, aiming to comprehensively capture different forms of input signals and thus improve the accuracy of rolling bearing fault diagnosis. In the data preprocessing stage, data enhancement is performed by introducing Gaussian noise and randomisation methods to simulate the real environment, increase the diversity of the data, and verify the model's ability to resist noise. Meanwhile, the multi-branch structure of MS-MD-CNN effectively mines the feature information of multimodal signals. To solve the problem of information transfer and gradient vanishing, the model introduces residual connectivity. Finally, the single-head self-attention mechanism is designed for adaptive learning of the relationship between features to enhance the model's feature extraction ability and suppression of noise in the classification task. The model is evaluated using the Western Reserve University dataset, and the experimental results show some practical value.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis and Measurement of Drone Tasks Based on Environmental Interference Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The analysis and evaluation of drone task reliability is a pressing issue, especially for fundamental tasks such as target recognition. This paper proposes a reliability analysis and evaluation method for drone target recognition tasks based on environmental interference simulation experiments. By designing the task profile for target recognition, the process of the target recognition task, the involved software and hardware systems, and potential influencing factors are clarified. Based on simulation experiments of external environments, such as wind fields, the impact of such interference on drone flight attitude and target recognition tasks is analyzed. By measuring the changes in algorithm recognition accuracy before and after interference, the reliability of drone target recognition tasks can be evaluated to a certain extent. This paper provides a method for analyzing and measuring the reliability of drone task execution from the perspective of software and hardware system coupling, which can guide drones and other unmanned systems to perform tasks more reliably.

articleTitle: Feature Separation of Health Factors for Domain-Adaptive Battery Capacity Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Accurate capacity estimation is essential for the operational safety of lithium-ion batteries. Traditional domain-adaptive methods, while aligning features across different domains, often overlook important domain-specific features, which can lead to reduced predictive accuracy. To address this issue, we propose the Health Factor Feature Separation Network (HFFS-Net), a novel approach designed to separate hidden representations of handcrafted health factors into domain-invariant and domain-specific features. This strategic separation preserves critical degradation information, improving adaptability across various usage conditions. Comparative experiments show that HFFS-Net outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, delivering superior accuracy in capacity estimation, which is crucial for ensuring battery safety.

articleTitle: Performance Degradation Characteristics Extraction of Lithium-ion Batteries Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Currently, lithium-ion batteries, with their high energy density and memoryless effect, are comprehensively applied to the fields of aerospace, new energy vehicles, and mobile terminal devices. However, the performance degradation caused by capacity loss will weaken the efficiency of lithium-ion batteries, and even cause property damage and casualties in serious cases. Battery capacity is a physical quantity that reflects the remaining useful life of the battery, but collecting the capacity data of battery directly is costly and has a long cycle. Therefore, this paper proposes a Performance Degradation Characteristics (PDCs) extraction method to find PDCs that can indirectly and effectively reflect the decline of battery capacity. First, a characteristic extraction method based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is proposed to extract PDCs from original battery data, which can automatically learn the characteristic representation, and possesses high extraction efficiency and strong generalization ability. Second, Nine PDCs, including seven Measurable Characteristics (MCs) and two Computational Characteristics (CCs), are extracted to describe the battery capacity decline validly. Finally, The feasibility and effectiveness of the extraction method are verified by using the nine PDCs to predict the remaining using life of lithium-ion batteries based on a series of CNN models.

articleTitle: Pognotis and Health Mnagement of Reactor Equipment Based on Cloud-Edge-Terminal Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the rapid development of cloud computing technology and the increasing intelligence of various reactor equipment in nuclear power plants, fault prediction and health management have become more and more important. Generally, traditional machine learning methods face the problem of difficulty in adequately handling massive data, which poses a serious challenge to health management. However, the Cloud-Edge-Terminal framework, which tightly integrates cloud computing, edge computing, and terminal devices for efficient data processing and business services, provides new ideas to solve the above. Firstly, this paper describes the importance of reactor equipment fault diagnosis, then reviews the development of fault diagnosis at various stages, then integrates the cloud-edge-end architecture into reactor critical equipment health management, and focuses on the technological approaches involved in reactor equipment prognostics and health management under this model, and finally discusses future research directions and development trends.

articleTitle: Prognostics and Health Management Technology for Aircraft Assembly Production Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: At present, it is difficult to accurately capture and transmit the status data of key links in aircraft assembly production lines, and the operating status of equipment cannot be quantified in real-time. The cost and difficulty of emergency maintenance are high. The performance level of each state, the probability of equipment failure, and the remaining useful life (RUL) are difficult to calculate precisely. Based on the actual operation of precision machining system equipment on the aircraft assembly production line, a model is built using the performance degradation state, fault conditions, and expected life during its working process. A device performance prediction method based on the CNN-LSTM neural network algorithm is proposed. The CNN-LSTM classifier fully screens long time series information through gating units and uses effective information for time series prediction. After preprocessing the samples, they are input into the CNN-LSTM prediction model to predict the failure time and probability of the equipment. Then, by adjusting the size of the time window, an optimal performance binary classification model is obtained to better adapt to the needs of predictive maintenance. This better achieves Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) of the precision machining system on the aircraft assembly production line in engineering.

articleTitle: Reliability Improvement of Acoustofluidic Devices for Cell Separation Through Optimized Micro/Nano Fabrication Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper presents the fabrication process and reliability enhancement of surface acoustic wave (SAW) microfluidic chips, specifically designed for the critical task of separating circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from red blood cells (RBCs), a pivotal step in both clinical diagnostics and biological research. The acoustofluidic device integrates interdigital transducers (IDTs) and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) chambers, created through advanced micro/nano-fabrication techniques such as photolithography and electron beam deposition. The study explores how key fabrication parameters, including exposure energy and development time, affect the structural and functional integrity of SAW devices. We also address the challenges involved in fabricating thinfilm electrodes and investigates the critical role of hard baking in forming durable microfluidic channels. Insights from this study contribute to advancing the reliability of microfluidic chips, though further research is necessary to fully comprehend the long-term impact of fabrication variations on device performance.

articleTitle: A Novel Method of Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on FDS-MOMEDA and IMCKDA
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Rolling bearings play an important role in ensuring the normal operation of machines, so the importance of bearing fault diagnosis is increasingly being emphasized. However, due to severe noise interference in the measurement signal, traditional methods are difficult to extract bearings features. Therefore, this study proposes a new method that combines the adjusted multipoint optimal minimum entropy deconvolution (FDS-MOMEDA) and the improved maximum correlation kurtosis deconvolution adjusted (IMCKDA) to distinguish the fault type of the bearings. Firstly, the improved MOMEDA method, FDS-MOMEDA, is used to denoise the original signal. Secondly, IMCKDA is applied to the denoised signal to enhance the pulse pattern of bearing faults, thereby extracting effective fault feature information. Finally, the fault type of the bearing is determined through the Hilbert envelope spectrum. By processing vibration signals from real experimental datasets, the results show that this method can effectively extract fault features of rolling bearings.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a PHM Vibration Monitoring System for Rail Vehicles Based on the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The principal constraints associated with conventional rail vehicle vibration monitoring systems pertain to their substantial volume, intricate wiring configuration, and restricted operational range. In light of the shortcomings of the extant railway vehicle vibration monitoring systems, this paper proposes a PHM vibration monitoring system for rail vehicles based on the Internet of Things (IoT). The system is capable of wireless data transmission, exhibits a high sampling rate, and employs IoT technology to reduce system costs. The MESH wireless intelligent network is utilized to transmit data collected by edge node sensors to the central node and subsequently uploaded to the cloud. Moreover, the system incorporates GPS and RTC modules for real-time positioning and timing. At the edge node level, the sampling rate can reach up to 2000 Hz. In comparison with the commercial equipment, the system has been tested for effectiveness and reliability. It is capable of collecting crucial vibration acceleration data for fault diagnosis and Prognostics Health Management (PHM) on rail vehicles.

articleTitle: Civil Aircraft Functional Reliability Requirements Capture and Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: As the complexity of civil aircraft continues to increase, ensuring their reliability becomes more important. As a leading manufacturer of civil aircraft, there is necessary to accurately capture aircraft-level top-level requirements in order to meet stakeholder requirements. As a key part of aircraft reliability design assessment, functional reliability assessment is an important design methodology to improve the level of aircraft reliability and complements previous reliability efforts. Through functional reliability requirement capture and decomposition, it can help leading manufacturer to grasp aircraft functions and the impact of failure states, and facilitate the subsequent better development of system and equipment specifications. This paper describes the process and results of functional reliability requirements capture and decomposition to guide the implementation.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Temperature Effects on a Silicon MEMS Resonator for Reliable Temperature Sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Temperature is a crucial environmental fact for power devices, sensing equipment or computing systems. MEMS resonator-based temperature sensors have been widely used in these areas due to their high performance, high reliability and low-cost production. Changes in temperature can cause variations in the elastic modulus and coefficient of thermal expansion of silicon, leading to shifts in resonant frequency. To achieve high-sensitivity and high-precision temperature sensors, it is necessary to modulate the temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF) of a MEMS resonator. This paper proposes numerical analysis of the temperature effects on a silicon MEMS resonator with degenerated doping. Temperature theoretically influences the Young's modulus of the silicon material within a I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>BAR structure. Finite element simulations are conducted on the degenerately doped silicon resonator, by analyzing the temperature impact on resonant modes, S-parameter and Q-factor. The results reveals that the TCF of the resonator in the LE mode is approximately −22.88 ppm/°C and the Q value changes from 71632 to 71711 in the temperature range of −40 to 85°C.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction of Uniform Demagnetization Faults Based on Joint Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper investigates the uniform demagnetization fault of permanent magnet synchronous motors through joint simulation. The joint simulation is built by Ansys Electronics Desktop and Simulink, which can simulate the finite element model of the motor with control methods. In Ansys Electronics Desktop, the average value of the dq axis inductance of the motor is calculated through a finite element model. In Simulink, a sliding mode observer was used to estimate the back electromotive force and rotational speed. The estimated rotational speed value was compared with the simulated rotational speed value, verifying the accuracy of the sliding mode observer. According to the simulation results, two types of fault features were extracted separately in transient and steady-state conditions.

articleTitle: A Health Management Platform Architecture Design for Civil Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper introduces a design for a Health Management computer architecture for civil aircraft, grounded in the Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA). The proposed architecture exhibits robust scalability and flexibility, facilitating data interaction across various devices and subsystems, with services capable of being invoked both locally and remotely. The platform software based on SOA technology utilizes the APEX port in accordance with the ARINC653 specification for data exchange. The service layer software can be ported between operating systems that comply with the A653 specification without the need for code modification. The infrastructure layer, which includes drivers, supports incremental driver integration. This paper introduces the system's architectural design and implementation principles and validates the functionality of the system through examples.

articleTitle: RUL Prediction of Rolling Bearings Based on Crested Porcupine Optimization Algorithm Optimized CNN-BiGRU-Attention Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: A traditional rolling bearing life prediction model often suffers from low prediction accuracy and weak robustness. To further enhance the accuracy and robustness of the prediction model, a rolling bearing remaining useful life (RUL) prediction model is proposed, integrating four modules: the Crested Porcupine Optimization (CPO), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and Attention mechanism. Firstly, to accurately describe the bearing degradation process, a Health Indicator (HI) for the bearing is constructed using Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Then, fault points on the HI curve are detected using Cumulative Sum (CUSUM), and the steady-state data is removed. Finally, the data after the fault points is input into the CPO-CNN-BiGRU-Attention model for RUL prediction. Through comparative validation with CPO-BiGRU-Attention, CPO-CNN-Attention, CPO-CNN-BiGRU, and CNN-BiGRU-Attention models, it is demonstrated that the proposed RUL prediction method achieves the lowest prediction error and the highest prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of an Auxiliary Equipment for Testability Test of Airborne Electronic Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the increasing thermal power consumption, heat flux per unit volume and surface area of airborne electronic equipment, testability test is faced with problem of ensuring different heat dissipation requirements of various airborne electronic equipment. Aiming at the heat dissipation requirements of different airborne electronic equipment, this paper designs an auxiliary equipment for testability test that integrates liquid cooling source and air-cooling source. The test auxiliary equipment provides a reference for the design of similar air-cooling source and liquid cooling source.

articleTitle: Fault Mechanism Assisted Intelligent Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Improved Generative Adversarial Network for Two-Stage Gearbox
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
