abstract: Artificial intelligence and digital twin technology show the excellent ability in the fault prognostic and health management of machinery equipment. However, interaction between the data driven and physical informed is a challenge for modeling the digital twin framework. In response to this limitation, a fault mechanism assisted intelligent fault diagnosis method based on improved generative adversarial network for digital twin two-stage gearbox is proposed. Firstly, the twenty-six degree-of-freedom dynamic model is established to realize the virtual entity of two-stage gearbox. The initial parameters of dynamic model are determined by the prior knowledge based on the fault mechanism of gear. Then, the improved generative adversarial network is designed to achieve the interaction of virtual entity and physical entity. The measured signal from the physical entity is used to train the proposed model for minimizing the difference of simulation signal from the dynamic model. The loss of proposed model is introduced by combining the physics knowledge of gear dynamic mechanism and observations from the sensor. Finally, the proposed method is applied to simulate the vibration signal of gear fault under different conditions that is consistent with the measured signal, which can be applied for the fault diagnosis of gear. The two-stage gearbox fault experiments with missing sample are used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Research on the Risk of Hot-Swapping in Safety-Class DCS Based on Sneak Circuit Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In nuclear safety-grade Distributed Control System, to enhance the rapid maintenance and replacement capabilities of the DCS system, reduce Mean Time To Repair (MTTR), and improve maintainability, it is necessary to insert or remove modules without powering down the DCS system, ensuring that the normal operation of other modules in the system is not affected during the process. Due to the uncontrollability of human error, there is a certain degree of randomness in the insertion and removal of hot-swapping modules, leading to various combinations of signal contact sequences. Furthermore, in complex application scenarios involving intricate module combinations and chassis structures, unexpected states that deviate from the design may arise, potentially impacting the normal functionality and performance of the system. Based on the electrical characteristics of the hot-swap circuit network in the DCS system, this paper integrates graph theory, path searching, and analysis to determine the various transient and steady-state circuit conditions of hot-swapping under different initial contact states. By examining the combined states of practical engineering applications and conducting path searches for potential pathways in the minimal application units of hotswapping, we identify weaknesses in the design of hot-swap circuits. Additionally, we analyze real-world cases of potential risks and propose improvement recommendations. This work provides a latent pathway analysis method for the subsequent application of hot-swapping in DCS systems, thereby enhancing the safety and operational reliability of safety-grade systems.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability Analysis Based on Vehicle Path Planning Algorithm: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: As a review article, this paper first introduces some path planning algorithms based on two-dimensional raster. Secondly, some path optimization algorithms are introduced in conjunction with practical engineering application scenarios. Finally, trajectory tracking algorithms are introduced, which are applied to various paths, and their reliability is evaluated.

articleTitle: Electronic System Life Prediction Algorithm Based on the Physical of Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Enhancing the availability and safety of electronic systems necessitates a comprehensive investigation into their reliability. This study proposes an electronic system life prediction algorithm based on the physics of failure. For commonly used components, both failure physical models and degradation physical models are presented. An improved binary decision diagram (BDD) is constructed, accompanied by the development of a model-solving algorithm. Ultimately, the proposed methodology is applied to the driver circuit board of an electronic controller as a specific case study, thereby demonstrating its effectiveness and validity.

articleTitle: Varying-Parameter Time-Frequency Manifold Signal Reconstruction for Gearbox Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Noise reduction of vibration signals has always been an important issue in gearbox fault diagnosis. Time-frequency manifold (TFM) is effective in suppressing the noise in the signal time-frequency distribution (TFD). However, the amplitude information of the TFM features is largely deviated from that of the fault component. This paper proposes a new varying-parameter time-frequency manifold signal reconstruction method to restore the amplitude information of the fault component for gearbox fault diagnosis. First, variational mode decomposition (VMD) is employed to extract the fault component in the resonance band. Second, varying-parameter short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is conducted to construct a high-dimensional TFD, followed by down-sampling to reduce the data size. Third, local tangent space alignment (LTSA) is performed to learn the TFM features, and a threshold is set to greatly remove the in-band noise. Fourth, the TFM features are weighted summed to reconstruct the TFD of the fault component, where the weights are obtained based on Euclidean distance. Fifth, with a series of inverse transformations, the time-domain signal of the fault component is reconstructed, which restores the fault amplitude information. Finally, the gearbox fault characteristic frequency can be easily identified in the envelope spectrum of the reconstructed signal. The application in a gearbox fault diagnosis validates the advantages of the proposed method in noise removal, fault impulse enhancement, and amplitude recovery.

articleTitle: Machine Fault Diagnosis Based on Probabilistic Bayesian Active Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the field of machine fault diagnosis, data-driven approaches have been widely applied. However, we often encounter situations where there is a lot of healthy data but a scarcity of fault data. And for some devices, sample labeling is a time-consuming and laborious process. Under these cases, developing fault diagnosis models using data-driven supervised learning approaches becomes exceedingly challenging. Therefore, this paper presents a machine fault diagnosis method based on probabilistic Bayesian active learning. The approach employs probabilistic Bayesian neural network to assess the uncertainty of samples, selects those with the highest uncertainty for labeling, and incorporates them into the training set, thereby realizing an active learning process. This method is expected to reduce the cost of sample labeling by actively selecting samples for labeling.

articleTitle: RUL Prediction of Rolling Bearing via Input Feature Alignment-Combined Different Failure Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Transfer learning methods for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of rolling bearings have been used for the problem of data distribution discrepancy under variable operating condition and have received sustained attention. However, the data distribution discrepancy still exists between different failure behaviors. To solve this problem, a novel RUL prediction method for rolling bearing under different failure behavior via input feature alignment is proposed. First, an alignment strategy between input features of envelope spectrum is proposed, which makes the data distribution smaller by aligning the input features of the test set and the training set. Meanwhile, it is also considered a normalized way that can be used for online prediction rather than using min-max normalization. Then, a RUL prediction method via the feature alignment strategy-combined failure behavior is proposed, which transforms prediction tasks from variable operating condition to different failure behavior to achieve the better RUL prediction results. Finally, Experiments conducted on IEEE PHM2012 run-to-failure bearing datasets validated the superiority of the proposed method according to the comparative results.

articleTitle: Design Method for Truncated Values in Testability Test Plans Based on the Degree of Discreteness
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the current testing experiments of equipment, how to select truncation values has always been a blank in research. If the sample size is small, there will be significant differences in the evaluation results of multiple experiments. If the sample size is large, especially for complex large systems, the implementation cost of the project will be high and the cycle will be long. Therefore, in the design of the testing experiment plan, the differentiation range of evaluation results and the limitation of the testing budget cycle should be considered as important factors in the design of the experimental plan. Therefore, based on the existing design of testing test schemes based on binomial distribution and the analysis of dispersion, this paper conducts research on the truncated values of testing test schemes to solve the problems of large differences in some testing tests and uncontrolled scale and cost of some testing tests, providing a theoretical basis for the in-depth development of model testing tests.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization and Validation of General Algorithm Model for Civil Aircraft Health Management
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This article analyzes and studies the optimization and verification methods of the general algorithm model library for civil aircraft health management, sorts out the overall technical route of optimization verification, and focuses on a detailed analysis of the challenges and corresponding solutions faced by the optimization and verification of the general algorithm model for civil large aircraft health management. This provides reference and inspiration for the optimization and validation of the general algorithm model for health management of large civil aircraft.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Operational Risk Assessment Method Combining System Failure and Human Errors in Civil Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Safety is always the first concern for public when it comes to airplanes. Thanks to the efforts made by all related stakeholders, taking an airplane now is significantly much safer than it was first invented. However, in this ever-changing industry, practitioners are still striving a lot to manage operational risks in order to maintain or enhance the safety level. In this paper, a hybrid operational risk assessment method is introduced that combines information from safety design, operational data used to calculate the dynamic operational failure probability, and non-normal procedures used to perform human error evaluation, which is derived from cognitive reliability and error analysis method (CREAM), to provide an insightful and overall risk picture for safety practitioners within the civil aviation industry.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Liquid-Filled Pipeline Inspection Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the rapid development of manufacturing industry, the prognostics and health management (PHM) of pipeline transportation plays a vital role in different industries and our daily life. Improving the reliability of pipeline transportation through traditional means such as manual checks and long-term fixed-point observation is difficult. In this paper, we provide a robot tailored for internal inspection within liquid-filled pipelines, addressing the current engineering issues concerning the safety of pipeline usage. The robot can be remotely operated through a control cabinet, cable retracting device, and armored optical cable to inspect specific conditions inside liquid-filled pipeline. It is characterized by its ability to minimize personal injury, assess the operational status of the pipeline, and offer a cost-effective solution. This paper focuses on the total schematic design of the robot and the structural and mechanics performance analysis. Then, a prototype robot for liquid-filled pipeline inspection is built up. Ultimately, the performance of the prototype robot is validated through a series of tests, including pipeline passability, pressure resistance, and navigation speed in water. The results indicate that the robot's performance meets the design requirements, which can enhance the accuracy of PHM and reliability of pipeline transportation.

articleTitle: Research on Rotor Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Multi-Sensor Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Given the extremely harsh working environment of aero engines, relying on data from a single sensor is often insufficient due to its susceptibility to its own quality issues and environmental factors, making it challenging to comprehensively monitor the operational status of rotor components. To address this issue, this paper proposes a rotor fault diagnosis method based on a deep residual shrinkage network (DRSN_CS) utilizing multi-sensor data fusion. First, the method treats signals from sensors placed at different locations as multi-channel inputs to the fault diagnosis model. Inspired by RGB image processing techniques, these multi-channel signals are constructed into an n-dimensional channel signal set, effectively addressing the challenge of feature-level multi-channel data fusion. Finally, by employing the deep residual shrinkage network, the method effectively filters out noise from fault signals, thereby enhancing the capability to learn the features of the original vibration signals. Experimental results on a self-developed rotor fault simulation dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior fault diagnosis accuracy, meeting the demands of multi-sensor data fusion for fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Degradation Modeling and Remaining Useful Life Assessment Based on the Hougaard Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To address the uncertainty issues arising from model selection in remaining useful life prediction based on degradation models, this study proposes a remaining useful life prediction method utilizing the Hougaard process. Firstly, we simplify the model using saddlepoint approximation. Next, we derive the remaining useful life expression based on Birnbaum-Saunders (B-S) estimation. Finally, we solve for parameters through maximum likelihood estimation. Case analysis demonstrates that the proposed model can significantly enhance the accuracy of remaining useful life assessment while reducing maintenance costs.

Author Keywords: degradation modeling remaining useful life prediction

articleTitle: A Module Layout Optimization Method of Integrated Rack Based on Simulated Annealing Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Aiming at the difficulties in module layout and liquid cooling flow distribution of integrated rack, an optimization model of module layout scheme is established, which aims to minimize the average temperature rise of all modules. Then, the optimal module layout scheme and the design parameters of the diameter of each flow channel are obtained by the proposed solving method based on Simulated Annealing Algorithm. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method are verified by an actual case of the module layout optimization of a two-story rack in an engineering project.

articleTitle: Assessment of Missile Health Status Based on Test Data Combination Weighting and Cloud Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper normalizes and quantifies missile parameter test data to obtain a health index. The combined weighting is derived from the health index and information entropy. Based on cloud model theory, MATLAB software is used to generate standard cloud charts and evaluation cloud charts, providing a more intuitive conclusion on missile health status assessment. This effective method for assessing missile health status holds practical significance for guiding the equipment support work of military units.

articleTitle: RM-YOLOv8-n: A Lightweight and High-precision Network for Rail Surface Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The surface condition of rail is important for ensuring the safe and stable running of railway vehicles, so real-time defect detection of rail surfaces is essential. However, manual inspection and mainstream non-destructive surface detection methods make meeting the accuracy and efficiency requirements difficult. This paper proposes a rail surface defect detection method: reversible multi-scale you only look once-v8 (RM-YOLOv8-n) on top of improved YOLOv8-n, which can identify rail surface defects more accurately and quickly with fewer parameters. First, the backbone is reconstructed by using the idea of reversible column networks (RevCol) to complete feature extraction more efficiently. Second, the multi-section block with attention and pooling (MSAP) module is designed to improve attention to defects and reduce noise interference in the process of feature fusion. In addition, ghost convolution with shuffle (GSConv) is introduced to reduce the computational complexity in the process of down-sampling and further optimize the information interaction. Experiments on the rail surface defect dataset show that our model achieves the highest mAP@O.5 of 77.4% while reducing computational consumption by 37%

articleTitle: The Influence of Contact Edge Rounding Radius on Fatigue Life of Fir Tree Tenon Joint Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The influence of the radius of contact edge rounding on the stress and strain distribution of a fir tree shaped tenon joint structure for a certain type of air-craft engine turbine blade was studied. The micro motion fatigue life of the tenon joint structure under different radius rounding was estimated using the equivalent stress-strain method and SWT critical plane method. After finite element analysis, the equivalent strain of the tenon joint structure decreased and the average life increased by 34% after adding rounding. The micro fatigue life of the tenon joint structure was longest when the rounding radius of the contact edge was around 0.1mm; The life prediction of SWT critical plane method is shorter than that of equivalent stress-strain method, and the error between the two is smaller when the life is shorter, within the double dispersion zone. This study can provide reference for the design of turbine blade tenon joint structure and other related work in the future.

articleTitle: Analysis of Compressor Sound Propagation Characteristics Driven by Simulation and Actual Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To collect high-quality acoustic signals for compressor, the sound propagation characteristics is analyzed by building simulation model and supplementing actual data. The simulation model is established by calculating the dynamic loads on the blades, the vibrational state of the compressor, and the sound propagation condition outside of the compressor. To address the discrepancy between simulated and actual condition, the actual data is employed to modifying the model based on the auxiliary classifier generative adversarial network (ACGAN), which can address the discrepancy between simulated and actual measured signals. Based on the high-quality generated signal, the sound propagation characteristics is analyzed for compressor, and it is significant for structural health monitoring of compressor. The efficacy of the proposed approach is validated through compressor experiments, which can achieve a high cosine similarity of over 0.6, underscoring the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: A Health State Assessment Method for Complex System Considering the Importance of Multi-Source Information
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Health status evaluation of complex system involves multi-source heterogeneous data (MSHD) from multi-subsystem and multidisciplinary, MSHD fusion with high confidence is a key step of health status assessment. This paper proposes a health status assessment method by combining hierarchical Bayesian network and random forest algorithm considering the importance of MSHD. In the proposed method, the importance of the multi-source heterogeneous data is firstly analyzed based on deep neural network (DNN) and random forest algorithm. Then, a hierarchical Bayesian network based on the hierarchical structure of the system is established. Considering the uncertainties from data monitoring and performance degradation, the health status of each node of hierarchical Bayesian network is evaluated and updated based on Bayesian information updating technology. The validity of the proposed method is illustrated by the health status assessment of industrial robots. This method can improve the assessment accuracy and robustness, which provides a reference for maintenance decision making of complex system.

articleTitle: Study on Intelligent Maintenance System in EV Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper is based on AI, Big Data, Cloud Computation, Digital Twins and Edge computation technology, around the requirements of high safety, high reliability, high efficiency and low power cost, designed the intelligent O&M dual platform architecture, and developed a series of data and service products, and developed the intelligent maintenance application system of the power swapping station including rule model development system, diagnosis and alarming system, equipment health management system, servo driving equipment alarming and diagnosis system, coolant over-limit prediction system, etc. These intelligent O&M products enable the O&M team to realize the real time monitoring, early alarming, diagnostic and health management, which has effectively improved the availability and the first-time through rate of service, reduced the MTTR, and laid a foundation for the automatic operation and unattended service of the power swapping station.

articleTitle: Modelling and Optimization of Warranty Policy for Heterogeneous Second-Hand Products Based on Historical Failure Information
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Considering the heterogeneity in past and existing end users, a novel preventive maintenance model for second-hand products is proposed in this paper. The historical failure information before the acquisition and these between the resale and the inspection time are utilized to derive probabilities that the past end user and the exiting end user belong to “the general sub-population” (the sub-population with smaller failure intensity function). Preventive maintenance or replacement actions are carried out according to the relationships between the aforementioned probabilities and the corresponding thresholds. Taking the profit rate of second-hand products over the warranty period as the objective function, the level of the preventive maintenance and the probability thresholds are optimized jointly. A numerical example is given to illustrate the application of the policy.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method for EMU Traction Motor Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: A fault diagnosis method based on machine learning was proposed in this paper. Based on the high-density on-board data of Electric Multiple Units (EMU), data cleaning and feature processing methods for various parameters such as temperature and current were studied. Additionally, according to the parameter characteristics of different parts, three fault diagnosis methods for the drive-end bearing, non-driven-end bearing and motor body were proposed. Furthermore, a fault diagnosis model for the drive-end bearing was built based on the classification algorithm; A fault diagnosis method for the non-driven-end bearing based on hypothesis testing was established by temperature characteristic statistics; Then, the isolation forest algorithm was used to diagnose the traction motor body fault. Finally, the test results showed that the accuracy and recall rate of the models were acceptable. As a result, the fault diagnosis method proposed in this paper can not only effectively diagnose all kinds of traction motor fault that had been tested, but also locate the fault.

articleTitle: Gas Leakage-Based Fault Prediction for a Boron-Coated Proportional Counter
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Large reaction cross-sections, low operating voltage, extended lifespan, good stability, and suitability for high-temperature and intense gamma radiation settings are among the features of boron-coated proportional counter tubes. Consequently, it has been extensively employed in the nuclear-measuring system outside of the reactor, where the source range detector is a boron-coated proportional counter tube. This paper studies boron-coated proportional counter tubes using a comprehensive approach that combines Monte Carlo simulation with lifespan prediction in health management. The wavelet packet decomposition approach was used to extract feature information from the pulse signals of the boron-coated proportional counter tube. A counter tube defect prediction model was established based on a multi-kernel correlation vector machine, where the impact of different wavelet packets and correlation vector machine kernel functions on the model's prediction performance was examined. The study's findings demonstrated that the particle swarm optimization algorithm-optimized multi-kernel correlation vector machine model exhibited superior prediction accuracy for the counter tubes' future operating conditions. The primary goal is to comprehend how gas loss affects gas pressure and to determine the lifespan of detectors within a detector system.

articleTitle: A Point Cloud Gridding Method for Detecting Rail Intruding Foreign Object
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Intruding foreign objects (IFO) pose a serious threat to railway safety operations. Existing detection algorithms often suffer from significant false alarms and missed detections, rendering them ineffective in practical IFO detection. To address this issue, we propose a point cloud gridding method for detecting rail IFO. Firstly, this method provides effective IFO detection hardware by selecting an appropriate lidar angular resolution based on the requirements for detecting IFO. Secondly, we map pillar point clouds to Bird's Eye View (BEV) to form detection grids, enabling effective IFO detection and improving detection accuracy and recall rates. Extensive experiments and real-world applications have demonstrated the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Research on APU Life Prediction Method Based on Weibull Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper introduces a life prediction method based on Weibull analysis. It establishes a reasonable life prediction method based on the historical data of similar APU components, as well as the design life and reliability of APU components. The influence of reliability, Weibull slope, and component life distribution on the life prediction of APU systems is analyzed. A reasonable component system and unit life prediction model is proposed. Combining with the example of a certain type of APU, this paper analyzes the influence of the life distribution of APU components and different reliability on the life prediction results, as well as the influence of component units and component quantity in the component system on the component system life. For the first time, an APU life prediction method based on Weibull analysis is presented, laying a foundation for APU life prediction.

articleTitle: Simulation of Fault Model of High-Speed Train Air Brake System
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The air brake system is a crucial component that affects the safe and reliable operation of high-speed trains. During prolonged operation, various faults may occur in the air brake system, posing a threat to the safety of train operation. In actual train systems, multiple pressure sensors are usually installed on the air brake system to detect faults. To study the pressure response of various measurement points under different fault conditions, a simulation model of the air brake system for train faults based on Simulink/Simscape has been proposed. First, a fluid dynamics simulation model of the high-speed train's air brake system was established based on its working principles. Then, based on the fault mechanisms, models for valve faults, sensor faults, and pipeline connection faults in the air brake system were analyzed and created, and simulations of different faults were implemented. The simulation results demonstrate the impact of different faults on the pressure response.

articleTitle: Study of Reliability Assessment on Nuclear Safety DCS Module with Small Sample Size
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In order to establish a reliability assessment method on the nuclear safety DCS module with small sample size for assessing on reliability of the nuclear safety DCS module with small sample size, this study transforms operation data of the other similar nuclear safety DCS modules to operation data of the nuclear safety DCS module to be assessed based on the reliability ratio from the process of reliability prediction for solving the problem of small sample size. It's carried out a reliability assessment on the MPU (Main Process Unit) module of the nuclear safety DCS by using the operation data of the MPU module, transformed operation data of the other similar safety DCS modules and the reliability data of these modules from reliability prediction. It turns out the result of this assessment has good agreement with the reliability prediction. Thus, the reliability assessment method used in this study can be used in reliability assessment on the nuclear safety DCS module with small sample size.

articleTitle: Multi-Attribute Maintenance Decision Making for Aircraft Engines Based on Entropy Weight TOPSIS Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Reasonable maintenance timing plays an important role in determining the efficiency and economic benefits of aircraft-engine utilization. To address the problem of multiple conflicting attributes in maintenance decision-making, this paper constructs a multi-attribute maintenance decision-making model that integrates availability, maintenance cost, and reliability indexes. The entropy weighting method is adopted to calculate the weights of each attribute, and these indexes are combined with the TOPSIS method for a comprehensive evaluation. The optimal maintenance timing of the aircraft-engine is evaluated and selected using the TOPSIS method. Finally, the C-MAPSS dataset is utilized to analyze an example, comparing the single-attribute decision-making model with the proposed multi-attribute decision-making method. This comparison verifies the advantages of the proposed method in terms of rationality and practicality. The results show that the method can effectively balance various maintenance decision attributes and provide a more comprehensive and accurate maintenance decision reference.

articleTitle: In-Situ Fault Sensing Methods for Degradation Mechanism of SiC Power MOSFETs in Power Supplies Under Power Cycling Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper investigates a fault sensing method for SiC power MOSFETs in power supply based on voltage transient. The impact of SiC power MOSFETs degradation on voltage transient have been theoretically analyzed. The effect of the degradation is represented by the voltage changing rate measured by a RF voltage probe with a noninvasive manner. The degraded devices were obtained through the power-cycling test, and a BOOST circuit is used to simulate the real working environment and conditions. We extracted voltage changing rate of SiC power MOSFETs when SiC power MOSFETs were working, and compared the changes in voltage changing rate before and after degradation. The feasibility of the fault sensing method was verified by experimental results. The results may aid in the degradation monitoring of SiC power MOSFETs in power supply, thereby improving the safety of power supply operations.

articleTitle: The Research and Design of Self-Diagnostic Function for NPP I&C System
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Self-diagnosis is one of the most efficacious approaches to enhancing and ensuring the reliability of NPP I&C (Nuclear Power Plant Instrumentation & Control) systems. According to the requirements of IEC 61508 on self-diagnosis, a self-diagnosis design scheme for NPP I&C system is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the overall fault analysis of the NPP I&C system is carried out to identify the potential faults and derive the fault types to be diagnosed. Secondly, in the level of fault diagnosis design, the static and dynamic combination diagnosis design mechanism, the specific diagnosis design for different fault types is implemented, including the CPU core diagnosis design of LoongArch (loong architecture), and the diagnosis framework design suitable for multi-service scenarios are proposed. Finally, at the level of fault handling and warning, the design mechanism of the equipment's fault handling state transition, the system's data-oriented safety output, the fault bit information arrangement, and the local and network warning are proposed. This paper provides a systematic and detailed design scheme for the self-diagnosis of NPP I&C system, which can effectively improve the reliability of the system itself.

articleTitle: A Frequency Fault Injection Technology for Sine Signals Based on Spectrum Separation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the testability test of avionics system and equipment, fault injection work needs to be carried out for sine signal frequency parameters.At present, there is no effective means. This paper analyze the spectrum structure of sinusoidal signal, and design a frequency fault injector based on the method of spectrum separation. Without changing the amplitude and mean value, the on-line control of sinusoidal signal frequency fault is realized. The online fault injection test results show that the method is stable, and the control error of amplitude mean and frequency satisfies normal distribution at 0.05 significance level, which can meet the actual engineering requirements.

articleTitle: Impact Damage Monitoring of Composite Materials Using Optical Fiber Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Composite materials are widely used in aircraft manufacturing, and ensuring the safety and reliability of these materials is very important for flight safety. The barely visible impact damage (BVID) sustained by composite structures will pose significant safety hazards if not promptly detected. In this paper, a new method for damage detection of carbon fiber reinforced polymers (CFRP) during the impact process is proposed based on the interlayer strain changes and damage by using a stereo optic fiber sensor network embedded between composite interlayers. In this method, the strain field distribution change under the impact load is analyzed and the damage state could be judged by measuring the damage change according to the strain change.

articleTitle: Real-Time Residual Life Prediction Based on Adaptive Wiener Process with UKF
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Life span prediction is of significant importance for enhancing the reliability and safety during the use of equipment. In this study, we introduce an innovative degradation model, grounded in the Wiener process, for accurately estimating the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of systems, offering enhanced predictive capabilities compared to existing approaches. Initially, the variability of degradation drift is considered to construct a state-space model for online updating of the equipment's remaining life. Subsequently, an analytical expression for the remaining life in terms of the first passage time is derived, and the Expectation-Maximization (EM) method is applied for estimating the model parameters. Finally, an example of fatigue crack growth demonstrates that the constructed model has a good accuracy in estimating the RUL.

articleTitle: Reliability Study of Through Ceramic Via Substrate Under Temperature Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the development of electronic technology, through ceramic via (TCV) has gradually become key technology in the manufacture of electronic products. In this experiment, different TCV-Cu samples were prepared using different current densities. The samples were heated to 350 °C and the helium leakage rate of the samples were compared before and after heating. In order to investigate the reason for the change of the helium leakage rate, the microstructure of the Cu/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> interface was observed by SEM. Finally, the mechanical simulation of TCV was carried out to verify the relationship between stress and interface crake. It was found that cracks appeared at the Cu/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> interface after heating, leading to the helium leakage rate decrease of the sample. Cracks were produced by stress mismatch between Cu and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ceramic. Mechanical analysis of the samples structure revealed that the stress at the interface can be reduced by increase the radius and thickness of the electroplated Cu soldering pad.

articleTitle: A Mission Reliability Optimization Model for Safety-Critical Equipment Considering Both Internal Degradation and External Shocks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Safety-critical equipment such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), submarines, fleets, and military aircraft must perform a variety of missions where mission reliability and equipment survivability are paramount. To enhance survivability, mission can be aborted upon encountering certain failure conditions. In this study, a novel mission abort policy is devised that allows for risk control of both internal degradation and external shocks. The cumulative impact of shocks on system degradation is quantified via a generic stochastic model. Inspections are executed equidistantly to reveal the underlying degradation damage, following which adaptive abort decisions are made using a control limit policy. By jointly optimizing the inspection interval and abort threshold, the long-term operational cost of the system is minimized. Numerical experiments exemplify the model effectiveness in mission risk control and loss mitigation.

articleTitle: Information Extraction from Aircraft Maintenance Records Using Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper analyzes the characteristics of aircraft maintenance records and develops an information extraction Agent using general large language models (LLMs). The Agent demonstrates effective extraction performance across maintenance records from different aircraft models and airlines, supporting various LLMs of different scales and capabilities. Utilizing this Agent, we extracted key information from 17,544 maintenance records of COMAC ARJ21, forming a dataset used for relationship finding and completion tasks in the ARJ21 maintenance knowledge graph. Despite its effectiveness, challenges remain in extracting key information from complex troubleshooting measures involving multi-step isolation procedures and dealing with non-standard abbreviations and multiple names for the same component. Future work will focus on refining the Agent, further subdividing processing steps to handle more complex maintenance records, and providing editable prompt templates and a visualization interface.

articleTitle: A New Model for Calculating the Time-varying Meshing Stiffness of Cracked Gears Considering Deformation Compatibility
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The development of a novel model integrating coupling flexibility, extension of contact, and deformation compatibility for analyzing cracked gears addresses existing limitations in current models. By considering these crucial factors, the proposed model enhances the convenience, precision, and efficiency of time-varying mesh stiffness (TVMS) analysis in gear dynamics. The results from this new model are compared and validated against simulation outcomes, demonstrating a strong alignment with finite element (FE) models. This alignment signifies the model's accuracy and reliability, providing a robust basis for future research in gear dynamics analysis and offering insights into the behavior of gears with cracks, ultimately contributing to advancements in dynamic stability and fault diagnosis of gear systems.

articleTitle: Construction of Avionics Display Equipment Fault Knowledge Graph Based on BiLSTM-CRF
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the development of avionics technology, fault diagnosis of avionics display equipment plays an increasingly important role in health management. However, due to the complexity of the software of civil aircraft display systems, their failure modes have become more and more complicated. Traditional fault diagnosis methods rely on logical reasoning and fault tree analysis after the occurrence of faults, which are inefficient and difficult to accurately locate the cause of faults when dealing with complex systems, and do not take into account the fact that there is a lot of valid information hidden in the large amount of testing and logging information generated during the development and testing process of civil aircraft display software. This study proposes a knowledge graph construction method for avionics display equipment health management based on BiLSTM-CRF, aiming to visualise health management related fault information. By using BiLSTM-CRF model for text extraction of fault information, constructing knowledge triples by means of knowledge matching and rules, and visualising health management related fault information in Neo4j, it provides an effective tool for health management of avionics equipment.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Diagnosis Method Using Multiscale Features for Compound Fault Diagnosis in Air Brake Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Neural network-based methods are effective for single fault diagnosis, but compound faults present challenges due to fault characteristics spanning multiple scales. Single-scale feature extraction leads to misdiagnosis from overlapping signals, and many methods treat compound faults as single faults, making accurate diagnosis difficult. This paper presents a multiscale convolutional neural network (MSCNN) for compound fault diagnosis. Raw signals are processed through the Res2Net block (RB) to reduce feature overlap. To minimize feature map redundancy, the attention block (AB) is used, featuring an one-dimensional simple and parameter-free attention module (1D-SimAM). Finally, a multilabel classifier categorizes the faults. Experimental validation on a high-speed train braking system simulation shows the proposed method outperforms four existing methods”,demonstrating superior performance.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of the Unbalance Impact on a Rotor Supported by Incorporating Elastic Support
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In rotor systems, vibration is unavoidable. Significant vibration not only generates noise and diminishes machine performance, but also compromises the service life and reliability of the equipment, potentially leading to safety hazards. The causes of rotor vibration are diverse and complex. One of the primary reasons for rotor system vibration is unbalance. However, there is limited experimental research on the coupled effects of unbalance and inlet pressure of squeeze film damper (SFD) on the dynamic characteristics of rotor system. This paper investigates the impact of unbalance and inlet pressure on the dynamic characteristics of a rotor-SFD system, as well as their combined effects, through modal and transient dynamic experiments. The results indicate that as the unbalance magnitude increases, the critical speed of the rotor system significantly shifts higher. The speed through the critical speed slows down. The amplitude of acceleration vibration significantly rises, exacerbating system instability. When the unbalance is relatively small at low speeds, reducing the inlet pressure of the SFD within a certain range can decrease the vibration amplitude of the system and enhance its stability. However, in the circumstances of significant imbalance and high speeds, the suppressive impact of inlet pressure on rotor system vibrations is significantly weakened.

articleTitle: Importance Analysis of Xi'an Metro Stations Based on K-shell Decomposition and Passenger Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Urban rail transit plays an important role in urban systems. Key stations in rail transit always transfer many passengers in a short time, which depends on the transition ability of the urban rail transit network. So it is essential to identify key stations for enhancing the transit system reliability. However, network topology is used in the reported research work to identify the key nodes in transit networks without consideration of attributes for stations. This paper integrates the structure features based on complex network theory and attributes features based on passenger flow to identify the key stations. The K-Shell-Passenger flow (KSP) method is developed by combining the K-shell decomposition algorithm with passenger flow information. Taking Xi'an metro as an example, Degree Centrality (DC), classical K-shell decomposition method (KS), and Degree centrality & K-shell decomposition method (DC+KS) are introduced to analyze the importance rankings of stations for verifying the effectiveness of the proposed method. The mean Average Precision (mAP) is used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method quantitatively. The mAP of KSP is 99.67%, which is 7.4% higher than that of DC+KS method. Therefore, KSP is effective to analyze the key stations of the transit network, which can provide a targeted preventive maintenance strategy for stations based on the importance measures for improving operational efficiency.

Index Terms: Importance Of Nodes In The Network

articleTitle: Bearing Degradation State Estimation Based on EEMD Improved Alignment Entropy and Correlation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of non-stationarity, nonlinearity, non-Gaussian and other characteristics of the vibration signal of rolling bearings and the low sensitivity of the arrangement entropy to extract the performance degradation characteristics of rolling bearings, a bearing degradation state estimation based on EEMD improved permutation entropy (IPE) and correlation analysis was proposed. Firstly, adaptive noise complete set of empirical mode decomposition algorithm vibration signals were decomposed eigen mode function, choice the IMF component and component of the original signal correlation signal reconstruction. Then, the degradation characteristics are extracted by the improved arrangement entropy, and the relationship between the extracted degradation characteristics and reliability of the extracted rolling bearings is evaluated by correlation analysis, so as to achieve the purpose of evaluating the degradation characteristics of bearings from the evolution law of bearing reliability. In this paper, the whole life data of bearings from Xi 'an Jiaotong University is used to verify the method. Compared with the method of permutation entropy, permutation entropy, etc., this method can estimate the degradation state of bearing effectively.

articleTitle: Coupling Sensitivity Analysis and Life Prediction of Multi-Degradation Variable Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Based on the Copula function model, this paper proposes a method for predicting the equipment life under the coupling conditions of multiple degradation models. It considers the uncertainties of multiple degradation variables and degradation description models, extending the univariate and deterministic description models to the conditions of multivariate coupling and uncertain degradation description models. The degradation description model and Copula function are selected through degradation data hypothesis testing and Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), respectively. Sensitivity analysis is conducted on the impact of different degradation models on the multivariate j oint distribution under the same expectation conditions. The proposed life prediction method under multivariate coupling conditions is validated using a binary degradation variable simulation case.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of an Aerodynamically Integrated Cabin Pressure Regulation System Simulation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The cabin pressure regulator is a crucial component for ensuring the normal operation of an aircraft, as it maintains the internal cabin pressure at a safe and comfortable level during flight. By controlling the airflow into and out of the cabin, the regulator adjusts the internal pressure to accommodate changes in high-altitude environments. This paper focuses on the modeling of the cabin pressure regulator, employing an AMESim model to simplify the complexity of the real-world system. By fine-tuning parameters, the simulation model becomes more aligned with actual conditions, aiding practitioners in the subsequent maintenance or further development of the pressure regulator.

articleTitle: A Reliability Modeling Method for Directed Acyclic Graph Network System Including Backup Bypass
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: A mission reliability modeling method is proposed for directed acyclic graph network system including backup bypass. By decomposing it into sub directed acyclic graphs along all connected and disconnected path direction until it is decomposed into device units, and mixing the sub directed acyclic graphs adjacent to each node in series, parallel, and bypass models, a mission reliability block diagram model of the network system is constructed in which the sub networks and devices are mixed layer by layer, and the discrete event simulation method is used for calculation, which can effectively solve the mission reliability modeling and calculation problem of such network system in engineering.

articleTitle: Blade Icing Fault Identification Based on Domain-Adaptive Spatiotemporal Attention Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: As one of the key components of wind turbines, the health of wind turbine blades directly affects the utilization rate of wind energy. Blade icing fault identification based on SCADA data is low-cost and effective. However, SCADA data has strong spatiotemporal correlation, and there are strong distribution differences in the spatiotemporal characteristics of different wind turbines, which makes the identification of cross-turbine blade icing faults extremely poor. And the actual state labels are precious and difficult to obtain. To address the above problems, this paper proposes a domain-adaptive spatiotemporal attention model for cross-turbine blade icing fault identification. By introducing a feature extraction network based on spatiotemporal attention and using the maximum mean difference algorithm to quantify and minimize the feature differences between source domain data and target domain data. It reduces the dependence on a large amount of labeled data and improves the generalization ability of the model. Experimental results show that this method significantly improves the identification rate of cross-turbine blade icing faults, verifying the effectiveness and practicality of this method.

articleTitle: Research on the Semi Physical Simulation Test of Fault Injection and Validation for Traction Motor in Railway Transit
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To verify the prognostics health management (PHM) technology of traction motor, the construction of a traction system fault injection and validation platform is essential. The semi physical simulation platform combines the advantages of both physical and virtual simulation platforms, overcoming their respective shortcomings, and has become an incubator and accelerator for promoting the practical application of the PHM technology. On this basis, the paper proposes a semi physical simulation test method of fault injection and validation for traction motor, focusing on the mathematical modeling of the motor on health and fault condition, and the construction of the semi physical simulation test platforms. Firstly, motor models on health and fault condition are analyzed, where two faults of stator interturn short fault and rotor broken bar fault are involved; then it defines the input and output ports to realize the segmentation and connection of the physical and simulation, in which the motor power system is downloaded and runs in the simulator whereas motor control algorithm performs in the physical circuit board; finally, the results of the physical and semi physical simulation test for both health and fault are compared, and the sample data under the stator and rotor fault in the semi physical simulation test is further analyzed to detect the fault.

articleTitle: Improved Gerstner Function Wave Model Based on Elfouhaily Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Aiming at the limitations of a single wave simulation approach across various marine environments, and with the aim of enhancing the reliability and realism of wave 3D modelling in different scenarios, this paper proposes a wave formation approach ground on the combination of the Gerstner function and the Elfouhaily wave spectra, which achieves the modelling of waves with different wave strengths, and feasible application of the model to further the reliability and safety of sea surface modelling is also outlined. Firstly, the improved Gerstner's functional equation system is selected as the wave construction model, and it is extended into a three-dimensional form to simulate the details and realism of the waves; secondly, in order to control the wave model and achieve the stochasticity and realism of the waves, the Elfouhaily wave spectra are used to gain the parameters for the control of the wave model, and then to establish the reliable wave simulation model; Finally, wave simulations and model comparisons are carried out with respect to the spectral parameters of multiple wave spectra, and issues related to the safety of ocean engineering applications and offshore activities based on the model are briefly presented. The experimental results show that the proposed method is reliable and practical, with high realism, and is applicable to a variety of wave scenarios, which is of great significance in improving the prognosis and safety assessment of the marine environment.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of FMEA in Civil Aircraft Safety Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) is an analytical work carried out in civil aircraft airworthiness qualification activities. Aiming at the civil aircraft development procedure and stage division, the FMEA work planning of civil aircraft development stage is clarified. Taking an engine drive pump as the research object, based on the FMEA method, the reliability block diagram of the equipment is established, and structural analysis, functional analysis, fault identification and risk analysis are carried out. FMEA is integrated in the design iteration process to provide a basis for the safety design of civil aircraft system.

articleTitle: Study on Environmental Stress Screening of Nuclear Power Plant Safety DCS Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Environmental stress screening (ESS) of electronic components is a critical safeguard for ensuring reliability in electronic products before installation, which can be regarded as an extension of electronic product quality testing and failure prevention. This study focuses on the ESS challenges faced by nuclear power plant safety digital control system (DCS). On the basis of the actual working environment of nuclear power plant safety DCS modules and a comparison of existing standards and norms in the industry, this paper proposes some ESS schemes for nuclear power plant safety DCS. To provide a reference basis for selecting an appropriate ESS protocol for safety DCS modules in nuclear power plant, a comprehensive analysis of multiple schemes is conducted, considering factors such as screening strength, temperature holding time, and others, in the meantime, ensuring that new faults are not introduced.

articleTitle: Effects of Manufacturing and Installation Factors on the Initiation and Propagation Characteristics of Bending Fatigue Crack in Spur Gear
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Root bending fatigue is the main cause of root crack formation, and the crack initiation and propagation process is also influenced by factors such as tooth surface morphology, manufacturing, and assembly. In order to address the short-comings of existing research on crack initiation and propagation in root bending fatigue, this study establishes a finite element model for crack propagation in root bending fatigue guided by experimental results based on linear elastic fracture mechanics principles. The effects of surface roughness and center distance variation on the crack propagation process are considered and validated. The research shows that the crack initiation location and initial propagation direction are not affected by changes in the load magnitude. Surface roughness and center distance factors have a significant influence on the stress intensity factor during the crack propagation process, thereby affecting the crack propagation rate and trajectory.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method for Small Sample and Multi-Condition Based on Denoising Autoencoder and Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To address the problem of fault diagnosis under multiple working conditions, a fault diagnosis method based on denoising autoencoder and convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed. First, the multi-channel one-dimensional sensor data is processed into two-dimensional square matrix data, and the denoising autoencoder is trained using this data. The encoder part of the trained denoising autoencoder is used as a feature extractor to extract features from the two-dimensional square matrix data, which are then fed into the CNN for classification. Experimental results show that this method can achieve a diagnosis accuracy rate of 99.67% on the motor fault dataset from the subway train transmission systems simulation experiment. The effectiveness of incorporating the denoising autoencoder in the method is demonstrated through comparative analysis of the experimental results, as well as highlighting key considerations for data preprocessing.

articleTitle: Multi-Hierarchical Dispersion Entropy: A Novel Nonlinear Measurement Approach for Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearing
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Hierarchical dispersion entropy (HDisE)is an effective way to measure the dynamics of nonlinear signals. However, HDisE only extracts features at a single level, resulting in the loss of a large amount of deep information. In addition, HDisE is very sensitive to the length of time series. As the number of decomposition layers increases, the length of the original sequence decreases dramatically, which may lead to instability and inaccuracy of entropy estimation when dealing with short-term sequences. To solve these limitations, this paper proposes a new time series complexity measurement method, multi-hierarchical dispersion entropy (MHDisE), for feature extraction of signals. MHDisE not only enriches the hierarchical nature of information by integrating the high-frequency and low-frequency features of multiple decomposition levels, but also improves the stability and accuracy of short-time series entropy estimation. Based on the advantages of MHDisE, a fault diagnosis method for rolling bearing combining MHDisE and Support Vector Machin optimized by Spider Wasp Optimizer (SWO-SVM) was proposed. Finally, the CRWU public dataset and experimental data of rolling bearing are used for verification. The results show that the proposed method can effectively extract feature information, improve the fault identification accuracy and stability, and show significant advantages in processing short-term sequences.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearings Based on Attention Mechanism and Joint Correlation Alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Due to the data distributions in the source domain (SD) and the target domain (TD) are significantly different, many techniques have been developed to adapt to different domains. However, in the existing domain adaptation (DA) methods, the influence of domain samples on network weight has not been considered. Moreover, most of these methods only focused on marginal distribution alignment (MDA), while the class conditional distribution alignment (CDA) has been ignored. In view of the above shortcomings, an adaptive network based on attention mechanism and joint correlation alignment (AM-JCA) is proposed in this paper. The attention mechanism is utilized to extract crucial fault feature information. The joint correlation alignment method is used to effectively reduce the difference of marginal distribution between two domains, and further minimize the difference of conditional distribution between different categories. In addition, in order to learn more separable fault features, a new N-Softmax loss is proposed, which has a stronger classification ability than the traditional softmax. Finally, experimental results show that the proposed method has significant effects and superiority.

articleTitle: Vibration Analysis and Fault Diagnosis of Dynamical System Under Strong Noise Background Based on Transformer-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Dynamical system such as wind turbine gearboxes are subjected to heavy-load, and low-speed operational conditions, frequently generating vibrations with abnormal noise. To effectively diagnose gearbox faults under such conditions of strong noise, this paper proposes a novel fault diagnosis method integrating Transformer and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. First, a Transformer encoder is utilized for the initial extraction of global-level features from raw data with strong noise. The output sequences from the Transformer are subsequently input into the CNN to further extract local features. Then the fault category probabilities are outputted based on the extracted features. Finally, the model was trained, validated, and tested on this dateset comprising 4800 samples from wind turbine gearboxes, categorized into four classes: healthy, bearing fault, high-speed stage fault, and low-speed stage fault. The results demonstrate an overall accuracy of 99.9%, significantly outperforming standalone CNN, Transformer, and ResNet models.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetic Bistable Energy Harvester for Wireless Health Monitoring Nodes on Freight Train Bogies
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Monitoring the operational status of freight train bogies with sensors, such as accelerometers and temperature sensors, provides crucial data for accurate fault prognostics and health management of axle bearings and bogie frameworks. However, monitoring sensors on freight train bogies cannot be powered by centralized sources, and the use of chemical batteries has limitations. These energy supply issues hinder the development of PHM systems for heavy-duty freight vehicles. This paper designs an electromagnetic energy harvester based on ring-moving magnets, which converts mechanical energy from the freight train bogies into electrical power for powering sensors. Initially, the vibration characteristics of the bogie are analyzed using a 80 open wagon model to determine the design requirements. Bistability is achieved through magnetic forces, spring elasticity, and the gravitational force on the moving ring magnet, with an analysis of how changes in the inner diameter of the fixed ring magnet affect the bistable potential well to derive the optimal dimensions of key components. The prototype was tested under conditions similar to those of freight train operations. The results show that the energy harvester has a frequency bandwidth of 5-35Hz and generates an average power of 19.56mW at 20Hz and 2.5g. This harvester can provide stable power to sensors on freight trains and is suitable for the actual operating conditions of freight vehicles.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Fourier Convolution Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Rolling bearings are critical yet vulnerable components in rotary machinery. Its malfunction hinders industrial production and equipment operation. Despite the significant success of Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Deep Learning (DL) in bearing fault diagnosis, the issue of poor model interpretability remains. Recent Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) springs up, which enhances the interpretability of DL models. This paper explores the application of KAN in bearing fault diagnosis and proposes an improved method for one-dimensional convolutional Fourier KAN layer. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved one-dimensional convolutional Fourier KAN model performs well in fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: AC Motor Fault Diagnosis Based on Multi-Source Signal Fusion SDP
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of the limited ability of a single signal to characterize the fault state of AC motors, this paper proposes an AC motor fault diagnosis method based on multi-source signal fusion SDP (Symmetric Dot Pattern). Firstly, the current and vibration signals acquired from the AC motor and converted to image by SDP image conversion method. Then, an adaptive parameter selection method is employed to adaptive acquire the optimal parameters to amplify the image differences between different fault states. Finally, the fault diagnosis model is built by AlexNet for diagnosing AC motor faults. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, it was tested on an AC motor fault experimental platform. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method diagnostic accuracy is 99.16%. By comparing with a single-signal source, the proposed method has the highest accuracy, further validating the advancement of the proposed method. This study provides an efficient and feasible diagnostic method for AC motor fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Pressure Distribution Analysis of Metro Braking System with Different Working Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To study the braking performance status of an in-service metro train braking system, a method that identifies specific working conditions based on data-driven techniques and studies the distribution range of brake cylinder pressure under different conditions is proposed in this paper. By employing the Pearson correlation analysis method, a substantial amount of historical on-board data from a metro line is analyzed, leading to the identification of two data points closely related to brake cylinder pressure. To address the limitations of correlation analysis, the principle of the blending brake of EP brake(electro-dynamic brake) and ED brake(electro-pneumatic brake) was combined with the actual brake cylinder pressure curve to determine four key characteristics for classifying different braking conditions and summarize three typical braking processes. Based on the sliding window algorithm and logical judgment, the distribution of brake cylinder pressure under these three specific conditions are investigated in this study, which is crucial for evaluating the performance of the braking system in actual operation. The method proposed in this paper is also applicable to the analysis of other rail transit trains' braking systems.

articleTitle: Vibration Analysis of Notched Damaged Aero-engine Compressor Blades
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Compressor blades are important components in aero-engines and are prone to foreign object damage (FOD). FOD-damaged compressor blades are susceptible to fracture under vibration loads, severely risking the aircraft safety. Hence, this paper aims to investigate vibration characteristics of FOD-damaged compressor blades through experimental and finite element (FE) analysis. To accomplish this, vibration test is conducted by applying a 3D full-field scanning laser vibrometry method and the experimental results are compared with numerical results. A good consistency is observed between the experimental results and numerical predictions. Moreover, damaged compressor blade models with FOD of different depths are established based on the validated model, and are successfully utilized for studying the static and dynamic modal analysis of damaged blades. The results demonstrate that the increase in the depth of notch damage leads to the reduction of natural frequency of blade, threatening the safety of aero-engines.

articleTitle: An Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Method for Subway Train Transmission System Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the modern rail train system, the safety of fault diagnosis technology is very important. At present, the mainstream algorithms based on data-driven have achieved excellent results in fault diagnosis. However, the current research often focuses on a device data set itself, and its training set and test set are often in the same distribution. Due to the diversity of equipment and working conditions, it is difficult to apply it to industrial practice. To solve this problem, we propose an unsupervised domain adaptation method for subway train transmission system fault diagnosis that integrates convolutional neural networks(CNN) and domain adaptation transfer. Firstly, we extract features based on the data set of subway train transmission system with multiple working conditions and divide the training set, validation set and test set. Secondly, we use the training set to train the CNN to obtain the model weight file. After that, we train the domain adaptation model based on the weight file and the labeled training set and the unlabeled test set. Finally, we tested the accuracy of the model on the test set. Experiments show that compared with CNN without domain adaptation training, the fault diagnosis accuracy of the domain adaptation model is improved by about 27.24%, which verifies the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Fault Diagnosis Method of Planetary Gearbox Based on ITD and CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis of planetary gearboxes (PGs) is crucial for preventing equipment failures and extending their lifespan. To enhance the efficiency and accuracy of PG fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a novel method integrating intrinsic time scale decomposition (ITD) with convolutional neural network (CNN). The proposed method leverages the demodulation capability of ITD to decompose and reconstruct the original signal, effectively removing irrelevant noise and isolating core fault features, and the learning ability of CNN to accurately identify the fault features. Compared to methods relying on CNN only, the proposed method not only improves the computational efficiency but also achieves higher fault diagnosis accuracy.

articleTitle: Wear State Classification of Bearing Based on Deep Belief Network Using Combined Online Oil and Vibration Monitoring Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the purpose of improving the wear state classification accuracy of bearing based on combined online oil and vibration monitoring data, this paper proposes a new method to classify the wear state of bearing based on the K-means clustering and deep belief network (DBN). First, we carried out several groups of full life test for bearings on a bearing life test bench to obtain the online oil parameters such as wear metal debris, oil viscosity, temperature, density, and permittivity and vibration data during the whole test. The data are pretreated and normalized to form the wear state classification input data. Then, K-means method is used to cluster the input data to obtain the training label with validation for further wear state classification. A five-layer DBN feature extraction model is constructed and trained using the labeled input data. The model is used to extract features from combined online oil and vibration monitoring data and to classify the wear status of other tested bearings. Finally, the experimental results indicate that the DBN model can effectively classify the wear state of bearings. Compared with the support vector machine (SVM) method previously used, the accuracy of classification has slightly improved.

articleTitle: Research on the Prediction Technique for Battery Performance Degradation Trends Based on Hierarchical Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries have a wide range of applications as a new energy source, and it is of great significance to realize the prediction of the performance degradation trends of lithium-ion batteries. At present, data-driven prediction technology for performance degradation trends has become an effective method for the prediction of lithium batteries. However, in the actual prediction process, lithium batteries have less data available for training, resulting in poor training accuracy. In this paper, we propose a prediction algorithm for battery performance degradation trends based on hierarchical federated learning to improve the accuracy of lithium battery prediction.
