First, we propose a federal grouping technique based on improved K-medoids clustering to group multi-formulation batteries. Then, we perform hierarchical federated learning based on the grouping results. Com pared with traditional client-server federation learning, hierarchical federation learning reduces the server communication burden and improves the model convergence speed. In addition, we use a multiscale time convolutional network prediction method to predict a single cell. The method involves predicting trends at both large and small scales, followed by a refinement process to enhance the accuracy of the predictions. The method proposed in this paper has good performance on the dataset.

articleTitle: Application of Sneak Circuit Analysis in the Safety Classification DCS Burst Valve Control Module of ACP100
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the development of nuclear power control technology and the improvement of requirements for nuclear power plants, burst valves have been introduced into the nuclear safety classification distributed control systems (DCS). In previous studies on the application of burst valves in nuclear power plants, only the sneak path of burst valve controllers (control modules) were analyzed and researched, while the sneak timing was ignored. There are clear timing requirements during the driving process of burst valves. Therefore, the existence of sneak timing in the control module may lead to abnormal burst valve control, causing the burst valve to fail to detonate successfully when needed or misfire when not needed. Aiming at the lack of sneak timing analysis during the development of burst valve control modules, this article introduces Markov chain for sneak timing analysis in the sneak circuit analysis process of ACP100 safety classification DCS burst valve control modules. The analysis results show that Markov chain can effectively detect the sneak timing existing in burst valve control modules.

articleTitle: A Wind Gearbox Fault Detection Method Based on a Lightweight Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: It is of great importance to realize effective fault diagnosis of wind turbines gearbox in modern industrial systems. This paper proposes a fault diagnosis method that based on a lightweight attention network. This method uses a lightweight convolutional neural network MobileNetV3_L based on the Transformer to improve the new network RepViT network for wind gearbox fault diagnosis. The diagnosis process includes short-time Fourier transform processing of the laboratory artificial wind gearbox fault data set, and establishing a fault classification and recognition model based on a lightweight convolutional neural network. Finally, the model is used to perform fault diagnosis on a real wind gearbox dataset to verify its performance. Experimental research is conducted on the University of Macau gearbox dataset to validate the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the method exhibits superior stability and accuracy than other methods.

articleTitle: Intelligent Health Monitoring of Machinery Using Multi-Channel Time Series Compressed Data and Deep Reconstruction Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Nowadays, the safety and reliability of operating equipment are critical in various sectors such as wind energy, manufacturing, transport, and the chemical industry. Intelligent condition monitoring (CM) tracks the operating status of machinery, ensuring effectiveness, maintaining production quality, reducing unplanned breakdowns, and minimizing economic losses due to equipment failures. Rolling element bearings, widely used in almost all rotating machinery, contribute significantly to many machinery failures. However, the operation of rotating machinery spans from months to years, generating vast amounts of data from installation to failure. Moreover, it is common to collect multi-channel data such as vibration, acoustic, and temperature, etc., presenting a challenge in selecting the appropriate data source for optimal tracking degradation. This paper developed an intelligent approach, utilizing a novel deep learning model, named CLSTM, multi-channel and compressed data, for tracking the degradation process of bearing. CLSTM first extracts hidden features from the convolution neural network (CNN) and then uses long short term memory (LSTM) network to learn dependencies between samples. Experimental validation demonstrates that the developed method is effective and outperforms other statistics indicators and single-channel strategy.

articleTitle: Domain Generalization Using Pseudo Triplet Network Learning for Vibration Signal-Based Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Domain generalization (DG) based intelligent fault diagnosis has developed rapidly in recent years owing to the need for applying trained neural networks to unseen domains. However, models trained using DG often suffer from performance degradation when in presence of nonstationary working conditions. To address this challenge, this work proposes a DG based intelligent fault diagnosis approach based on a vibration response mechanism guided pseudo triplet network, which extracts suitable features that correlate well with the health conditions. Firstly, the proposed approach estimates the cyclic spectral correlation maps of vibration signals to provide vibration response mechanism of different health conditions. Then, a pseudo triplet neural network is designed to calculate the distance between the representations of the prior input, the negative input from the representation of the main input. The prior input is the specific part of the cyclic spectral correlation map with the selected carrier band and it guides the network focus on the fault-related features. Finally, the proposed approach is evaluated through experiments conducted on data collected from nonstationary working conditions.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Based on Vibration and Torque Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In recent years, intelligent fault diagnosis technology has become a research hotspot in the field of fault diagnosis by virtue of its powerful performance and broad prospects. However, most of the current research is based on the fault diagnosis of a single vibration signal, and the model trained by single-modal data often has the problems of poor fault tolerance rate, susceptibility to noise and poor generalization. Therefore, in order to explore the connection between different signal fault features and extract and integrate complementary fault features, this paper proposes a new method to fuse vibration and torque signals, called VTCNN-LSTM, which is experimentally verified on the bearing dataset Paderborn of the University of Paderborn in Germany. The results show that VTCNN-LSTM has nearly 100% diagnostic accuracy in a noise-free environment. It also has good performance in high noise environment, which shows the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Parallel Relation Network for Intelligent Fault Detection and Localization of Train Transmission Systems with Zero-fault Sample
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning methods have empowered the fault detection of train transmission systems (TTS). However, the existing methods require a large number of fault samples, which are often difficult to obtain in TTS. In order to address the challenge, we propose a parallel relation network (PRN) for fault detection of TTS. The PRN method uses residual shrinkage network to extract the effective features from input samples and then form feature pairs to describe the relationship between the samples. Finally, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KAN) is used to assess the health states of the samples. In addition, we generate different auxiliary sample libraries to enhance the model's ability to extract features inherent to the health state. In experiments, we verified the feasibility of the PRN method, which achieved more than 98% accuracy and recall in different fault states of TTS.

articleTitle: An Online Monitoring Method for Intelligent Tool Wear Prediction Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In response to the shortcomings of traditional monitoring methods, which often rely on empirical approaches or signal processing techniques and suffer from poor real-time performance and low accuracy, a milling tool wear monitoring model combining CNN with LSTM based on attention mechanism (ATT) is proposed. Firstly, the wavelet scalogram of the axial cutting force and its corresponding tool wear status are obtained. CNN is used to adaptively extract deep multidimensional features from the scalogram, which avoids the issue of information loss that might occur with traditional feature extraction methods. The multidimensional features are then input into the LSTM, which is well-suited for handling time series, and regression is used to accurately predict tool wear during the machining process. The ATT mechanism is introduced into the LSTM model, assigning different probability weights to the hidden layers. This addresses the issue of information loss in long sequences, enhances the influence of important features, and reduces the impact of less relevant features on predictions, thereby improving the model's prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Maintenance Decision for Manufacturing System Based on a Two-Stage Deterioration Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the rapid development of modern manufacturing, the complexity and diversity of manufacturing systems are increasing, which makes it particularly important to study the degradation and maintenance decision of manufacturing systems. However, in the contemporary research on this problem, how to determine the inspection interval and evaluating the impact of maintenance decision on the system are still a major difficulty. In this paper, a manufacturing process maintenance decision model is proposed. It first combines the two-stage deterioration theory with the deterioration-based fault probability modelling of the system degradation and fault generation probability. Secondly it combines different maintenance decisions to calculate the specific probability expression formulas for detecting different types of situations during inspection. Thirdly it combines the costs corresponding to the maintenance measures for different types of situations, and calculates the inspection interval corresponding to the lowest expected costs. The effectiveness of the proposed maintenance decision model is also evaluated through simulation experiments, which proves the feasibility of this study.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Diagnosis Method for Emulsion Pump Faults Based on PCA and Bi-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the fault of underground emulsion pump is difficult to diagnose under strong background noise, an intelligent fault diagnosis model of emulsion pump based on principal component analysis and bidirectional long-term memory network is proposed. Initially, the time-domain and frequency-domain features of the emulsion pump state data amalgamate to form a diverse set of features, thereby amplifying the saliency and robustness of the input features. Then principal component analysis is used to further reduce the dimension to improve the stability of features. On this basis, the accuracy of fault classification of emulsion pump is improved by using Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory. The test data from the test bench were used for verification. The results show that the proposed method has high classification and recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Li-Ion Battery Second-Life State of Health (SoH) Estimation with Polynomial Chaos
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Traction batteries, such as those used in electric vehicles, demand precise energy and power specifications. Operating under extreme temperatures, experiencing a high number of partial cycles, and facing fluctuating discharge rates contribute to notable battery degradation in the initial years of use. Nevertheless, a battery that has reached the end-of-life status in the traction application can find a “second life” in less demanding scenarios, such as stationary applications in a smart grid or low-power electric vehicles like golf carts. Second-life applications typically lack access to extensive measurements and monitoring infrastructure, although some level of monitoring remains essential to prevent potentially catastrophic failures. This work presents an approach to monitor the performance of second-life batteries by estimating the State of Health using measurements obtained during the first life and solely considering terminal voltage during the second life. The approach employs a polynomial chaos series to learn the relationship between the extracted features and the battery's discharge capacity in its initial life. In the subsequent life phase, the trained model is applied to estimate the SoH.

articleTitle: Life Prediction of BGA Solder Joints in Ceramic SIP-3D Packaging Under Temperature Cycling
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the development of electronic packaging technology towards miniaturization, low cost, and high integration, system in package (SIP) has become a key technology in the fabrication of electronic devices. However, the miniaturization of electronic packaging also brings some reliability issues. Such as the cracking problem of BGA solder joints under temperature cycling conditions. In this paper, a system integration package (SIP) was proposed based on ceramic package, which can achieve high integration while also achieving hermetic package. The lifetime of BGA solder joints under temperature cycling was studied through experimental and simulation methods. the experimental results were consistent with the simulation results. This package provides a solution for miniaturization of SIP.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis with Extremely Limited Samples: A Generalization Generator Improves GAN-Based Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Recently, generative adversarial networks (GANs) have provided a powerful data augmentation means for fault diagnosis in limited samples scenarios. Nevertheless, the challenge of poor generalization ability with extremely limited training data still limits effective applications of GANs-based methods for industrial fault diagnosis. To address this challenge, a novel generalization generator is proposed for machinery fault diagnostics under extremely limited samples. It mainly consists of a random sampling module, a generating module and a generalization module to improve the quality of generated samples. Meanwhile, our proposed generalization generator can be flexibly combined with the architecture of GANs, which proves its universality and robustness. A case study for machinery fault diagnostics considering extremely limited samples has been carried out to validate the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed method. Experiment results have demonstrated that our proposed generalization generator can generate high-quality time-series samples and achieve superior diagnostic results under extremely limited training data, in contrast to some mainstream data augmentation approaches.

articleTitle: Research on Federated Learning Privacy Protection Model for Valve Fault Intelligent Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Control valves are the core equipment in the braking system and fluid lines of rail transportation, and control valve troubleshooting can effectively enhance the service reliability of rail transportation equipment, improve the work safety, and reduce the maintenance cost. Current control valve fault diagnosis methods usually require sufficient high-quality condition monitoring data for model training, and the engineering application of diagnostic models often faces failure problems due to the difficulty of obtaining labeled sample data, “data silos” caused by data privacy protection, and the demand for cloud-side-end collaborative operation and maintenance. To this end, we propose a different specification control valve fault diagnosis method, GSI-FL, for multi-user siloed private data federated model migration, which performs a grayscale graph transformation on multi-user traffic data, uses convolutional neural networks to extract features and construct user local models, improves parameterization strategies to reduce the number of local model parameters, and collaborates with multiple users to construct a shared model for migration learning and sends it to the users, who use the local data to fine-tune the shared model to improve its performance. Users use the local data to fine-tune the shared model to realize fault diagnosis of control valves with different specifications. The test verifies the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Design for Testability and Evaluation System Based on Systems Modeling Language
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In modern complex system design, design for testability is a critical aspect to ensure system reliability, maintainability, and safety. Traditional methods of design for testability can no longer meet the complex demands of new generation equipment and systems. This paper explores testability design techniques based on SysML (Systems Modeling Language) and analyzes their specific applications in the testability design and evaluation system. By thoroughly analyzing system functional requirements and combining SysML modeling methods, a new design approach is proposed to enhance the clarity and traceability of testability requirements, optimizing the design of diagnostic schemes, condition monitoring, and fault detection. Through case studies, this paper demonstrates how to use self-developed testability software to conduct testability analysis and evaluation at different stages of system design, ensuring that the design meets predetermined testability requirements, and showing the effectiveness and feasibility of this method in practical applications.

articleTitle: Motor Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Multimodal and Spatial Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Currently, with the wide application of three-phase asynchronous motors, it is becoming increasingly important to accurately diagnose motor fault in complex environment. Due to the limitation of single-type modal data, traditional single-modality methods tend to be susceptible to external disturbances. The multimodal methods, in contrast, can take advantage of the complementary relationships between the different correlated modalities, compensating for the information lost by the disturbed modality, reducing the influence of external interference, and carry out motor fault diagnosis more comprehensively and accurately. Depending on multimodal methods, targeting the three modalities of vibration, sound and current of three-phase asynchronous motors, this paper compared two proposed algorithmic structures, proposes a method of multimodal motor fault diagnosis to achieve more accurate motor fault detection.

articleTitle: Research on the Reliability Tolerance Design Method of Nuclear Safety Analog Signal Isolator
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The reliability of analog signal isolators directly affects the operational safety of reactor protection systems. Due to parameter drift of electronic components, the reliability of analog signal isolators will decrease in high-temperature environments. To address this issue, a reliability tolerance design method is introduced. Based on the mechanism of analog signal isolators, an equivalent accuracy model of signal isolators has been established. Various parameters that affect circuit accuracy were selected using orthogonal method, and the signal-to-noise range of the parameters was analyzed. Based on the analysis results, optimization was carried out on the factors that have a significant impact. Through Monte Carlo simulation, it was confirmed that the tolerance design method increased the qualification rate from 93.98% to 99.83%, demonstrating the effectiveness of the design method.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Investigation on Data Redundancy of Large Battery Degradation Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) methods have demonstrated superiority in state of health (SOH) estimation of lithium ion batteries. Previous work has focused on collecting extensive data to train ML models; however, the richness of the information within these datasets remains unknown. This study systematically investigates redundancy in three datasets to quantitatively assess their information richness. We propose an iterative filtering (IF) method to remove redundant data and evaluate model performance after training on various sizes of the filtered data. The IF method proves more effective than random filtering, which randomly selects a proportion of data from the dataset. Results suggest that the root mean squared error (RMSE) increases by only 10% after removing up to 95% of the training data. The removed data results in lower errors than the test data split from the original dataset, further demonstrating that the removed data lacks new ageing information. Additionally, we demonstrate the generalizability of the proposed data filtering method by training one ML model on data filtered by another ML model. This work highlights that information richness is more important than dataset volume.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Model of Silk Dryer Based on KPCA-POA-KELM
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Identifying and detecting faults in the silk dryer is of great importance, as it serves as crucial equipment for tobacco drying. This article presents a novel fault diagnosis model for silk drying machine based on KPCA-POA-KELM. Firstly, the optimal feature set is obtained by utilizing Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) for feature optimization. Secondly, the regularization coefficient C and kernel function parameter σ of the Kernel-based Extreme Learning Machine (KELM) are optimized using Pelican Optimization Algorithm (POA). Finally, the proposed model is compared with other models, and the results show that the proposed model achieves a ten-fold cross-validation accuracy of 96.81 % in detecting complex faults. In comparison, the ten-fold cross-validation accuracy of the KPCA-KELM model is found to be the lowest at 68.88%.

articleTitle: Research and Application of an Improved RCM Method in Intelligent Operation and Maintenance of Train Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the traditional reliability-centered maintenance (RCM) analysis is too difficult and the cycle is too long, this paper puts forward an improved RCM method which is suitable for the characteristics of the train control system of rail transit. This method identifies the RCM analysis object through the field data, and clearly analyzes the pattern of the failures with time of the object based on the principle of reliability statistics. Based on this method, this paper analyzes the operation control system of a certain type of urban rail transit train, gives the life prediction method of typical components used in it, and puts forward the preventive maintenance strategy of the control system, which can be used as a credible input for the intelligent operation and maintenance of the control system.

articleTitle: Temperature Effects on Dual-MEMS Resonator-Based Measurement Circuits for Accurate Operating Temperature Diagnosis of Power Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper discusses the temperature effects on the dual-MEMS resonator-based temperature measurement circuits for accurate operating temperature diagnosis of the power equipment. The effects of temperature variation on the gain and phase of the transimpedance amplifier as a sustaining circuit, the effects of temperature on the resolution of the time-to-digital converter in the frequency-ratio measurement circuit, the effects of temperature on the impedance and phase in the PCB circuit, etc., are mainly discussed, respectively. The main purpose of this study is to explore the effects of temperature on each circuit module to guide the design of the highly-accurate temperature measurement circuits to improve the reliability of devices such as narrow-linewidth lasers.

articleTitle: A Multi-Feature Fusion Method for Fault Diagnosis with Applications in Tail Paddle Lever Bearing
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Aiming at the problems such as difficult monitoring and inaccurate state evaluation of helicopter tail rotor rod bearing. In this paper, temperature and vibration sensors are used to collect the temperature and vibration signals of bearings. Then the collected signal is constructed by means of noise reduction, feature extraction and feature fusion. And the characteristic data set is used as the input of fault diagnosis model after state index evaluation, health index generation and dimensionality reduction. Last, the improved gravity search algorithm (GGSA) is used to optimize the parameters of support vector machine (SVM) diagnosis model to form GGSA-SVM model for bearing fault diagnosis. In the simulation test, compared with the previous method, the number of iterations of the model is reduced by 21 times, the fitness is reduced to 0.4%, and the accuracy of bearing fault diagnosis is increased by 4.4% to 97.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. The experimental results show that the model can be used for bearing fault diagnosis better.

articleTitle: Weak Fault Diagnosis of Ship Fuel Injectors Based on Adaptive CYCBD and RCHBDE
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Accurately diagnosing weak faults in marine fuel injectors is essential for minimizing diesel engine testing and maintenance expenses. Consequently, this paper introduces an innovative weak fault diagnosis method for common rail injectors, integrating the Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (ISSA) optimized maximum second-order cyclicality blind decoding (CYCBD) with Refine Composite Hierarchy Bidirectional Diversity Entropy (RCHBDE). Initially, we propose the ISSA algorithm to find the optimal filter length for CYCBD under different states of fuel injector signals, and apply the optimal CYCBD filter to denoise and filter the fuel injector source signal. To overcome the limitations of Multiscale Bidirectional Diversity Entropy (MBDE) in capturing high-frequency component information, we introduce RCHBDE for extracting fault features from the filtered signals. This proposed method effectively detects weak fault conditions in common rail injectors and, compared to existing methods, demonstrates superior fault recognition rates.

Author Keywords: Refine Composite Hierarchy Bidirectional Diversity Entropy

articleTitle: Hierarchical Improved Diversity Entropy for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearings
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Adequate extraction of feature information from nonlinear dynamic signals is the difficult and the most central part of realizing intelligent fault diagnosis of rolling bearings. The existing diversity entropy (DE) has excellent characteristics, but it only considers the relationship between the angles of neighboring orbits in phase space, and there are still inherent defects in feature extraction, which affects the diagnostic accuracy. In order to solve this problem, this paper firstly proposes the improved diversity entropy (IDE), and further proposes the hierarchical improved diversity entropy (HIDE) by combining the idea of hierarchical decomposition. Then, experiments with different types and degrees of rolling bearing failures are designed to compare and validate with other three advanced entropy-based methods. The experimental results show that compared with hierarchical diversity entropy (HDE), hierarchical weighted permutation entropy (HWPE), and hierarchical dispersion entropy (HDispE), the HIDE proposed in this paper has more prominent feature extraction capability and fault diagnosis accuracy. It also provides an efficient tool for intelligent fault diagnosis of rolling bearings.

articleTitle: Application of HMM in Fault Diagnosis of Permanent Magnet DC Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of fault diagnosis of permanent magnet DC (PMDC) motors, this paper applies Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to the fault identification and classification of motor. In this paper, based on the dynamic differential equation of the PMDC motors, the current simulation data of four motor states are obtained, including normal, inter-turn short circuit, brush wear and resistance increase. Then, the HMM is constructed, and the HMM is used to identify and classify the fault of the current simulation data. The results show that when the PMDC motors are faulty, its current signal characteristics will be abnormal, and the use of HMM to identify and classify the current signal of the motor has achieved good results, reflecting the advantages of HMM in the analysis of time-domain signals. The research results have certain reference value for the fault diagnosis of PMDC motors.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Complex Systems by Fusing Multi-Level Information
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction holds great importance reliability and is regarded as a crucial step in prognostics and health management (PHM). Traditional methods often demand extensive testing durations and large sample sizes, or they might pose considerable risks in estimation. Consequently, the utilization of multi-level information is considered to overcome these limitations and a novel method for estimating the residual life of complex systems is presented. Firstly, the fusion of multisource information is employed to determine both the prior and posterior distributions of components, subsequently the multiorder moments of reliability under the posterior distributions are derived. On this basis, the moments of the whole system are calculated by these moments of components. Finally, the compound Simpson formula is applied to obtain the estimations of the system's residual life. An illustrative example is provided and by comparing with the Monte Carlo simulation results, the validity of the proposed method is proved.

articleTitle: Lamb Wave Damage Detection of Composite T-Joint Based on Cross Correlation Peak of Local Signal Envelope
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The damage monitoring of composite T-joint in their service is very important to ensure the safety of aircraft structures. However, the load variations have significant effects on the Lamb wave-based damage detection of composite T-joint. In order to mitigate the load effect, a damage index method based on cross correlation peak of local signal envelope is developed, which measures the similarity of Lamb wave signals by the maximum cross correlation coefficient of the signal envelopes. The validity of the method is assessed by the synthetic signals and damage detection of composite T-joint under tensile load. The results show that the method can effectively mitigate the load effect on the Lamb wave-based damage detection, and detect the damage of composite T-joint under tensile load accurately.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Signal Integrity of Nuclear Safety DCS Main Control Module
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In response to the problem of difficulty in quickly and effectively evaluating the signal transmission quality of high-speed serial communication hardware PCB design in the hardware design stage of nuclear safety DCS main control module, this study proposes a method of establishing a complete signal simulation using the Tx-Diff and Rx-Diff models of ADS simulation software. The simulation accuracy is improved by optimizing the differences between PCB design and board factory production, increasing the location of ports to extract S parameters, and adding crosstalk and signal jitter factors to the simulation schematic. Then, frequency domain simulation is carried out to obtain the eye diagram of high-speed serial communication wiring. The research results show that the eye height of the conventional simulated eye diagram is 392mV and the eye width is 175 ps. The eye height of the simulated eye diagram in this paper is 346 mV and the eye width is 143 ps. The eye height measured by a professional laboratory is 321.271 mV and the eye width is 109.016 ps. The simulation results are in good agreement with the measured results, and both are far greater than the PCIE 2.0 specification and the receiver chip judgment standard of eye height greater than 110mV and minimum eye width greater than 0.3U1 (60 ps). Therefore, the signal integrity simulation method established in this study can be used to evaluate the signal transmission quality of high-speed serial communication hardware PCB design and improve the reliability of hardware PCB design.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method of Rolling Bearing Based on Feature Mode Decomposition and Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Rolling bearing failure will affect the normal operation of the mechanical equipment. Effective early failure diagnosis can avoid unnecessary losses caused by bearing fault. A fault diagnostic method of rolling bearing relying on Feature Mode Decomposition (FMD) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is proposed in this article. Firstly, the effective fault feature information in rolling bearing vibration signal will be extracted by FMD method, and then the collected feature information is introduced into the CNN framework to effectively classify different types of faults of rolling bearing. This method is of practical significance for the fault classification of rolling bearing under the strong background noise.

articleTitle: A Frequency Adaptive Vibration Analysis Method for Variable Speed Rotating RV Reducer
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Industrial robots commonly perform cyclic reciprocating motions during operation. The dynamic loads caused by frequent acceleration and deceleration make the RV reducers of the robots prone to failure and generate abnormal vibration during operation. However, the variable speed condition makes it difficult to analyze the frequency of the vibration signal. This paper proposes a frequency-adaptive method to analyze the vibration signals to identify the frequency range of vibration energy distribution. A filter bank is designed based on this frequency range, enhancing the target frequency while lowering other unnecessary frequency components of the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) spectrogram. Features extracted from the enhanced spectrograms were employed to identify and classify various failure types. In experimental trials involving a six-joint serial industrial robot, the frequency-adaptive approach achieved a classification accuracy of 93.06% across 108 trials. These results suggest that the proposed method is highly effective for monitoring variable speed conditions and diagnosing faults in RV reducers.

articleTitle: Zero-Shot Fault Diagnosis Model for Manufacturing Process with Multi-Dimension Attributes
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The problem of unbalanced fault samples or even zero samples at the initial stage of production line deployment for manufacturing processes will affect the accuracy of fault diagnosis models at batch production. In this case, zero-shot learning is well utilized for fault diagnosis of manufacturing processes. However, existing zero-shot learning methods ignore the representation of fault attributes in different dimensions. Based on this, this paper proposes a zero-shot fault diagnosis method for manufacturing processes based on multi-dimension attribute descriptions to fully utilize the public knowledge to identify unknown faults. First, the fault modes in the manufacturing process are analyzed using process failure mode and effects analysis (PFMEA) to form the multi-dimension fault attribute description space in fault dimension, equipment dimension and process dimension. After that, a multilayer network is utilized to extract the features related to the fault modes in the process quality data and establish the mapping relationship between the attribute space and the feature space in order to realize the zero-shot fault diagnosis of the manufacturing process. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using the Tennessee-Eastman Process (TEP) process.

articleTitle: An X-Ray Substance Recognition Method Applied to Explosives Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The detection of Improvised Explosive Devices (IED) represents a significant challenge in the field of security. The implementation of conventional X-ray transmission security inspection equipment for improvised explosives in the organic explosives sector presents a challenge. In contrast, the application of the X-ray back scattering principle enables more accurate detection of organic materials. However, the X-ray back scatter signal is of low intensity, which gives rise to the issue of how the parameters of the X-ray back scatter detection device should be set and enhancing identification accuracy. In this paper, a material identification method based on X-ray back scattering of plastic scintillator detector is proposed, and an X-ray back scattering detector device is constructed to collect data of simulated organic explosives, detonation devices, and metal shells. Ultimately, the distinction between the three types of substances was successfully achieved through preliminary data processing.

articleTitle: Software Reliability Prediction Model Based on Improved Resampling Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Reliable software can provide security in finance, aerospace and other fields, and it can help find and repair potential software defects and problems, reducing the cost of software maintenance and support. The difficulty of software reliability is that modern software systems are becoming more and more complex, which makes it more difficult to predict and analyze software errors. In this paper, a software reliability evaluation model based on an improved particle filter algorithm is proposed. In the resamping stage, the selection probability of unique position particles is improved through the adaptive distance comparison step. In addition, the method further proposes the strategy of generating new particles, re-selecting low-weight particles and adding random noise, and finally obtaining small batches of new particles. The software reliability model and improved particle filter algorithm are combined to predict the number of software faults, and more accurate prediction results are obtained.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Online Monitoring System for the Grab-type Ship Unloader Based on Multi-source Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The bridge-type grab ship unloader is one of the main ship unloading equipment at dry bulk cargo terminals. In recent years, with the continuous advancement of the construction of automated terminals, the operation mode of GSU has undergone tremendous changes, gradually shifting from operation by operators on large equipment to remote operation or automated operation. The traditional operation and maintenance of GSU is passive, and the main mode is planned maintenance. This method has problems such as poor timeliness and high cost, and is also not suitable for the development trend of automated terminals. Under such circumstances, strengthening the real-time monitoring of the operating status of GSU is particularly important. In response to the problems existing in traditional operations in this paper, the finite element modeling analysis of the mechanical structure of GSU was carried out, and combined with the daily operation and maintenance records, the main monitoring parts were determined. The overall architecture of the online monitoring system of GSU was designed, and the functional designs of the stress analysis subsystem, vibration analysis subsystem, fault diagnosis and real-time early warning subsystem of the online monitoring system of GSU were carried out, and it was applied on the port GSU. The design and application of the online monitoring system of GSU can promptly discover the potential safety hazards of the equipment and play a positive role in promoting the construction and development of automated terminals.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis and Optimization Allocation for FOWT Systems Based on FTA
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In response to the reliability and safety concerns associated with the operation of Floating Offshore Wind Turbine (FOWT) in marine environments, this study meticulously applies the Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) method to assess the dependability of the mooring, generator, tower, and floating foundation systems integral to FOWT. By developing comprehensive fault tree models, this research qualitatively determines that the generator and mooring systems are the most susceptible to failure within the context of FOWT, scrutinizing the pivotal failure locations and their underlying causes. Subsequently, quantitative analysis reveals the failure probability of 1.0909xl0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> for the subsystems and establishes a Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) of 91.66 hours. Through these methods, the paper delves into strategies aimed at optimizing the allocation of reliability, suggesting preemptive measures and a suite of Reliability Optimization Allocation (ROA) methodologies, including the equal allocation method, expected value allocation method, and the AGREE allocation method. Utilizing these approaches, the study aligns the reliability demands of individual subsystems with the overarching system's reliability goals, thereby offering valuable guidance for improving the reliability standards of FOWT.

articleTitle: Application of Highly Accelerated Life Test Technology in Fully Electronic Interlocking Controller in Rail Transit
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous development of electronic technology, rail transit equipment has been constantly updated, especially signal control systems, which have fully entered the era of all-electronic technology. All-electronic technology has achieved good application results in many fields such as rail transit, providing good technical support for the development of China's rail transit industry. Products using all-electronic technology require high reliability and rapid development and verification. Highly accelerated life test (HALT) is an efficient reliability tool that fully exposes the potential defects of products by simulating high-stress environments, thereby improving the reliability level of products. This paper takes a certain type of safety controller in all-electronic interlocking as the research object, conducts HALT in the product R&D phase, and significantly improves the reliability of the product by improving the defects found, achieving good application results.

articleTitle: Research on Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Multiscale Hybrid-Domain Information Entropy
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To enhance the accuracy and reliability of fault diagnosis for rolling bearings in aero-engines and address the poor stability of traditional time-domain feature parameters under varying operating conditions, this paper proposes a fault feature extraction method based on multiscale hybrid-domain information entropy. Utilizing Shannon entropy theory and the concept of information fusion, this method integrates information entropy from the time-domain, frequency-domain, and time-frequency domain to construct a comprehensive feature vector. Specifically, it employs entropy measures such as fuzzy entropy, power spectrum entropy, and singular spectrum entropy, and calculates the hybrid-domain information entropy matrix using normalized Euclidean distance. The method is experimentally validated on multiple bearing fault types, analyzing entropy characteristics under different fault conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits good stability and robustness across various fault conditions. The hybrid-domain information entropy fusion method significantly improves fault diagnosis accuracy and consistency, effectively extracting fault features of rolling bearings. This proposed method is not only applicable to fault diagnosis of aero-engine rolling bearings but also holds broad application potential for health monitoring and fault prediction in other complex mechanical systems. It introduces new perspectives and tools for fault diagnosis in complex mechanical systems, contributing to enhanced precision and reliability in equipment health management.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method of Train Transmission Systems Based on Multi-sensor Data Fusion and Multi-channel Convolutional Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To accurately diagnose the train transmission system faults, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on multi-sensor data fusion and multi-channel convolutional attention network (MCCANet). Firstly, multi-source signals collected from key components of the transmission system are converted into multi-channel data utilizing the proposed data fusion method, effectively integrating the fault status information of all components. Next, MCCANet is proposed to process multi-channel sensor data, which combines one-dimensional convolutional kernels with attention mechanisms to extract features of data, using average pooling and global average pooling for dimensionality reduction to capture key fault features effectively. Finally, to address the issue of generalization under cross-working conditions, MCCANet serves as the base model, and probabilistic voting is applied to the predictions from several trained models. Probabilistic voting leverages the probability distributions predicted by these models, enhancing the accuracy and robustness of the results. Fault diagnosis experiments on the train transmission system dataset of 2024 PHM-Beijing data challenge demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy with small samples and across working conditions, proving its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Semi-Supervised Fault Diagnosis Method for Gearbox Based on Convolutional Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To address the issues of limited labeled data and the tendency of traditional supervised neural networks to overfit, resulting in low fault diagnosis accuracy in real industrial scenarios, this paper innovatively proposes a semi-supervised learning method based on Convolutional Autoencoder (SSCAE) for gearbox fault diagnosis. First, both labeled and a large number of unlabeled samples are used to pre-train the improved convolutional autoencoder(CAE), introducing a classification loss to guide the encoder in learning features beneficial for sample classification. The pre-trained encoder parameters are then loaded into a classifier, and the classifier is trained using the labeled information, with supervised contrastive loss introduced to fully utilize the labeled information. Finally, the method was validated on a gearbox dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed method, in situations with a small number of labeled samples, effectively utilizes the unlabeled information and achieves better fault identification performance than traditional supervised and semi-supervised fault diagnosis methods.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Cutting Tools with an Optimal Feature Construction Method of DiCCA
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction plays an essential role in the prognostic health management of cutting tools, which aims to ensure workpiece surface quality and extend tool life. Although deep learning methods have exhibited great performance in the field of tool RUL prediction, establishing an effective deep learning model usually requires extensive training data, and collecting substantial tool failure data in the actual milling process is time-consuming and expensive. Alternatively, constructing robust tool degradation features and developing a lightweight prediction model might be more practical and deployment-friendly. Therefore, this paper introduces an optimal tool degradation feature extraction method with a tailored dimension reduction algorithm named dynamic-inner canonical correlation analysis (DiCCA), where the temporal dependency and dynamic information hidden in the sequential tool degradation process are captured for the RUL prediction of cutting tools. Experimental studies are performed with a milling dataset, and the results indicate that the optimal tool degradation feature extracted by the proposed DiCCA can explicitly reflect the degradation process of cutting tools, and accurate RUL prediction can be achieved through a lightweight BP model.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis of Multi-Mode Electromechanical Compound Transmission System for Hybrid Electric Vehicles Based on Kernel Density Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To effectively monitor operational status and detect faults during mode transitions in hybrid electric vehicles, This study examines the multimode electromechanical compound transmission system (MM-EMCT HEV), a specific model of power-split hybrid electric vehicles. It identifies key faults based on their occurrence frequency and the feasibility of simulating them in MM-EMCT HEVs. A fault diagnosis framework is developed utilizing analytical redundancy relations (ARRs), which incorporates strategies for generating residuals across sensors and actuators, along with evaluation methods using kernel density estimation. The detectability and isolatability of the MM-EMCT are analyzed in detail. Simulations and verifications of the residual responses under common faults are performed using Matlab/Simulink and Simscape. The findings indicate that residual evaluation based on kernel density estimation effectively detects and isolates faults in multimode electromechanical compound transmission systems.

articleTitle: Research on Safety Index of Telecommunication System Based on Markov Chain and State Continuity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of being able to comprehensively, intuitively and dynamically reflect the safety of railroad telecommunication system, this paper proposes a research method of safety index of telecommunication system based on Markov chain and state continuity analysis. Adopting Markov chain theory, an average state transfer matrix is established by analyzing the transfer probability between the three states of normal, fault and accident of the telecommunication equipment in a certain period of time. At the same time, the state continuity coefficient is introduced to quantify the impact of the duration of each state in a certain period of time on the system safety, and a comprehensive safety index model reflecting the dynamic safety of the telecommunication system is constructed. Finally, an example verification is carried out with a telecommunication system as an example, and the results show that the model can accurately capture the change trend of the equipment state, significantly improve the ability to reflect the operational safety condition of the telecommunication system, and provide a reliable reference basis for equipment management and maintenance decision-making.

articleTitle: UAV Imagery Based Fine-Grained Defect Recognition System of Noise Barrier Fasteners in High-Speed Railroad
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Noise barriers along high-speed railroads have the function of blocking the high-pressure airflow generated by the passage of high-speed trains and preventing the intrusion of foreign objects. However, under the influence of complex operation environment and natural factors, along with the increase of service time of noise barriers, various defects generated by noise barriers pose a threat to the safe operation of railroads, especially the defects of fasteners that are used for fixing noise barrier bases. In addition, classical learning-based deep networks are difficult to make decisions on fine-grained fastener defect categories. This paper proposes a fine-grained defect recognition system of noise barrier fasteners using Region Shuffling and Position Regression Network (RPNet). First, RPNet leverages tailored shuffling rule to achieve destructive fastener images, which can assist the RPNet to focus on the local vital details. Second, a position regression structure integrated in RPNet are employed to learn and regress the original location distribution after feature extraction of RepVGG-based backbone. Third, based on dual-branch fully connection structure, RPNet enables the decision-making of subtle defect categories. Finally, the comprehensive experiment results represent that proposed system can acquire a faster inference speed yet maintains a higher detection rate in the complex UAV -based noise barrier dataset.

articleTitle: A New Collaborative Learning Method for Fault Diagnosis of Traction Motors Considering Information Missing
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: As the core component of complex equipment such as tanks, the health of traction motors directly affects the safety and reliability of the equipment. In practical applications, motors often face the problem of missing information caused by multi-rate sampling of sensors. However, existing methods have the following limitations: 1) They directly ignore the missing data and labels. 2) Supervisory signals that rely on tagged data in the absence of data and cannot effectively utilize untagged data. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents a collaborative learning strategy (CESSL), implemented in two stages. The first stage uses an unsupervised data reconstruction strategy, merging a parallel self-learning feature extraction network with a Generative Adversarial Network that includes identity mapping residual blocks, to efficiently extract features from incomplete data. The second stage employs a semi-supervised learning model based on this feature extraction network for label completion and classification, enhanced by a multi-layer Local Maximum Mean Discrepancy (LMMD) module to evaluate domain differences under various operating conditions and integrates predictive and consistency regularization losses into the loss function for improved model performance. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through fault simulation experiments on a three-phase motor. The CESSL method outperforms other state-of-the-art diagnostic methods, maintaining high accuracy even when both data and labels are missing.

articleTitle: A Method for Fault Diagnosis of Train Axle Box Bearings Based on Impact Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To address the issues of poor decoupling ability and stability in traditional impact pulse methods, a train axle box bearing fault diagnosis method based on impact detection is proposed. Firstly, fast squared envelope kurtogram (FSEK) analysis, resonance demodulation and adaptive frequency band search are utilized to extract the target impact components from the vibration signals. Then, a high fault sensitivity inverse standard deviation (ISD) indicator is constructed, which can effectively extract and amplify the impact characteristics of the fault signal. Finally, a regional averaging strategy is used to achieve continuous and automatic fault detection for long time series data. The effectiveness, stability, and decoupling performance of the proposed indicator and method are verified using test bench data and real vehicle data. The results show that the proposed indicator can effectively extract the impact characteristics in fault signals. Compared with other methods, the proposed method demonstrates better stability under varying operating conditions and superior decoupling performance under multi-source vibration coupling. In the test with bench test data, both the accuracy and recall rate of the proposed method reached 100%.

articleTitle: Intermittent Fault Diagnosis Technology: Research Status and Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The advancement of technology has led to intermittent faults (IFs) posing a serious problem for system safety and maintenance costs. Though fault diagnosis technology has progressed, there is limited research on diagnosing IFs. This paper introduces the concept of IFs, presents the challenges and current research, discusses diagnosis technology from different perspectives, and aims to provide a reference for future research in this area.

articleTitle: Event-Driven Explainable Fault Diagnosis Method for Drilling Pump
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis is a critical aspect of Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) for drilling pumps. The variable speed and load characteristics of drilling pumps present challenges for extracting fault-sensitive features. In this paper, a novel event-driven explainable fault diagnosis method for drilling pumps is proposed. The influence of rotational speed on original signals is eliminated, the correlation between component motion and vibration impacts is established, and the most sensitive features representing the operational state of a drilling pump are extracted, resulting in high-precision fault diagnosis. The diagnosis process employs order tracking and angular domain resampling to convert time-domain non-stationary original signals into angular domain stationary signals. Critical motion events are determined based on the correlation analysis method for rotating-reciprocating components. A fault identification method based on a cloud model is constructed. Finally, the proposed method is validated by experiments resulting with an average accuracy of 98%, which is significantly higher than other methods.

articleTitle: Overview and Design of Central Maintenance System for Civil Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In order to ensure the maintenance and support capability level of large-scale aviation equipment, the central maintenance system of large-scale aviation equipment is crucial. It is required to accurately grasp the health status of equipment, conduct real-time monitoring, and timely formulate corresponding maintenance and support strategies based on the fault status of aviation equipment and its various subsystems, combined with ground maintenance and support resources, to achieve precise fault localization. It is of great significance to improve the operational safety of large-scale aviation equipment, reduce maintenance and support costs, and enhance maintenance and support efficiency. It is a landmark system in the intelligent development trend of large-scale aviation equipment and a key subsystem essential for various types of key equipment.. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Compound Fault Diagnosis Framework based on Multi-Source Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Condition monitoring and fault diagnosis of rotating machinery play an important role in the field of prognosis and health management (PHM). To address the challenges in compound fault diagnosis of rotating machinery, we propose a fusion method in feature-level for multi-sensor data, which can extract effective fault features from multi-sensor data. Meanwhile, we employ a multi-output classifier to solve the decoupling of compound faults which is able to recognize unseen compound fault combinations. Based on these two techniques, we designed a CNN model for compound fault diagnosis. In our model, the multi-sensor data are first fed into two parallel channels, time-domain and frequency-domain, where the features in multi-sensor data are extracted and fused in the time and frequency domains respectively, then the extracted features go into a module where the time-domain and frequency-domain features are fused, and finally, multi-output classifier is used to decouple the compound fault and output classification decision. The experimental results show that the proposed compound fault diagnosis model has achieved good performance.

articleTitle: State-of-Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on EIS and CNN-Transformer Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Estimating the state of health (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is a challenging task. In this paper, we propose a novel convolution neural network (CNN)-Transformer model for the estimation of SOH, using only electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data. The publicly accessible datasets are employed for both the training and testing phases. In the data preprocessing stage, highly correlated EIS features are selected using the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC). The proposed model is implemented in MATLAB for training and prediction on a low-performance platform devoid of Graphical Processing Unit (GPU) support, thereby demonstrating its broad applicability. The simulation outcomes indicate that the mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) are maintained within 3%, and the coefficient of determination (R2) reaches 98.72<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, outperforming standalone Transformer and LSTM models. The proposed model is therefore both accurate and practical, offering the possibility of applying deep learning models into battery management systems (BMS).

articleTitle: Decision on Fault Diagnosis of Liquid Propellant Rocket Engine Based on Deep Analytic Hierarchy Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Fault diagnosis is critical for liquid-propellant rocket engines (LREs). Although there are mature single diagnostic algorithms for both slow-varying faults triggered by abnormal slow-varying parameters and fast-varying faults triggered by abnormal fast-varying parameters, these algorithms differ in parameters and principles, resulting in a lack of effective interaction. Consequently, a comprehensive decision-making method is urgently needed for the LRE system to achieve final decisions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a comprehensive decision-making method based on the Deep Analytic Hierarchy Process (DAHP). Firstly, two diagnostic algorithms are selected for each type of fault: the thermodynamic model algorithm A and the multi-parameter adaptive threshold algorithm B for slow-varying faults, as well as the vibration analysis algorithm C and the displacement analysis algorithm D for rapid-varying faults. Then, DAHP is utilized to comprehensively consider the individual and overall performance of the algorithms, applying prior knowledge from offline evaluations to calculate two layers of weights. The first layer weights are computed based on the fault detection rate, accuracy, false alarm rate, and missed alarm rate of each algorithm. The second layer weights are determined by integrating the overall fault coverage and detection speed of the slow-varying and rapid-varying algorithms. Finally, expert decision-making experience in the field of fault diagnosis, combined with practical engineering rules, is used to determine the final decision. Case studies using historical test data demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed deep analytic hierarchy process. This method not only enhances the accuracy and reliability of fault diagnosis but also provides more scientific decision support for the health management of liquid propellant rocket engines.

articleTitle: A Review and Study of Fault Prediction Algorithms for Civil Aircraft Mechanical Products
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the process of civil aircraft operation, due to the changing operating environment and long-term operation, mechanical products gradually age and the remaining uesful life gradually decreases, which has a great impact on the safety and reliability of civil aircraft. This paper focuses on the characteristics and application status of mechanical product remaining useful life prediction research methods, reviews the current research status of related literature at home and abroad, summarizes the current hotspots and achievements of mechanical product remaining useful life prediction research, and summarizes the current remaining useful life prediction research of civil aircraft mechanical products in the theoretical modeling and testing of a number of problems. Meanwhile, based on the nominal stress method, the contact fatigue remaining useful life is predicted for a typical civil aircraft mechanical product-roller slide. This method can be used for remaining useful life prediction after the real-time transfer of aircraft loads, which provides a reference research direction for future in-depth remaining useful life prediction research of civil aircraft mechanical products.

articleTitle: Incremental Multistep Forecasting of Battery Degradation Using Pseudo Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Data-driven models accurately perform early battery prognosis to prevent equipment failure and further safety hazards. Most existing machine learning (ML) models work in offline mode which must consider their retraining post-deployment every time new data distribution is encountered. Hence, there is a need for an online ML approach where the model can adapt to varying distributions. However, existing online incremental multistep forecasts are a great challenge as there is no way to correct the model of its forecasts at the current instance. Also, these methods need to wait for a considerable amount of time to acquire enough streaming data before retraining. In this study, we propose iFSNet (incremental Fast and Slow learning Network) which is a modified version of FSNet for a single-pass mode (sample-by-sample) to achieve multistep forecasting using pseudo targets. It uses a simple linear regressor of the input sequence to extrapolate pseudo future samples (pseudo targets) and calculate the loss from the rest of the forecast and keep updating the model. The model benefits from the associative memory and adaptive structure mechanisms of FSNet, at the same time the model incrementally improves by using pseudo targets. The proposed model achieved 0.00197 RMSE and 0.00154 MAE on datasets with smooth degradation trajectories while it achieved 0.01588 RMSE and 0.01234 MAE on datasets having irregular degradation trajectories with capacity regeneration spikes.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Time-Frequency Alignment with Convolutional Block Attention Module
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In various complex industrial scenarios, the collection of bearing fault data is expensive and time-consuming, making intelligent fault diagnosis a highly challenging task in scenarios with few labeled fault samples. To address this issue, we propose a self-supervised time-frequency alignment with convolutional block attention module (SSTFA-CBAM). This framework combines the characteristics of time-domain and frequency-domain signals, and achieves efficient feature extraction and transfer learning through self-supervised learning. Firstly, an overlapping segmentation strategy is adopted to increase the diversity of the original samples. Then, through fast Fourier transform and Gaussian noise enhancement, the data is input into frequency domain and time domain encoders respectively to extract deep features of unlabeled data. During this process, we utilized the convolutional block attention module (CBAM) to adaptively weight the features, enhancing the network's attention to key features. Finally, a small number of labeled samples are used to fine tune the classifier after the time-domain encoder, achieving accurate judgment of fault data. The SSTFA-CBAM framework significantly enhances the reliability of bearing fault diagnosis through precise feature extraction and self-supervised learning, providing robust data support for Predictive Health Management (PHM) systems and reinforcing the overall stability and safety of industrial systems.

articleTitle: Non-Integer Order Polynomial Network: A Novel Fault Diagnosis Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Non-Integer Order Polynomial Network (NIOPN) designed to achieve higher approximation accuracy by employing fractional moments to approximate nonlinear functions, compared to the integer moments used in traditional Multidimensional Taylor Networks (MTN). The fractional moment polynomials offer richer and more precise mathematical representations, enhancing the accuracy of function approximation. To validate the effectiveness of NIOPN, we applied it to fault diagnosis in Air Handling Units (AHU) within HVAC systems. Fault diagnosis in AHU systems is critical for maintaining operational efficiency and preventing system failures. By utilizing NIOPN, our model achieved a high diagnostic accuracy of 100%, outperforming traditional methods such as random forest, support vector machine, K-nearest neighbors, and the latest residual MTN. These results demonstrate NIOPN's strong potential as a powerful tool for fault diagnosis in HVAC systems. Given its versatility as a general model, NIOPN can also be employed in in other classification, regression, and prediction tasks. This model presents a new universal approach distinct from neural networks, offering a new tool for pattern recognition tasks.

articleTitle: Review of Ground Test Methods and Techniques of Space Motion Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Space motion mechanism is the key component of satellite, spacecraft and space station and other spacecraft, which plays a decisive role in mission reliability and life of spacecraft. The function of space mechanism is complex and the environment condition is special. The main means of design verification is to carry out ground simulation test in the development process. In this paper, based on the needs analysis of ground verification for space motion mechanism, the requirements of verification tests are discussed. In addition, the general situation of the verification tests for typical space mechanisms such as the restrain-release mechanism for SAOCOM, Hexapod Linear Actuator (HLA) for the Athena and robotic arm joint mechanism for China Space Station are described in detail. Finally, according to the application and development needs of the space motion mechanism in the future, the relevant key test technologies are summarized, and the further research content is also discussed, which can provide support for the development of the test methods and technologies of the space motion mechanism.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Regional Features in Visible Light Images of Maritime Ship Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Given the current state of visible light monitoring and recognition of ship images, this paper proposes a method for analyzing the regional features of maritime ship targets based on visible light image data. By performing preprocessing operations such as grayscaling, binarization, and edge extraction on ship images, better input is provided for the extraction of Hu invariant moments and Angular Radial Transform (ART) descriptors in this experiment. The paper selects the two most discriminative feature values of Hu invariant moments, retaining their sensitivity to image brightness and contrast, to form a new feature vector, NEWHu. NEWHu reduces the dimensionality of the feature vector, simplifying the computation and storage process while reliably distinguishing different types of ships. The paper proposes linearly weighted fusion of NEWHu and ART features into a feature vector, NHA, for the classification of maritime ship targets. NHA captures multiple aspects of the target's shape, texture, and spatial distribution, allowing for more accurate and reliable classification of different types of ships. This comprehensive feature vector enhances the recognition accuracy and improves the distinction between different ship types compared to Hu invariant moments, NEWHu, and ART. Therefore, this method offers greater practicality and reliability in naval military and monitoring applications.

articleTitle: A Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network for Small Sample Fault Diagnosis of Rotating Machinery
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Graph convolutional network (GCN) provides an excellent feature extraction way for fusing condition monitored multi-channel signals, making it widely employed in fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. Some spatial-temporal networks based on GCN have been proposed with the aim of improving diagnostic performance by extracting features from both the spatial and temporal domains. The improvement in feature extraction has also enhanced the diagnostic performance under small sample scenarios. However, most of the existing studies construct spatial-temporal framework by stacking spatial and temporal modules, which could degrade the spatial-temporal correlation. To obtain more inherent fault representations and improve diagnostic performance under small sample scenarios, this paper proposed a spatial-temporal graph convolutional network. In the proposed method, each sensor channel is treated as one node to build a multi-channel interactive graph. The data at each time step is constructed as a subgraph, and every three adjacent subgraphs are connected by the same nodes to form a spatial-temporal graph. With the help of learnable position embeddings, graph convolution is conducted on spatial-temporal graphs to synchronize the extraction of spatial-temporal features. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through a subway train transmission system fault dataset. Comparative studies show that the proposed method possesses strong feature extraction capability, and exhibits better diagnostic performance in scenarios with small samples.

articleTitle: Critical Scenario Risk Modeling and Analysis: A Case Study of Autonomous Rail Transit Trains
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In recent years, the development direction of next-generation railways has been to enhance the autonomy of driverless trains. Although there are anticipated benefits in reducing human errors and significantly improving overall efficiency and safety levels, the development of driverless trains will undoubtedly introduce new risks to the braking process. This paper aims to identify the sensitive factors that increase the risk of train accidents and predict the dynamic changes in these risk conditions.
