First, through literature review and expert consultations, the paper analyzes risk scenarios directly related to train operation safety and key factors leading to a decline in braking performance. It then models the sequence of events leading to risks using a hybrid causal logic approach. Next, addressing issues such as structural redundancy and the lack of consideration for temporal dynamics in traditional HCL methods, the study introduces dynamic Bayesian networks for model transformation. Finally, the Expectation-Maximization algorithm in GeNIe software is used to calculate the state transition and conditional probabilities of the model, predicting the overall trend of train accident risk and analyzing the most sensitive factors leading to risks at different time intervals. These findings are significant for enhancing the autonomy and safety of driverless trains.

articleTitle: Redundancy Digital Output Module Design Based on 1oo2D Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Considering that most current nuclear power manufacturers have implemented diagnostic technologies for high reliability digital output modules to ensure the correctness of digital output signals, such technologies can only confirm the fault status of the digital output channels and report failures. however, Unable to predicted failures in advance to transition faulty modules into a safe output state. This paper discusses the design of a redundant digital output module based on a 1oo2D architecture. By paralleling the output channels of mutually redundant digital output modules and providing a communication channel for status interaction between redundant modules, the design achieves controllable status of redundant output channels in the event of a single module failure, ensuring safe output of redundant channels. Additionally, based on fault analysis, static and dynamic diagnostic circuits are added to detect short circuit and open circuit conditions of the relay contacts executing the digital output signals. This ensures that the downstream load equipment will not fail to act or act incorrectly when a single module fails, and allows for the prediction of failures in advance. Finally, the design's feasibility is validated through functional testing and fault injection testing.

articleTitle: Markov Latent Frequency Transition Analysis for Robust Bearing Diagnosis in Transient Noise Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In real-world applications, the diagnostic accuracy of rolling bearings is often compromised by environmental factors such as variable rotational speeds, transient noises, and unexpected mechanical impacts. These factors can obscure damage symptoms, making precise detection of bearing failures challenging. Conventional diagnostic methods struggle to handle these complexities and often miss failure features hidden in multifaceted random transient noise. To address these issues, this research introduces the Markov Latent Frequency Transition Peak Rate (MLFTPR) methodology. MLFTPR focuses on accurately monitoring temporal state transitions and identifying anomalous signals, aiming to mitigate transient noise at the source and improve resistance to external disturbances. This enhances precision and reliability in demodulation band selection. Additionally, an amplitude interference-reduction feature is integrated to recognize and suppress transient noise effectively. Experimental results validate the efficacy of MLFTPR, demonstrating its capability to accurately diagnose bearing defects even amidst transient disturbances.

articleTitle: A New Incremental Remaining Useful Life Prediction Framework Based on Online Knowledge Distillation and Stochastic Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction in practical engineers usually has the following challenges: (1) the RUL prediction with sequentially-collected online data easily suffers from varying working conditions with no historically-accumulated whole-life data available, (2) degradation randomness, as well as noise interference, will unavoidably result in the accumulation of prognostic error. To address these problems, this paper introduces stochastic process model and proposes an incremental RUL prediction framework based on online knowledge distillation. Using offline whole-life data and early part of online degradation data, the teacher model is first initialized by means of time series recursive prediction. For each online data block that sequentially arrives, the soft-labels are calculated by the teacher model, while the pseudo-labels are further determined by a Bayesian updated Wiener process model. By minimizing the loss between the student model's output and these two kinds of labels, an online knowledge distillation is realized for the incremental RUL prediction. A set of experiments is conducted on the two widely-used bearing datasets IEEE PHM Challenge 2012 and XJTU-SY. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can periodically update the prediction model and then obtain accurate prediction results on sequentially-collected online data, which offers a feasible solution to actual prognostic tasks.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Few Sample Rolling Bearings Based on SE Attention and Similarity Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning has demonstrated excellent performance in the diagnosis of rolling bearing faults due to its outstanding feature extraction capabilities. However, when faced with limited small sample datasets, this technique still faces challenges in feature learning and fault type discrimination. This study proposes a new learning framework, namely the SE Attention based similarity comparison method. In this framework, we extract features from scarce samples through an encoder, and then use the similarity and difference between labeled samples to construct positive and negative sample pairs. The encoder further extracts features with the assistance of contrastive learning, and then completes fault classification through a classifier. In addition, we introduced the SE Attention mechanism to enhance the efficiency of feature extraction. This framework significantly reduces the manpower and time required for annotating samples. Experimental results have shown that the bearing fault diagnosis model proposed in this study has high accuracy and effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Metric Learning-based Health Indicator for Early Degradation Point Detection of Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The construction of a reasonable health indicator (HI) to describe the degradation process of equipment and identify the early degradation point (EDP) is the focus of machines condition monitoring. However, HIs based on manual feature extraction rely on prior knowledge. Moreover, most of the methods with good trendability are not sensitive to early fault of machines due to the presence of strong noise. To address above problems, a HI construction method based on metric learning is proposed for identifying EDPs of machines. Firstly, a triplet network stacked with residual-attention (RA) block is constructed and optimized by genetic algorithm (GA) for feature extraction. Then, triplet loss is used to promote intra-class aggregation and inter-class separation for EDP detection. After that, convex optimization (CO) is applied to assign corresponding weights to the features for optimizing the trendability of the degradation process. Finally, the weighted relative similarity between two samples is calculated as the GA-RA-CO-HI of machines. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified on two benchmarks. The results show that the proposed GA-RA-CO-HI can effectively detect EDP while promising desirable trendability and monotonicity.

articleTitle: Integrating IoT and Predictive Analytics for Remote Asset Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The rapid evolution of the Internet of Things (IoT) has transformed industrial asset management by enabling continuous monitoring and predictive maintenance of critical infrastructure systems. However, existing IoT solutions often require integrating multiple systems, leading to challenges in data compatibility, system interoperability, and management complexity. This paper presents Sentinel Motion, an IoT -enabled technology developed by Ridgetop Group, designed to address these challenges through a comprehensive, integrated solution for asset health monitoring. Aligned with the IEEE 1856–2017 PHM Standard, Sentinel Motion combines smart sensors, data management tools, and advanced software platforms to enhance asset reliability across various industries. The paper explores its applications in sectors such as railroads and introduces the integration of Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors for structural health monitoring, further extending the capabilities of IoT in industrial maintenance.

articleTitle: Compound Faults Diagnosis in Wind Turbine Gearbox Based on Deep Learning Methods: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Wind turbines play an important role in capturing energy from wind. However, they are prone to failure because they are exposed to harsh conditions in operation. As an important component of the wind turbine, the health of gearbox in the power drivetrain system is particularly critical to the safe operation of the wind turbine. Traditional fault diagnosis methods, such as vibration analysis and temperature monitoring, are difficult to handle effectively compound faults. In recent years, artificial intelligence techniques have been increasingly used in the field of fault diagnosis, and deep learning methods have shown great advantages and potential in this field. This paper explores recent research progress in deep learning-based compound faults diagnosis methods for wind turbine gearboxes. The advantages and limitations of convolutional neural network (CNN), deep belief network (DBN), autoencoder (AE) and recurrent neural network (RNN) in gearbox compound faults diagnosis are discussed. These methods demonstrate that deep learning-based methods can significantly improve fault diagnosis performance, especially in noisy and complex data environments. Future research prospects are summarized which encompass the interpretability of algorithms, complex fault modeling, and advanced signal processing for further advancing intelligent fault diagnosis of wind turbine gearboxes.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis with Imbalance Dataset Based on Modified Bilateral-Branch Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The classical intelligent diagnosis methods based on deep learning generally require huge amount of labeled data with balanced samples among classes to train the model. However, for rolling bearing dataset in engineering scenarios, samples in normal condition occupy the vast majority of runtime data, while fault samples account for only a small fraction. The bilateral-branch networks (BBN) can effectively improve the recognition performance for the imbalance long-tailed dataset. This paper proposes a framework of modified BBN for bearing fault diagnosis with imbalance dataset, which aims to further enhance the diagnostic performance. Specifically, the modified BBN improves the diagnostic performance of imbalance tasks in three aspects. First, instance-class sampling strategy is adopted in the rebalancing branch to balance the attention of feature extraction among the imbalance classes. Second, parabolic increment curve is selected for the trend of trade-off parameter in the cumulative learning to alleviate the distribution distortion of the learned features. Third, τ-normalization is introduced for the trained classifier to further rebalance the classification among the imbalance classes via moving the decision boundaries. Experiments on a bearing dataset validate that the modified BBN proposed is superior to the existing methods, especially on extremely imbalance tasks.

articleTitle: Combining Fourier-Based Channel Attention with TCN and Informer for Railway Accident Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The rapid expansion of railway networks and technological advancements has introduced significant challenges in ensuring railway safety. To address the critical need for effective prediction and prevention mechanisms, this paper proposes the FCAM-TCN-DSInformer model, a novel approach to railway accident prediction. The model integrates the Fourier-based Channel Attention Mechanism (FCAM), Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), and De-stationary Informer (DSInformer) to capture both temporal and spectral features from time series data effectively. Extensive experiments and ablation studies were conducted to validate the model's performance. The results demonstrate that the FCAM-TCN-DSInformer model significantly outperforms both traditional and advanced models, including ARIMA, LSTM, GRU, Transformer, Autoformer, and FEDformer by achieving the highest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{{2}}$</tex> score and substantial reductions in error metrics such as RMSE, MAE, and MAPE. These improvements confirm the model's accuracy and robustness, making it a powerful tool for railway safety management. Moreover, the model's adaptability to different univariate time series datasets, such as the Daily Minimum Temperatures Dataset and the US Births Dataset, highlights its strong generalization capabilities. Future work will focus on optimizing the model for real-time predictions and expanding its application to multi-step prediction tasks, thereby fully realizing its potential across diverse forecasting contexts.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation Metrics of PHM: A Review from Different Perspectives of Metrics System Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) is a multidisciplinary technology essential for enhancing equipment reliability and operational efficiency across various industries. In the past decade, numerous researchers have proposed various metrics to measure the performance of PHM systems. This paper reviews PHM performance evaluation metrics from different perspectives of constructing a metrics system: function-based, component-based, and end-user-based. From a function-based perspective, we categorize the metrics affecting the comprehensive performance of PHM systems into three main dimensions: diagnosis, prognosis, and decision-making, and secondary dimensions such as computational performance, human-computer interaction, and cost-benefit. The majority of the performance evaluation metrics from the three main dimensions are summarized and presented. We anticipate this review work to guide PHM practitioners in selecting appropriate metrics during system design and development, fostering more reliable and user-centric PHM solutions.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis of Resistance Parachute Lock Mechanism in Complex Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The drag parachute locking system is an important part of the aircraft takeoff and landing system. The reliability of the system directly affects the safe landing of the airplane. This paper combines the typical use environment of a certain type of aircraft, and carries out the investigation of the functional reliability of the mechanism under the action of the complex environment. The failure mechanisms of hinge thermal expansion and creep relaxation of steel cable are considered. The influencing factors are parameterized in the dynamic simulation and numerically simulated under the stochastic principle. Functional data of the drag parachute locking mechanism are obtained under consideration of time evolution. The reliability and kinematic performance of the locking mechanism in complex environments are evaluated.

articleTitle: Improved Physics-Guided PINN Design and its Application in Bearing Acceleration Response Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In engineering, dynamic and fault modeling is crucial for predicting system behavior and diagnosing faults to ensure reliable and efficient operation. Recently, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have gained significant attention and demonstrated great potential in modeling applications. However, general PINNs (G-PINNs) are not well-suited for long-period simulations, and embedding complex dynamic equations can be challenging, leading to difficulties in training. This paper proposes an improved physics-guided PINN (IP-PINN) approach to address these issues. The method utilizes three key techniques: frequency domain loss function, transfer learning, and sine activation function. To demonstrate the advantages of the IP-PINN approach, the acceleration responses of bearings with outer race fault, inner race fault, and ball fault are modeled and compared with simulation data. The results show that the IP-PINN method provides accurate solutions even for long-duration simulations. Additionally, analyzing the impact of different weights for the frequency domain loss and activation functions allows for the selection of suitable parameters for various fault types. This approach addresses the limitations of G-PINNs and offers a novel method for bearing fault signal modeling.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis with Both Health Condition Label Scarsity and Rotating Speed Variations
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD) can significantly reduce the workload of operators, and has important research value and engineering application significance. Existing intelligent diagnostic algorithms still require a large amount of labeled data for training. Self-supervised learning utilizes unlabeled data to automatically learn its intrinsic structure, which can significantly reduce the demand for labeled data in IFD. Therefore, this article conducts research on IFD algorithms that effectively utilize unlabeled monitoring data based on self-supervised learning. Firstly, a self-supervised learning method based on vibration signal time-frequency graph is constructed, and two new data augmentation methods are introduced to assist in self-supervised network training, learning valuable representations for downstream diagnosis tasks. Afterwards, based on the self-supervised learning network, global fine-tuning is performed with a small amount of labeled data to achieve the construction of a diagnostic network. Finally, validations were conducted based on the bearing fault dataset of the multi-stage transmission experimental platform. Extensive experiments have shown that the self-supervised learning based network can hold performance with only a small amount of labeled fault data. The research content of this article will provide some reference for the effective utilization of unlabeled monitoring data in real-life applications.

articleTitle: Unbalanced Few-Sample Fault Diagnosis Approach for Mechanical Equipment Based on Multi-Scale Class-Weighted Balanced Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Mechanical equipment operating in extreme environments is prone to damage critical components, thus affecting its performance and remaining service life, which leads mechanical equipment diagnosis to be a focus. Data-driven fault diagnosis approaches have been recognized as the emerging research directions. However, they are limited by the fact that only few-sample unbalanced datasets can be applied in real industrial backgrounds, leading to serious overfitting and performance degradation. Therefore, an unbalanced few-sample fault diagnosis approach for mechanical equipment based on multi-scale class-weighted balanced network is proposed to improve the diagnosis performance by gradually resolving the quantitative and qualitative imbalance among classes. In the feature extraction stage, multi-scale feature fusion convolution module and channel class balancing mechanism are designed to enhance the ability of recognizing few classes. In the network optimization stage, the quantitative imbalance among classes and the accuracy imbalance within classes are firstly calculated to weight the cross-entropy loss, and then the triplet loss in metric learning is added, making it possible to ignore the quantitative and qualitative imbalance and guide the network to efficiently learn the features of all the classes. Experiments are conducted on the Case Western Reserve University bearing dataset to validate the effectiveness. The results show that even under the most extreme unbalanced few-sample condition, the average fault diagnosis accuracies of the proposed approach under all operating conditions are still above 94%, which are better than comparison approaches.

articleTitle: Comparison of Feature and Information Fusion Health Indexes in Railway Balise Health Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the development of dynamic detection technology, the amount of data related to railway ground equipment has grown significantly. To make full use of this data, researchers have proposed various health state assessment techniques that are crucial for intelligent maintenance and health management. This paper introduces a novel balise health state assessment method that integrates multiple feature information to evaluate the health status of condition features that lack standard test criteria. Additionally, a differential information fusion method based on Dempster-Shafer (D-S) evidence theory is applied to combine different health indices. The proposed method is validated through comparative analyses of single and multiple degradation scenarios of key components, demonstrating its effectiveness and applicability in diverse scenarios for comprehensive health assessment.

articleTitle: Resource-Constrained Dynamic Kernel Density Estimation for Data Streams Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the rapid development of monitoring system and sensor technology, a large amount of data streams that continuously arrive with intensive data traffic have been generated in various fields. Anomaly detection is the core part of identifying the state changes of monitored objects. Considering that monitoring data streams is constantly generated in real time and not suitable for ex-post analysis, an anomaly detection method for data streams based on kernel density estimation is proposed to deal with the situation of limited computing resources. The method consists of dynamic kernel density estimation and dynamic threshold setting. In the dynamic kernel density estimation, a fusion mechanism for new data points based on the minimum distance constraint is established, and a merge strategy for buffer kernel functions based on the minimal spatial angle criterion is designed to realize the real-time probability density estimation of data streams under the limitations of storage and computation resources. In the dynamic threshold setting, the probability distribution fine-tuning strategy is adopted to update the initial thresholds online after the arrival of new data points. In view of the concept drift of data distribution, the increment and deletion strategy of the thresholds is set. In order to verify the validity of the method, simulation data, NAB standard data and industrial data were selected for analysis. The results show that the method can effectively and accurately perform online anomaly detection on large-scale data streams.

articleTitle: Probabilistic RUL Prediction Based on Nonlinear Wiener Process and Monte Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is the core of intelligent operation and maintenance, improving operation and maintenance efficiency and reducing maintenance costs. Aiming at the limitations of RUL prediction methods based on mathematical derivation in terms of adaptability and flexibility, this paper proposes a probabilistic RUL simulation method for complex systems or complex degradation processes. The method constructs a degradation model using a complex nonlinear Wiener process, estimates the model parameters using maximum likelihood estimation, and updates the stochastic parameters based on the Bayesian updating strategy. On this basis, the prediction of probabilistic RUL is realized by the simulation algorithm. Compared with the mathematical derivation method, the prediction of the method proposed in this paper is accurate, which verifies the effectiveness and practicality of the simulation method. In a complex system or complex degradation process, the method in this paper can construct the probabilistic RUL prediction model faster.

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling Method of Piezoelectric Ceramic Materials Under High Temperature and Radiation Coupling Field
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Nuclear power is an important source of clean energy, and has been developing rapidly around the world in recent years. The safe, reliable and stable operation of nuclear power plants is the top priority of nuclear power development. High-temperature radiation-resistant piezoelectric sensors are important components for the implementation of health status assessment and prediction of key reactor equipment. Therefore, ensuring the high reliability of high-temperature radiation-resistant piezoelectric sensors is the key to accurately, reliably, and timely grasp the health status of key reactor equipment. However, the research in the reliability of piezoelectric sensors under high-temperature and radiation coupling field is lack, and it is difficult to grasp the performance changes of piezoelectric sensors under the coupling field. In order to solve the above problems, this paper studied the reliability modeling method of piezoelectric ceramic materials under high temperature and radiation coupling field, mainly focusing on several aspects including the calculation of piezoelectric ceramic materials, structural model, molecular dynamics model, acquisition of piezoelectric parameters, irradiation model and parameter setting. Finally, the reliability modeling of piezoelectric ceramic materials under coupled fields is realized. The results provide theoretical support for the reliability study of piezoelectric ceramic materials under high temperature and radiation coupling field.

articleTitle: Damage Identification of Thermal Protection Tiles Based on an Optimizable SVM Algorithm and Temperature Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: During the service of reusable launch vehicles, thermal protection tiles are easily damaged, which in turn threatens flight safety. However, monitoring the back wall temperature of thermal protection tiles can reflect their damage status. Based on this principle, combined with machine learning methods, we proposed a thermal protection tile damage identification method based on an optimizable SVM algorithm and temperature monitoring. The method is verified by the bottom temperature data of the thermal protection tile collected from ground simulation tests. Results show that the optimizable SVM algorithm can quickly identify various types of thermal protection tile damage, with an identification accuracy of up to 98.44%. This work lays a foundation for further development of thermal protection structure health monitoring and management system.

articleTitle: TADmobileNet: A More Reliable Automatic Modulation Classification Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) is a technique that detects the modulation information of the received signal prior to demodulation and plays an important role in non-cooperative communication. However, AMC performs poorly at low signal-to-noise ratios. The Threshold Automatic Decoder Noise Reducer (TAD) architecture is designed to adaptively remove noise from the signal. The MobileNetV3 model incorporates an attentional mechanism and uses depth-separated convolution, resulting in a significant reduction of the model parameters and dramatically shorter prediction times, making deployment on mobile devices possible. In this paper, we synthesize the advantages of MobileNetV3 and TAD to develop the TADmobileNet model for automatic modulation classification. Experimental results show that our model improves the classification accuracy by 3% under low SNR conditions compared to MobileNetV3, which enhances the robustness and reliability of the model. Moreover, TADmobileNet achieves an average accuracy of 62% on the RML2016.10A dataset. The accuracy consistently exceeds 90% when the signal-to-noise ratio exceeds 0 dB. In addition, this paper explores the impact of signal preprocessing techniques such as data augmentation, L2 regularization, and truncation migration on the performance of the TADmobileNet model.

articleTitle: An Improved Variational Autoencoder-Based Anomaly Detection Model for Rolling Bearing
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In practical industrial scenarios, engineering equipment typically operates under normal monitoring conditions, where acquired signals lack fault data. Moreover, it is difficult to extract the fault features of the nonlinear vibration signal obtained by the sensor and the calculation cost is high. In response to this challenge, this work introduces an anomaly detection method based on a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) improved with the assistance of a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN). This proposed method introduces adversarial generation ideas into the VAE framework and uses only normal bearing samples during training to establish an anomaly score threshold. By setting an anomaly status threshold, the method effectively determines whether a bearing has developed a fault. The accuracy of this method is further verified through practical applications and validation on the publicly available XJTU-SY bearing dataset. Comparative analyses are conducted using three metrics: early fault detection location, false alarms, and missed detections to evaluate the performance of the anomaly status detection. The experiments demonstrate that the VAE-GAN outperforms traditional data-driven algorithms in terms of early fault detection performance.

articleTitle: Independent Reliable High-Speed Sampling for Oil & Gas Drilling and Exploration System
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The reliable data sampling and collection system in Oil &Gas Drilling and Exploration System includes a data acquirer installed in the measurement while drilling system to transmit a sampling collector identification signal to one of a plurality of sampling collectors coupled to the data acquirer. Each sampling collector includes a sensor and a plurality of RAM pages to store sensor data received from the sensor. When one of the sampling collectors receives the enable signal from the data acquirer, a current RAM page currently receiving sensor data from the sensor continues to receive sensor data without interruption and an immediately preceding RAM page storing a last completed page of received sensor data is transmitted from the one sampling collector to a memory of the data acquirer and from there to a surface computing system. As such, recent data is retrieved and transmitted for processing without interrupting the continuous collection of sensor data. The reliability of data acquisition is very crucial of the Oil &Gas Drilling and Exploration operation.

articleTitle: A Novel Temporal Distribution Matching-Based Transfer Learning Method for State of Health Estimation of Li-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Accurate evaluation of the state of health (SOH) is crucial for ensuring the safe functioning of lithium-ion batteries and maximizing their potential for usage and optimization. The deep learning-based approach to assessing the SOH of lithium-ion batteries has difficulties in attaining strong generalization across many domains due to the wide range of battery types and usage conditions, as well as the high cost of collecting battery data. To address this problem, this paper proposes a temporal distribution matching-based transfer learning approach to enhance the temporal generalization ability on the basis of parameter transfer and feature transfer. First, multi-dimensional features are retrieved, and the feature expression score (FES) is computed using the gray relational analysis (GRA). The task with the greatest FES is chosen as the base model for transfer learning. During the transfer learning phase, the initial 25% of the target dataset is utilized to refine the base model. Simultaneously, temporal distribution matching is performed to improve temporal feature alignment by taking into account the output of each hidden state in the temporal network. The accuracy and robustness of the proposed model are effectively demonstrated through experiments done on two datasets. Our solution outperforms previous transfer learning algorithms in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Bearing Domain Adversarial Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Wasserstein Distance Driven by Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: When solving the problems of data scarcity and cross-domain adaptability in bearing fault diagnosis, traditional methods often find it difficult to obtain a large amount of fault data, which limits the application and development of data-driven methods. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel domain adversarial fault diagnosis method driven by digital twins. First, by constructing a dynamic simulation model of bearing faults, the vibration signals of bearing faults are successfully simulated, thereby obtaining rich simulated fault data. Secondly, by using the SAE network and Wasserstein distance transfer strategy, the fault diagnosis knowledge is automatically learned from the simulated time domain signals, and this knowledge is successfully transfer to the diagnosis problems under different working conditions. Finally, by introducing the domain adversarial mechanism and gradient reversal layer (GRL), the transfer of target domain data features to source domain data features is realized. At the same time, the accurate classification of fault features and the adaptation of domain distribution are realized in the feature extraction process, which effectively solves the domain offset problem in cross-domain fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Outlier Detection via SVDD with Mixed Kernel in Distributed Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In this study, a strategy for denoising nonstationary signals and detecting outliers is proposed for distributed fiber optic sensors (DFOS). Bi-dimensional Empirical mode decomposition adaptively decomposes bi-dimensional detection signals with nonlinear attenuation into multiple intrinsic mode functions to suppress confusion of noise and outliers. The unsupervised learning method, Support Vector Data Description (SVDD), is employed for classification. SVDD excels in handling imbalanced samples by converting them into outliers, thereby designing an optimal separation hypersphere with the smallest volume. This feature is particularly advantageous in unsupervised scenarios where labeled data is scarce or unavailable, as it allows for robust outlier detection without the need for prior knowledge. A calculation module integrates classification outputs to obtain the location of high-speed trains. Finally, an experiment is conducted based on the basis of the data collected from a high-speed line in China. Results validate the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: A Weighted Multi-Scale Global-Local Feature Fusion Framework for Cross-Turbine Diagnosis of Wind Turbine Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Data-driven approaches for diagnosing wind turbine faults have gained significant popularity, particularly due to the promising diagnostic performance of deep learning models. However, training fault diagnosis models for every wind turbine is both time-intensive and resource-demanding. Therefore, for wind turbines with limited data or applications with limited computational resources, transfer learning becomes crucial. To tackle these challenges, we propose a weighted multi-scale global-local feature fusion network (WMGLFFN) framework, which is comprised of two parts. The first part utilizes multi-scale wavelets and a spatio-temporal convolutional neural network to learn global and local features. The second part is a multi-task learning module, which learns invariant features for different turbine domains using a dynamically weighted domain adversarial network. Meanwhile, in order to enhance the feature discrimination ability, we introduce deep metric learning. We used four existing networks to compare with the proposed method and validated it with SCADA data from two wind turbines. Our WMGLFFN significantly outperformed traditional deep learning methods. The cross-validation experiments performed on two turbines prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A New Algorithm Based on Adaptive SSD-TET and Its Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: A signal processing method combining adaptive Singular Spectrum Decomposition (SSD) with Transient Extracting Transform (TET) is proposed to address the challenge of weak energy in early rolling bearing fault signals, which complicates fault classification based on time-frequency information. Initially, the optimal decomposition level for the SSD algorithm is determined using the instantaneous frequency mean method, and the original signal is decomposed into the corresponding singular spectral components. These components are then reconstructed based on the maximum kurtosis criterion, and transient feature extraction is performed to produce time-frequency maps that highlight concentrated fault information. Finally, fault classification is carried out using the C4.5 decision tree. Results demonstrate that the adaptive SSD-TET algorithm effectively extracts transient features of rolling bearing faults, shows greater noise robustness, and provides clearer time-frequency maps, improving fault diagnosis. In comparative tests, the adaptive SSD-TET algorithm achieved a diagnostic rate of 98.3% for various fault types, showing significant advantages over traditional methods.

articleTitle: Health Monitoring and Performance Degradation Prediction of Large-Size and Wide-Tooth Milling Machine Blades
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The disc milling cutter is the key moving part in the milling process of large-size and wide-tooth milling machine, which determines the machining accuracy and quality of the gear surface. Contact and collision between the blade and the gear surface leads to gradual dulling of the blades, affecting the accuracy of the tooth surface. The monitoring of blades during continuous machining has been a hot and difficult research topic. In this paper, a method for blade health state assessment and performance degradation trend prediction based on semi-supervised convolutional ladder network (SSCLN) with maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) is proposed. Wavelet packets are used to decompose the original vibration signals, from which the reconstructed vibration signals are computed to obtain the RMS thresholds for blade failure, and based on the results, the training and testing sample set labels are constructed. This approach solves the problem of indirect monitoring of blades, where health degradation labels cannot be obtained under continuous non-stop operation. The large, wide-toothed, disc-shaped gear milling machine tool manufactured by our team was used to practical process large inner-ring gear workpieces to obtain a sample dataset, which verifies the superiority of the methodology proposed in this paper. The obtained health assessment indicator has a better trend relative to the common indicators, and the predicted health degradation labels and remaining useful life (RUL) results are more accurate, which suggests that the method has practical application.

articleTitle: Wafer map Anomaly Detection Driven by Contrast Learning and Vision Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the rapid development of the integrated circuit industry, wafers, as the carrier for chip manufacturing, have made their production efficiency and quality the focal point of industry attention. Therefore, timely anomaly detection on wafer maps holds significant importance. Wafer maps provide a visual representation of the test results of each die on the wafer and effectively present data along with its associated spatial information. Timely anomaly detection on these maps is crucial for enhancing product quality and production efficiency. This paper introduces an anomaly detection method for wafer maps that leverages the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture and a contrastive learning mechanism. The ViT architecture is employed to deeply model the global information of wafer maps, followed by the use of a contrastive learning mechanism to capture key features that reflect healthy information in samples of healthy wafer maps. This method not only achieves leading performance but also demonstrates robust resilience under noisy and sample contamination conditions. This achievement provides strong support for the practical application of anomaly detection in wafer maps.

articleTitle: Physical Spatial-Temporal Weighted Graph Construction for FTU's Health Condition Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To ensure the dependable operation of hydropower generation, substantial research efforts have been dedicated to the health condition assessment (HCA) of Francis turbine units (FTUs). Typical HCA strategies encompass the creation of health benchmark model (HBM) and the calculation of performance degradation indicators (PDIs). However, Previous investigations have primarily concentrated on either the temporal or spatial relationships within pulsation signals and working condition parameters, ignoring the complex interactions between these relationships. In addition, a simplistic averaging of temporal and spatial relationships can lead to the loss of critical information. This paper proposes a physical spatial-temporal weighted graph construction for the health condition assessment of FTUs. Initially, a simulation model of the FTUs is developed, utilizing computational fluid dynamics theories to produce simulated pulsation signals. Then, actual pulsation signals are used to refine the simulation model, achieving a high-fidelity representation. Subsequently, the pulsation signals are modeled using graph data to capture both physical spatial relationships and essential features. On this basis, time-related statistical parameters are employed to allocate weights to each identified relationship. Furthermore, the integration of the feature relationships with physical spatial relationships leads to the creation of a physical spatial-temporal weighted graph, enhancing its signal representation capability. Ultimately, this graph is fed into the graph convolutional model to obtain HBM. To assess the performance, the PDI is calculated by extracting the Euclidean distance between the comprehensive features derived from the HBM-predicted labels and the actual signals observed in the degraded state. Validation experiment is conducted to verify the effectiveness of proposed method through the utilization of real-time monitoring data and working condition parameters from the FTU deployed within the hydropower station.

articleTitle: A Fault Tracing Method Based on Knowledge Graph and Weighted Path Ranking Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The structure of railway systems is complex, and accurately and rapidly identifying the root cause of faults post-occurrence is an emerging challenge in the industry. However, railway fault tracing mainly relies on manual experience and traditional data analysis techniques, with most tracing methods suffering from low efficiency and insufficient accuracy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a railway safety equipment fault tracing method based on knowledge graphs and weighted path ranking algorithm. The approach integrates knowledge graphs with Bayesian networks, attention mechanisms, and graph computation, utilizing a weighted calculation to run the weighted path ranking algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves excellent tracing performance in the field of railway equipment.

articleTitle: A New Health Indicator Based on the Energy and Distribution of Frequency Domain Fault Information for Rolling Bearing Condition Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Health condition monitoring of rolling bearings is of significance to ensure the safety and reliability of modern industry, which depends on a robust health indicator (HI). However, most existing HIs still struggle with accurate incipient fault detection and monotonic degradation assessment. To address this issue, a new HI based on the energy and distribution of frequency domain fault information (EDFF-HI) is proposed. Firstly, the improved clustering envelope spectrum (ICES) that developed from the recently proposed clustering weighted envelope spectrum (CWES) is used to identify the frequency-domain fault information. Through the ICES algorithm, the informative spectral frequency slices (SFSs) in the spectral coherence (SCoh) can be identified, and the potential fault characteristic frequencies (PFCFs) of each SFS can also be determined, which is also called its label. Secondly, the signal-noise ratio of each informative SFS is calculated according to its label to reflect the fault energy. Meanwhile, the sum of the signal-noise ratio of all informative SFSs is calculated to construct the HI, which considers the fault information distribution. To further enhance the performance of HI, the square root operation and moving average algorithm are introduced to obtain the final HI. This method only requires a rough estimate of FCFs rather than accurate values. Two bearing run-to-failure datasets are used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed HI. The results indicate that the proposed EDFF-HI can detect incipient faults earlier, and the incipient fault sensitivity (IFS) index is usually more than 1.5 times that of other popular HIs.

articleTitle: A Multi-Granularity Voiceprint Feature Adaptive Extraction Method for Rotating Machinery Based on Multi-Spectrogram Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Aiming at the difficulty of extracting low-frequency features and incomplete voiceprint features in the strong noise environment in rotating machinery fault recognition, this paper proposes a multi-granularity voiceprint feature adaptive extraction (MG-FAE) method for rotating machinery based on multi-spectrogram fusion. Firstly, the space-spectrogram joint feature set based on the nonlinear mapping advantages of Mel spectrum and mel frequency cepstrum coefficients (MFCCs) is constructed to improves the voiceprint feature representation capability of low-frequency signals. Then, the multi-granularity representation method of multi-spectrogram based on Gaussian Difference Pyramid (GDP) is proposed to fully characterize the geometric and semantic information in spectrogram, the Multi-Head Attention Mechanism (MHA) is introduced to adaptively extract multiple voiceprint features to achieve comprehensive representation. Finally, a MG-FAE method is proposed to representat the voiceprint features of rotating machinery. The effectiveness of the method is verified by iFL YTEK rotating machinery challenge dataset. The recognition rate is 97.64% in multi noise state, which is 37.36% higher than the original audio signal. Moreover, the t-SNE feature visualization technology verifies that the MG-FAE method proposed in this paper has clear boundary of voiceprint feature classification and good verification effect.

articleTitle: Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Integrated Features of Vibration Signals and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of traditional time-frequency domain feature extraction methods in effectively capturing key information, this paper employs the energy values obtained through wavelet packet decomposition (WPD), along with the correlation dimension, to form the integrated features. An innovative fault diagnosis approach for rolling bearings is introduced, leveraging integrated features and employing support vector machine (SVM) for classification. Firstly, the original signal is decomposed using WPD, and then the energy features of the resulting frequency bands are calculated. The chaotic features embedded in the vibration signals are characterized by the correlation dimension, computed using the Grassberger-Procaccia (GP) algorithm. Subsequently, the energy features and the correlation dimension are combined to form the integrated features. To address the challenges of the traditional SVM model, which can often succumb to local optima and overfitting during classification, a novel approach utilizing Bayesian optimization for SVM parameter tuning is introduced. The method first constructs integrated features through calculation and then inputs these feature vectors into an SVM optimized using the Bayesian algorithm to achieve fault diagnosis. The method was tested on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) dataset, achieving a prediction accuracy of 97.8%. The experimental results confirm the practicality of the method proposed in this paper, and at the same time open up a new path for rolling bearing fault diagnosis within the field of underwater equipment.

articleTitle: Spatio-Temporal Information Fusion with Graph Neural Networks for Aero-Engine Remaining Useful Life Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Aircraft engines, as highly complex thermodynamic composite power systems, are subject to extreme operating conditions that render them vulnerable to failures, such as fatigue. Predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of these engines allows for the implementation of more precise predictive maintenance strategies, which can significantly reduce the risk of unexpected failures and the potential losses they may incur. Most data-driven methods primarily rely on extracting temporal feature information to construct mappings, often neglecting the inter-sensory correlation within the data samples. To address this, we introduce a graph neural network combined with attention mechanism for predicting RUL of aircraft engines. By modeling data samples as spatiotemporal graph data and integrating this information, our method fully exploits the historical degradation data of aircraft engines for predictive purposes. Ultimately, by conducting experiments on the C-MAPSS dataset and comparing our method with other data-driven approaches, we have demonstrated that our proposed method can more accurately and effectively fulfill the task of lifespan prediction.

articleTitle: Research on Aircraft System Anomaly Detection Method Based on MHAVGAE Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of aircraft systems, there are different degrees of correlation in monitoring aircraft systems, which brings great challenges to anomaly detection in complex systems. In this paper, the method of anomaly detection for complex aircraft systems is studied, and an anomaly detection model based on variational graph autoencoder considering multi-variable coupling is established. Firstly, the detrended correlation quantification system is used to monitor the coupling relationship between variables, and the coupling relationship network is constructed. Secondly, the multi-head attention mechanism is introduced into the variogram autoencoder anomaly detection model to fully extract the hidden features of the network nodes, and quantitatively analyze the changes of the coupling relationship network during the operation of the aircraft system to accurately characterize the system health state. The reconstruction probability is taken as the evaluation index of system running state, and the threshold value of fault warning is determined by the criterion of Gauss distribution theory to realize the timely detection of system anomalies.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation: A Residual Attention Network for Gear Pump Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To ensure the reliability of products, deep learning-based fault diagnosis methods have received extensive attention in academic research and industry. These methods usually have two default assumptions: (1) a large number of labeled training samples, and (2) training and test data share similar distributions under constant operating conditions. Therefore, we propose a multi-kernel domain adaptation method based on residual network with transfer attention mechanism (ResNetTAM-MKDA) to solve the problem that the distribution difference between target domain data and source domain data in unknown conditions affects the model performance, and there is no labeled data in the target domain. First, we utilize to extract shallow features in the source and target domains and feed them into a stacked residual convolution module to learn higher-order generic fault information. Then, the higher-order fault features with higher transferability are weighted using the Migratable Attention Module, and the domain alignment is achieved using a multi-core domain adaptation method. Finally, the fault diagnosis classification module constructed using fully connected networks is used to map the higher-order fault features into fault labels. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, we simulate the gear pump contamination wear experiment to get the failure data under different working conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified in the six diagnostic tasks set up.

articleTitle: A Selective Convolution Kernel Residual Network for Wafer Map Defect Pattern Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The fabrication of wafers represents a pivotal stage in the production of semiconductors. Defects that emerge during the fabrication process have the potential to result in the production of faulty wafers, which in turn can impact the overall yield of the final product. The analysis of wafer map defect patterns can facilitate the identification of the root cause of defects, thereby enhancing the overall yield of wafers produced. However, the presence of wafer map defects presents a number of challenges, including diversity in location, variability in defect pattern, and size inhomogeneity. Moreover, the current Wafer Map Defect Pattern Recognition (WMDPR) classification algorithm displays shortcomings in terms of accuracy. A Selective Convolution Kernel Residual Network (SCKR-Net) incorporating an Attention Mechanism (Convolutional Block Attention Module, CBAM) is proposed as a solution to the aforementioned problem. The proposed approach employs a Selective Convolution Kernel (SCK) structure, which is capable of adaptively adjusting its parameters and convolution kernel size in response to the varying dimensions of wafer map defects. This adaptability enhances the network's capacity to process complex and variable data. To ascertain the efficacy of the proposed methodology, experiments were conducted on the Mixed-WM38 dataset. The results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits a markedly superior recognition performance compared to alternative models.

articleTitle: A Review of Fault Diagnosis and Remaining Useful Life Prediction of High-Speed Train Bearings
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the rapid expansion of China's high-speed railway network, the safety and dependability of train bearings, as vital components, are critical to the overall stability of the transportation system. This paper overviews the most recent developments in train bearing remaining useful life (RUL) prediction and fault diagnosis research. First, the significance of train bearings and the state of China's high-speed rail system are discussed. The structural properties of train bearings and failure modes are then thoroughly examined. The vibration signal-based fault diagnostic approaches covered in this study include both conventional signal analysis techniques and intelligent approaches like deep learning and machine learning. Furthermore, train bearing RUL prediction strategies are examined, including physical model-based, data-driven, and hybrid models. Finally, the paper discusses the challenges that current research faces, such as the limitations of data quality and quantity, the explain ability of deep learning models, the complexity of fault diagnosis, and RUL prediction under variable operating conditions, and looks to the future. This study intends to give scientific basis and technical support for fault detection and RUL prediction of train bearings in rail transit by conducting an in-depth review of present technologies and discussing future difficulties.

articleTitle: A Faster Neural Network for High-speed Railroad Environment Safety Hazard Segmentation and Risk Evaluation Using UAV Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Environmental safety hazards along the high-speed railroad (e.g. rubbish, plastic tarps, and temporary dwellings) will threaten the safety operation of train. However, existing deep learning-based approaches are constrained by scale-significance differences in safety hazards and limited semantic information, as well as inadequate risk evaluation of hazard instances. This paper proposes a faster neural network named FRESeg for environment safety hazard segmentation and risk evaluation using UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) imagery. Firstly, a novel cross stage partial connection module integrating partial convolution is developed and assembled into the FRESeg for mining rich feature information while keeping a low latency. Second, an image-to-real-world mapping model taking advantage of key UAV parameters (such as, flight altitude, lens focal length, etc.) is also integrated in the FRESeg for more complete estimation of risk distance and area. Finally, the comprehensive experiment results utilizing the complex UAV high-speed railroad dataset show that proposed method acquires a faster inference speed yet maintains a higher detection rate.

articleTitle: MCSA-Based Fault Indicator and a Log Likelihood Algorithm to Estimate the Severity of Bearing Faults in Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In this paper, a novel methodology for the quantitative diagnosis of bearings is proposed using measurements. The signature have a low dominance in the current spectrum as observed in the measurements. This demands a newer methodology to quantify the signature and correlate it to the severity of the bearing fault. The signal processing technique is developed which quantifies the sensitive frequency band in the spectrum using conventional parameters. A new parameter, named modified sparsity, is introduced which reduces the impact of higher noise levels in the frequency domain. This parameter evaluates the gain factor based on the strength of the peak occurrence and is used to correct the bias induced by the noise floor. Then, a control chart is applied to reduce the variability of the response, revealing the underlying trend. Finally, a data-based likelihood and log-likelihood approach is used to map the health indicator to a more physical parameter (displacement associated with one of the faulty bearings) so that the outcome of the health indicator is more meaningful to the user. The overall idea is to prevent interference from other sources towards the signatures while quantification and give more physical meaning to the severity based on the measurements.

articleTitle: Domain Adversarial Transfer Learning for Fault Diagnosis of Rotating Parts in Cross Working Condition Injection Molding Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In response to the problem of decreased accuracy of equipment fault diagnosis models caused by differences in the distribution of degradation data of injection molding machine rotating parts under various operating conditions, transfer learning can effectively minimize cross-domain data distribution differences by removing the inherent relationship between the data distributions of the source and target domains, thereby improving the diagnostic accuracy of the model under different operating conditions. Considering this, this article combines domain adaptation and adversarial training to propose a cross-working condition fault diagnosis domain adversarial transfer learning method. By introducing adversarial training, the relationship between sample data under various working conditions is established, and the difference in sample data distribution is minimized to achieve fault diagnosis under different working conditions.

articleTitle: Convolution Short-Time Passenger Flow Prediction Model of Urban Rail Transit Considering Interpretability
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This study focuses on the passenger flow prediction in subway stations, especially in the micro-network scenario. We use Granger causality analysis method and deep learning model to explore the relationship of passenger flow, which improves the accuracy and interpretability of short-term prediction of urban rail transit passenger flow. Based on the analysis of temporal and spatial causality of monitoring points, a convolution short-time passenger flow prediction model (ICCM-URTPFP model) of urban rail transit causality considering interpretability was constructed, and compared with the traditional model, which verified its advantages in passenger flow prediction.

Author Keywords: short time forecast of passenger flow

articleTitle: Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis Method of Acoustic and Vibration Multi-Level Fusion with Attention-1DCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Bearing faults are one of the most common causes of machine failures. However, due to the diverse nature of fault characteristics, a single sensor is insufficient for accurately identifying these features. Multi-source signals contain more comprehensive fault feature information. In order to effectively integrate multi-sensor signals and improve fault recognition accuracy, this paper proposes a rolling bearing fault diagnosis method based on acoustic-vibration multi-level fusion and Attention-1DCNN. Firstly, a single Attention-1DCNN module is employed to extract self-features from both the acoustic emission signal and vibration signal separately. Subsequently, complementary features are extracted from the fused acoustic emission and vibration signals using a feature mapping stacking method for fault identification. Finally, through softmax regression analysis, the fused features are classified into specific faults. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated using an experimentally constructed dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that under various fault modes such as outer ring crack, inner ring crack, and rolling body pitting, the proposed method achieved 100% recognition accuracy. Compared with single-sensor or single-level fusion diagnostic methods, this approach exhibits higher diagnostic accuracy and improved robustness.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Satellite Attitude Control System Based on GAT-TCN
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The satellite attitude control system (ACS) is a critical system for satellite mission execution, and its operational status significantly impacts the overall performance of the satellite. Addressing the challenges associated with the ACS, including high coupling, complex causality, and the difficulty of obtaining anomaly data, this paper proposes an unsupervised anomaly detection method based on Graph Attention Network (GAT) and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) for monitoring the telemetry data of the ACS. Given the complexity of the ACS and the high-dimensional nature of the data, the proposed method first utilizes GAT to capture the spatial dependencies among multidimensional parameters and reconstruct the monitoring data. Subsequently, TCN is employed to learn the temporal dependencies in the time series of the ACS, integrating partial mutual information to represent causal relationships for data prediction. Finally, based on the reconstruction and prediction residuals of the multidimensional parameters, the method assesses whether anomalies are present in the multidimensional sequences. The proposed method is validated through simulation data of the ACS, with the results demonstrating the effectiveness of the anomaly detection algorithm presented in this study.

articleTitle: Research on Performance Evaluation Metrics and Test Methodology of Predictive Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Predictive maintenance is an important scenario for the application of artificial intelligence technology in intelligent manufacturing, guiding enterprises to carry out equipment operation and maintenance through fault diagnosis and prediction, which can effectively reduce equipment downtime and improve production efficiency. However, the application of predictive maintenance technology has been in a bottleneck for a long time, and the fundamental reason is the lack of predictive maintenance performance evaluation index system, which makes it difficult for users to judge the effect of the application of this technology and thus lack confidence in it. Some scholars have proposed a preliminary evaluation index system, but the lack of testing technology to support the quantitative indexes makes it difficult to promote and implement the system. In this paper, by reviewing the related research on predictive maintenance performance assessment index system, we innovatively propose an on-off line assessment index system that can be standardized, and test some quantitative indexes through two different testing methods, namely, online testing and offline testing, in order to verify the applicability of the assessment index system.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method for Oil Pump Bearing Under Variable Operating Conditions Based on GADF and ConvNeXt Improved by SE Module
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Aiming at the serious consequences that may be triggered by oil pump bearing failures as well as the problems of traditional methods in terms of feature extraction, diagnostic accuracy, and model structure, this study proposes a variable operating condition fault diagnosis based on the combination of Gramian Angular Difference Fields (GADF) and ConvNeXt model improved by SE module. The model takes advantage of GADF's ability to capture the changing trends in a bearing vibration sequence through angular and relative variations, and the lightweight residual convolution structure in the ConvNeXt deep neural network, which is capable of extracting and learning the features in the vibration signals of the oil pump bearings end-to-end while consuming fewer parameters and arithmetic power. By randomly adding noise to 12kHz sampling frequency data of the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) bearing dataset to simulate real-world working conditions, and in turn, using model training, a 90.1% accuracy was achieved on the test set, significantly better than previously published results. Moreover, the optimal model ideally diagnoses faulty conditions on the CWRU bearing dataset under different operating conditions and JNU bearing dataset, possessing strong generalization ability and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Second-Order Time-Frequency-Multisqueezing Transform and its Applications in Rotating Machinery Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Rotating machinery holds a significant position in modern industry, and its fault diagnosis is crucial. The technique of time-frequency analysis (TFA) is crucial in fault diagnosis, as it adeptly handles nonstationary signals. Time-frequency-multisqueezing transform (TFMST) is an emerging TFA technique that can produce a time-frequency representation (TFR) with concentrated energy, and can effectively capture both harmonic and impulsive elements in nonstationary signals. However, limited by the performance of the estimation operator, TFMST faces challenges in producing a high resolution TFR when dealing with signals that exhibit strong nonstationarity. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a new TFA algorithm, the second-order TFMST, which embeds the second-order time-frequency estimation operator into the multisqueezing framework. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is confirmed through both numerical simulations and experimental results. The findings indicate that the proposed method achieves high-resolution TFR and demonstrates strong robustness against noise. In addition, the method can reconstruct the interested components.

articleTitle: Multi-level Preventive Maintenance Strategy for Railway Freight Car Coupler Device
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The coupler device, an essential component of railway freight cars, significantly influences operational safety and costs by its maintenance strategies. Periodic preventive maintenance strategies may lead to over-maintenance and/or under-maintenance. Thus, effective maintenance strategies are needed to ensure coupler reliability and control operational costs. This study addresses deficiencies in current maintenance strategies for railway freight car couplers, defining two levels of imperfect maintenance based on engineering scenario. The cost-effectiveness ratio is employed to decide maintenance methods at various intervals, and a multi-level reliability-based preventive maintenance model for the coupler device is developed. The proposed preventive maintenance model can reduce maintenance costs while maintaining a higher operational reliability, thereby enhancing the transportation efficiency of railway freight cars.

articleTitle: Fault Feature Recognition Of Satellite Power System Based On Incremental Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In modern communications and technology, satellite power systems play a central role, and their reliability and fault diagnosis technology are increasingly important. Traditional fault diagnosis methods mainly include signal processing and model-based methods, but they are often inefficient and have limited accuracy when processing complex data sets. This paper proposes a feature selection algorithm based on incremental learning to improve the efficiency and accuracy of fault diagnosis. Its advantage is that it can only evaluate the newly added feature set without the need to reprocess the entire data set, thus optimizing the feature selection process and significantly improving the efficiency and response speed of the algorithm. In order to verify its effectiveness, this article selected 8 public data sets and 4 satellite power system simulation data sets for testing. Then, widely used algorithms are introduced to compare with the algorithm proposed in this article for a more comprehensive comparative analysis. By comparing the differences in running time and classification accuracy of the algorithms, it is concluded that the algorithm proposed in this article can significantly reduce the running time while maintaining or improving the classification effect, verifying the feasibility of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Model for UAV with Small Sample Size and Imbalanced Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: With the development of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV), their application scenarios and task requirements have become more complex, demanding higher standards for subsequent fault diagnosis and equipment maintenance. The actual flight data of UAV usually exhibits small sample sizes and imbalanced characteristics. To achieve more efficient fault prediction for UAV, this paper establishes a SMOTE-IWOA-RF fault diagnosis model. This model optimizes the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) using chaotic initialization, nonlinear convergence factors, and Lévy flight strategies, resulting in better convergence accuracy and global search capability, as well as faster convergence speed. The model is compared with other classification models on data with different imbalance ratios, demonstrating that it is more efficient and accurate in UAV fault diagnosis, with the F1 score improving by about 10% compared to the pre-optimization state. Furthermore, the IWOA-RF model is combined with other data preprocessing methods, showing that SMOTE-IWOA-RF performs better on UAV operational data, indicating its practical value.

articleTitle: Enhanced Gear Damage Prediction Using Convolutional Neural Networks on Time-Series Sensor Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Gearboxes are essential in various industries, serving as the core mechanism for power transmission in machines like wind turbines and vehicles. Traditional fault detection primarily uses vibration analysis, which, although effective, often fails to precisely quantify gear damage. This paper introduces a novel approach by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with vibration data to enhance gearbox fault diagnosis. By employing machine learning algorithms, our model not only detects but also quantifies the severity of gear faults. This method involves collecting and analyzing vibration signals under different operational conditions to train a deep learning model that can accurately predict fault severity. This innovative approach, to the best of our knowledge, is the first to use AI to quantify gearbox faults, potentially revolutionizing maintenance strategies and improving industrial machinery reliability.

articleTitle: Enhancing Vision-Language Models Through Passive Online Target Recognition and Test-Time Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the realms of computer vision and natural language processing, researchers have aimed to effectively integrate images and text. Traditional methods, which depend on feature extraction and classifiers for target category inference, often fail to model the association between images and textual descriptions, resulting in insufficient information transfer when treating image processing and semantic inference separately. A novel approach based on vision-language large models offers an end-to-end learning framework that simultaneously processes and integrates image and textual information. This method enhances target recognition accuracy and robustness, exhibits strong zero-shot capabilities, and generalizes well across various image types. Furthermore, passive online target recognition, a form of unsupervised domain adaptation, eliminates the need for additional labeled data or external inputs by relying on target domain data for adaptation and learning. This technique automatically learns the feature distribution and structure of the target domain, enabling effective knowledge transfer from the source domain model to the target domain, even without source domain label data.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Tool Wear Prediction Model Based on an Improved Regressive Siamese Neural Network with Various Sample Sizes
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Tool condition has a great impact on the productivity and operating costs of enterprises.
