Many data-driven models based on the deep learning or transfer learning framework have already achieved significant results in tool condition monitoring. Nevertheless, the performance of these models typically varies with sample size, leading to poor application extensiveness across different-sized enterprises. This paper proposes a novel intelligent model for tool wear prediction, called Regressive Siamese Neural Network with Multilayer Perceptron-Support Vector Regression (RSNN-MLP-SVR). First, the Stockwell transform is utilized to extract more comprehensive time-frequency information from raw signals, and the absolute difference between tool wear values of paired samples is calculated as the corresponding label. Then, the backbone sub-network in the regressive Siamese neural network (RSNN) sub-model stacks multiple residual network modules to capture tool-wear-sensitive features from input paired samples. Subsequently, a new similarity measurement method based on multilayer perceptron (MLP) is proposed to evaluate the similarity between the input samples and incorporated into the optimization process of the RSNN sub-model. After sub-model training, a support vector regression (SVR) module is constructed to analyze features extracted by the backbone sub-network and predict tool wear values. Actual milling experiments were designed and conducted to gather available samples, and the following performance comparison experimental results prove the superiority of the proposed model under various sample sizes.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Ensemble Feature Selection Method with Combination of Sorted Subsets
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Rolling bearings are critical components in rotating machinery, where their failure can lead to abrupt system shutdowns and significant financial losses. A prevalent strategy for bearing fault diagnosis involves analyzing features extracted from vibration signals. To address the challenges posed by irrelevant and redundant features in the original feature set, as well as the instability in outputs from individual feature selection algorithms, this paper introduces a bearing fault diagnosis method based on Ensemble Feature Selection with combination of sorted subsets (shorten for EFS-CSS). This method integrates the outputs of multiple feature selection algorithms across various feature numbers to determine ensemble feature combinations that exhibit low dimensionality and robust fault characterization capabilities. Following feature identification, fault diagnosis is performed using four machine learning algorithms. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through classification experiments involving 24 and 48 fault conditions using the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) benchmark dataset. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior diagnostic performance compared to techniques reported in existing literature.

articleTitle: Fault Mechanism Knowledge-Driven Fault Detection of Rolling Bearings with Zero Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Deep neural networks have significant advantages in mass data learning, feature mining, accurate pattern recognition, etc., which have received extensive attention and in-depth research, and achieved prominent application performance. However, the network training depth depends on the labeled training set, and in practice, rotating mechanical equipment fault samples are scarce, or even zero samples, there is an imbalance in the training samples, and network training faces difficulties. To complete above challenges, this paper proposes a zero-sample intelligent fault detection method for rolling bearing driven by the knowledge of vibration fault spectrum. Firstly, an improved Hilbert envelope analysis is used to analyze monitored state signal of rolling bearing to obtain spectral features. Considering the fault frequencies of the inner and outer rings of rolling bearings are highly correlated with their structural dimensions, Ix, 2x and 3x frequency data under inner ring and outer ring faults are intercepted respectively as the training samples. Then, a new contrastive loss function is designed to optimize the network-based encoder by introducing the assumption that two samples acquired under continuous time series have high similarity. Furthermore, a fault detection algorithm is established to realize the intelligent detection of rolling bearing fault states. Finally, two standard rolling bearing datasets are used to analyze the effectiveness and reliability of proposed method. The results show that the proposed method can realize accurate detection for inner and outer ring faults with zero fault sample. This provides a new paradigm to carry out the zero-sample fault diagnosis for machinery.

articleTitle: Kernel Based Open CNN Algorithm for Known and Unknown Fault Diagnosis of Train Traction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Time-frequency map analysis method based on short-time Fourier transform (STFT) and deep learning algorithm based on convolutional neural network (CNN) are the most popular techniques in the field of vibration signal-based fault diagnosis. However, the unknown faults that often exist in open real-world environment, which causes the fault diagnosis accuracy of CNN based on traditional closed-set assumption show disastrous degradation. To solve the above problem, a kernel-based open CNN (KO-CNN) algorithm is proposed in this paper for known and unknown fault diagnosis of train traction motor. Firstly, the STFT is used to transform high-frequency vibration signal into time-frequency map to analysis time- and frequency-domain information simultaneously; Then, the kernel auto-encoder (KAE) is used to improve the conventional CNN for constructing the KO-CNN algorithm. The KO-CNN uses the diagnosis label from the conventional CNN and the feature data from the last fully connected layer of CNN to build KAE model for all known categories to diagnose between known and unknown faults at the same time. Finally, the PHM-BEIJING2024 train traction motor dataset is used to conduct the experiment. The results demonstrate that the proposed KO-CNN has better diagnosis performance of normal state, known faults and unknown faults in open real-world environment compared to conventional CNN.

articleTitle: Simulation Data-Driven Semi-Supervised Fault Diagnosis Method for Rolling Bearings
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In addressing the challenges of acquiring substantial and effective rolling bearing fault data in industrial environments, as well as the limited availability of labeled samples which hinders the generalization performance of intelligent diagnostic models, this paper proposes a semi-supervised fault diagnosis method driven by simulation data. Firstly, a fault-bearing simulation model under non-stationary conditions is established, generating comprehensive fault data by simulating various fault forms based on specific parameters set according to bearing type and operating conditions. Secondly, the proposed approach integrates a deep multi-scale residual network with traditional semi-supervised methods, effectively utilizing a large number of unlabeled samples along with a limited number of labeled samples for fault classification. Finally, by comparing the time-domain and envelope spectrum plots of the simulated data with real data, it is observed that the vibration waveforms and fault characteristic frequencies are highly similar. The proposed method demonstrates a significant improvement in diagnostic accuracy compared to traditional semi-supervised methods in various experiments. The results indicate the feasibility of using simulation-generated data to compensate for the lack of real data and highlight the superiority of the proposed semi-supervised method in fault diagnosis with scarce labeled samples.

articleTitle: A General Approach for Health Index-Based Remaining Useful Life Prediction Using Functional Principal Component Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Accurately predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) is crucial for industrial device prognostics and health management. With the advancement of sensor technology, multiple sensor data can be collected during the monitoring process of these devices. This requires analyzing data collected from multiple sensors and extracting useful information to predict the RUL of the product. Existing studies have proposed various methods for fusing multi-sensor data to construct a health index (HI). However, most of these methods rely on the assumption that sensors are independent of each other. In reality, during equipment operation, there is a certain correlation between sensor signals. Ignoring these correlations when constructing the HI may affect the accuracy of RUL predictions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a method based on functional principal component analysis (FPCA) for multi-sensor signal fusion. Compared to other data fusion methods, using FPCA to analyze data can extract orthogonal principal component functions from multiple sensors, effectively modeling the correlations between sensor signals. The proposed method utilizes FPCA to fuse data from multiple sensors, achieving dimensionality reduction while avoiding collinearity. Simulation studies and a case study on the C-MAPSS dataset demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively fuse data from multiple sensor signals and accurately predict RUL.

articleTitle: A New System-level Fault Diagnosis Method for Train Transmission Systems Based on Graph Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Efficient and reliable fault diagnosis of train transmission systems is crucial for ensuring the safety of train operations. With the advancements in big data and deep learning technologies, intelligent fault diagnosis techniques have made many achievements. However, a significant limitation in existing related research is the development of separate diagnostic models for each component, which neglects the mutual coupling relationships among different components and the propagation and interaction of faults. This oversight significantly hampers the overall diagnostic accuracy of these models. To address the aforementioned problem, a novel system-level fault diagnosis method is proposed for train transmission systems. In the proposed method, convolutional neural networks are first employed to obtain low-dimensional node attributes. Then, the graph attention mechanism is introduced for feature fusion by incorporating the spatial relationships between components, enabling the identification of the health status of each node. The efficacy of the proposed method is validated by designing and carrying out fault simulation experimental of the bogie transmission system at Beijing Jiaotong University. Experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement in diagnostic accuracy for each component node, with only a minimal increase in parameters and computational complexity.

articleTitle: Research on Personnel Risk Prediction Based on Job Hazard Analysis and Bayesian Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To accelerate the informatization and systematization of safety management in EMU depot maintenance operations, this paper focuses on first-level maintenance as the research subject and combines Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) with Bayesian Network (BN) for personnel risk prediction. First, the JHA method is used to systematically break down the first-level maintenance process, identifying potential risk factors. Based on these identified risks, a Bayesian Network is constructed to quantify the relationships between the risk factors, predicting the current probability of safely completing first-level maintenance at 99.48%. Finally, through posterior probability and sensitivity analysis, it is determined that the greatest safety impacts are from not wearing protective gear and insufficient EGS discharge time. This method provides a quantitative evaluation approach for the safety management of EMU depot maintenance operations, helping to enhance the risk control capabilities of maintenance personnel.

articleTitle: PBMT: A Novel Transformer-Based Model for Accurate RUL Prediction in Industrial Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In recent years, the prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) has become a research hotspot about prognostics and health management (PHM). Highly accurate RUL prediction is the basis for improving the reliability of mechanical system and reducing the probability of unexpected accidents. Although deep learning-based methods for RUL prediction have made significant progress in applications, the existing models still suffer from high computational complexity and insensitivity to the dependencies of each time step when dealing with long sequence data. To solve these problems, this paper proposes a new model that combines the time-step encoder with the ProbSparse Self-Attention mechanism, replacing the encoder in the traditional Transformer. This approach not only reduces the computational complexity of the model when dealing with long sequence data but also maintains a high prediction accuracy. It has been validated using NASA's C-MAPSS and N-CMAPSS datasets, and the results demonstrate the method's effectiveness and accuracy.

articleTitle: Tool Remaining Useful Life Prediction Under Variable Milling Conditions Considering Random Failure Threshold
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Tool reliability is one of the key factors to ensure the quality and efficiency of machine tool machining. Aiming at the influence of changing milling conditions on the degradation signal during tool machining and the uncertainty of the failure threshold, this paper proposed a method for tool remaining useful life (RUL) prediction under variable milling conditions considering random failure threshold. Firstly, high-dimension features are extracted from multi-sensor signals. The feature that best characterizes tool degradation is selected as a degradation signal through correlation analysis. Secondly, a degradation signal transformation algorithm is designed to eliminate the influence of milling conditions on the amplitude of the degradation signal. Then, the tool degradation model is constructed based on the Wiener process, and the RUL distribution is deduced considering the random failure threshold. The model parameters are obtained using the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) algorithm to achieve the tool RUL prediction. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is verified by the milling cutter experimental data. The results show that the proposed method can eliminate the influence of milling conditions on the degradation signal and improve the accuracy of tool RUL prediction.

articleTitle: Inverse Identification of Contact Forces and Prediction of Roller Stress Fields for Large Main Bearings Based on Physics-Informed Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The main bearings of large rotating machinery often encounter heavy overloads, significant offset loads, and variable loads during operation. Accurately sensing the internal contact force and the force field distribution of the rollers is crucial for evaluating the health status of the main bearing. To address the difficulty of precisely measuring contact forces of the main bearing, this study proposes an inverse calculation framework for the contact force within the main bearing based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). The proposed method embeds the equilibrium-physical-geometric equations and boundary constraints that describe the linear elastic contact boundary value problem into the loss function. By leveraging physical laws and limited observable data from roller end faces, the loss function is optimized through a two-stage process involving Adam and L-BFGS-B optimizers. This method predicts the distribution of displacement and stress fields, enabling the inverse identification of contact forces. Simulation experiments demonstrate that, driven by shear stress data, the coefficient of determination R2 for the inverse contact force reaches 93.92%.

Author Keywords: contact force inside the main bearing

articleTitle: A Novel Two-Stage Prognostics Framework for Aero-Engine Remaining Useful Life Estimation Under Dynamic Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Deep learning-based remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for aero-engines has been widely used to forecast impending failures and ensure flight safety. However, most existing methods ignore the intricate impacts of dynamic operating conditions on the monitoring data gathered by multiple sensors, thus hindering accurate estimation of RUL. To address this problem, we propose a novel two-stage prognostics framework for aero-engine RUL estimation under dynamic operating conditions. The core idea is to disaggregate the health and operational condition information in the monitoring data as much as possible to ensure that the input data to the estimation model is least likely to be negatively affected by dynamic operating conditions, thus improving the RUL prediction accuracy. Specifically, the first stage starts with training an unsupervised variational autoencoder with data decomposition capabilities. Subsequently, the well-trained encoder and decoder components with uniform operating condition data will generate high-quality monitoring data embedded with health information and without distractions caused by dynamic operating conditions. In the second stage, high-quality monitoring data are combined with current RUL estimation methods to extract degradation characteristics and make accurate RUL predictions. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework are demonstrated using publicly available aero-engine degradation datasets.

articleTitle: Analysis of Vibration Characteristics of Rotor-Stator Rubbing Faults in a Dual-Rotor System
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Studying rotor-stator rubbing faults in dual-rotor systems has significant engineering and practical value. This paper focuses on the vibration characteristics of dual-rotor systems under rotor-stator rubbing faults. Firstly, a dual-rotor system model incorporating a tapered beam structure is established based on the finite element method, and the corresponding dynamic equations are derived. Secondly, the blade-casing rubbing force model is applied to the dual-rotor system to investigate the vibration characteristics under rotor-stator rubbing faults. The Newmark-B method is used to solve the fault dynamic equations, exploring the impact of blade count and rubbing stiffness on the response. The accuracy of the simulation results is verified through experiments. The results indicate that, in rotor-stator rubbing faults, as the number of blades increases, the “hardening” effect of the rotor becomes significant, and the resonance speed point of the low-pressure rotor shifts significantly backward. As the rubbing stiffness increases, the vibration amplitude of the rubbed rotor decreases significantly at a constant speed, indicating that rotor-stator rubbing faults can be considered as a “constraint” effect on the rotor.

articleTitle: A Reliability Assessment Method Based on Environmental Stress and Multi-Source Information Fusion for Complex Product
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: A reliability assessment method based on environmental stress and multi-source information fusion is proposed for the problem of reliability assessment of complex products under small sample conditions. Firstly, considering the influence of temperature and humidity on complex products, the environmental stress acceleration factor is calculated based on the Hallberg-Peck model, and the working time in different environments is mapped to the reference environmental conditions. Secondly, multi-source information, such as historical test information and similar product information, are used to correct onsite use information. And according to the characteristics of different types of truncated data, the method of determining the corresponding distribution parameters is given. Then, the fitting factor is determined based on Bayes chi-square test and Bayes chi-square goodness of fit, and then the multi-source information is fused to carry out reliability assessment. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by an example analysis.

articleTitle: A Multi-Source Domain Adaptation Method for Fault Diagnosis of Train Axle Box Bearings Under Limited Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Transfer learning based on domain adaption demonstrates powerful capabilities in intelligent fault diagnosis. It enables diagnosis networks to utilize data from various sources, potentially improving the diagnostic performance of networks in practical engineering scenarios where measurement samples are limited. Nevertheless, current research faces several constraints: (1) They lack effective alignment methods to extract invariant representations of the source domain and the target domain. (2) They align distributions without taking into account the domain-specific decision boundaries that separate classes. To address the aforementioned limitations, a novel multi-source unsupervised domain adaptation framework is introduced for fault diagnosis of train axle box bearings. Firstly, it aligns the domain-specific distribution for each source-target domain pair. Then, utilizing the domain-specific decision boundaries, it aligns the classifiers for bearing fault states. Finally, we carried out two experiments to collect data, including train axle box bearing faults simulation and bearing faults finite element analysis. The proposed framework's effectiveness and superiority are validated through ablation studies and comparative method experiments.

articleTitle: Reliability Improvement Methods for Civil Aircraft: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Civil aviation, as an integral part of modern transportation systems, directly impacts passenger safety and transportation efficiency. A detailed literature survey is conducted to investigate the various techniques related to design and manufacture, maintenance processes, flight operations and data management. Based on such a method's merits and limitations, this paper suggests integrating multiple methods to enhance the reliability of civil aircraft during different stages of its life cycle. These solutions aim to improve aircraft design, enhance maintenance efficiency, and bolster flight operation safety, ultimately delivering higher reliability in civil aviation and providing passengers with safer and more comfortable flight experiences.

articleTitle: A Novel Physics-Based Polar Diagram for the Diagnosis of Compound Faults with Similar Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Compound fault diagnosis of rotating machinery, including bearing, rotor and gear, has always been attracting increasing attention from researchers. Among them, the classification and isolation of compound fault with similar characteristics remains a challenging issue. To this end, a physics-based polar diagram with convolutional neural network (CNN) model is proposed to distinguish the similar fault characteristics by fusing the self-sensing motor drive signals. Firstly, the misalignment and bearing fault model are constructed, and their impacts on q-axis current in motor drive are derived. Secondly, the empirical mode decomposition (EMD) is used to extract the feature-related components from the q-axis current signal. Subsequently, an improved physics-based polar diagram (PPD) is constructed using the feature-related q-axis current components and modified motor phase signal with physical knowledge and data features. Finally, comparative experiments with a baseline CNN shows that the PPD proposed in this paper is superior to traditional image representation methods in precision and transfer learning ability.

articleTitle: A Method for Reconstructing the Shape of Wing Panels Based on Fiber Optic Sensors and Tomographic Imaging Principles
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The aircraft wing structure shape reconstruction method based on discrete strain information not only provides data support for the digital collaborative health monitoring and prediction technology of wing structure but also helps to improve the aerodynamic shape and flight quality of the aircraft, achieve structural stealth, and enhance the pointing accuracy of the on-board conformal antenna. As result, a wing skin panel shape reconstruction method based on the principle of tomographic imaging and strain information perception is proposed. According to the idea of tomographic imaging, a “non-intrusive” layout form that only requires sensors to be arranged on the periphery of the monitoring area is designed, breaking through the limitation that sensors can not be arranged in the monitoring area under special working conditions. A method for constructing the deflection shape function of the wing skin panel based on the concept of synthetic curvature is proposed, solving the problem of error accumulation and elimination of deformation inversion at non-monitoring points of the measured structure caused by the uncertainty of the limited discrete layout of sensors and the choice of interpolation fitting method. On this basis, a model deformation monitoring and inversion system for wing skin panel based on fiber optic grating sensors is constructed. The experimental results show that under the single-end fixed bending and torsion working condition, the average relative error of the panel model shape reconstruction is 4.17%. Under the double-end fixed double-concentrated load working condition, the average relative error of the shape reconstruction is 8.07%. The wing deformation distribution information reconstructed by the method proposed in this paper can be mapped onto the virtual twin model of the wing, providing technical support for the safety assessment, early warning, and on-condition maintenance of the entire service life of key structures of the aircraft.

articleTitle: Improved Grey Markov Aviation Safety Prediction Based on XGBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The number of accident indicators and accidents are critical metrics reflecting aviation safety. The Grey-Markov prediction model effectively forecasts aviation safety metrics such as accident indicators and accidents, especially in scenarios with limited samples, nonlinearity, and randomness. It has been demonstrated that different Grey-Markov models exhibit varying prediction performances depending on the data. Therefore, this paper explores an improved Grey-Markov model based on XGBoost for intelligent state partitioning, aiming to enhance the robustness and accuracy of the Grey-Markov model. Four sets of aviation safety data were used for empirical validation, yielding an average relative error of 0.0973. Compared to traditional Grey-Markov models with a single state partition, this approach proved to be more intelligent and accurate, showcasing its potential in predicting small sample, nonlinear time series data. This model offers valuable insights for aviation managers in macro-level safety management.

articleTitle: Maximum Fault Information Envelope Spectrum Based on the Spectral Coherence for Bearing Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: As the core component of rotating machinery, bearings inevitably experience failures due to the complexity of internal mechanical systems and the harshness of their operating environments. Efficiently identifying incipient faults in bearings can enhance equipment operational efficiency and reliability while reducing production costs and risks. Therefore, there has been a surge of research in both academia and industry. Among the available techniques, envelope analysis is one of the most popular, found in nearly all commercial software. However, due to its reliance on the assumption of signal stationarity and the inherent limitations in frequency band optimization, envelope analysis often struggles to achieve satisfactory results in industrial environments with strong interference and heavy background noise. Cyclostationarity-based analysis breached the usual assumption of stationary, positing that bearing fault signals exhibit cyclostationary nature, thus providing another tool. Therefore, a new maximum fault information envelope spectrum (MFIES) based on the spectral coherence for bearing diagnosis is proposed to overcome the above limitations. In this work, firstly, the bi-spectral map is obtained. Then, a fault symptom index is introduced to assess the amount of fault information contained in each frequency slice. Finally, the frequency slice corresponding to the maximum index value is selected to generate the MFIES. This way, it enhances the fault features while suppressing other components. Moreover, Simulation analysis and experimental data validation have validated the effectiveness of this method. The results indicate that this method possesses strong capabilities for extracting bearing fault characteristics even in the presence of severe interference.

articleTitle: Cloud-Edge Collaborative Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Deep Q-Network for Rotating Machinery
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the actual, operating conditions of rotating machinery often change due to different tasks. Because of the delay in cloud model updates, the model cannot effectively match with the real-time data at the edge. To solve this problem, a new cloud-edge collaborative fault diagnosis method for rotating machinery is proposed in this paper based on deep <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Q}$</tex> network (DQN). In this method, Transformer is introduced into the DQN to learn fault features under unknown operating conditions and assign pseudo-labels to real-time data. Meanwhile, A reward function based on cosine similarity is designed to evaluate the above process. The DQN is optimized through online learning, updating the cloud model, and then deployed to the edge through model slicing and ensemble to achieve real-time fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions. The rolling bearing fault diagnosis experiment is implemented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that our method can adaptively update under varying operating conditions, and the updated model achieves higher fault diagnosis accuracy compared to the non-updated model.

articleTitle: Regularized Optimal Transport Enabled Few-Shot Cross-Domain Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In industrial scenarios, collecting adequate labeled fault samples for diverse conditions is challenging. The few-shot cross-domain domain diagnosis is a more challenging and underexplored scenario, where the model needs to generalize effectively to the target domain with only limited training samples from source domain. This paper proposed a regularized optimal transport-enabled few-shot cross-domain (ROTFC) fault diagnosis method via designing spectral regularized augmentation optimal transport for this problem. Specifically, the Mixup strategy is introduced into optimal transport to facilitate few-shot adaptation by extending source distribution, aligning source and target domain distribution and minimizing the vicinal risk, while learning domain-invariant classifier and cross-domain alignment. Besides, spectral regularization is used to balance the transferability and discriminability of the proposed ROTFC method by penalizing the eigenvectors. Experiments on three-phase motor fault diagnosis show the effectiveness of the proposed ROTFC method in dealing with few-shot cross-domain diagnosis, the diagnosis accuracy can be improved by at least 3 % in one-shot diagnosis.

articleTitle: An Edge-Cloud Collaboration Framework Based on Federated Feature Separation Autoencoding for Milling Cutter Remaining Useful Life Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Substantial progress has been made in remaining useful life prediction methods for mechanical equipment and milling tools. Nevertheless, the large-scale practical application of these methods still confronts two major challenges. Firstly, high-performance prediction models require high-compute devices to operate, resulting in a significant increase in costs. Secondly, there are issues related to data silos and privacy protection. We propose an edge-cloud collaboration framework based on federated feature separation autoencoding to address these challenges. The training process of the proposed framework is divided into two stages. In the first stage, multiple low-compute clients collaboratively train a feature separation autoencoder through Federated training. This FSAE is designed to extract public features with similar distributions from the data on different clients. In the second stage, the clients upload public features and corresponding labels to a trusted server, where a global prediction model is trained. The trained prediction model can be deployed locally or in the cloud based on the requirement. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework are verified through the full-life experimental data of milling cutters.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Bearings Based on Jensen-Shannon Divergence and Dynamic Multi-Time Scale Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is a key research task in intelligent maintenance of mechanical equipment. However, there are still shortcomings in bearings RUL prediction: 1) Due to the different degradation stages of rolling element bearings, health indicators (HI) also exhibit different degradation characteristics. However, the two-stage nature of the HI is often overlooked in existing research. 2) Model-based methods in current use typically employ a single model to describe the bearing degradation process, making it difficult to comprehensively describe the various potential degradation trends of bearings in the future. To deal with the aforementioned issues, this study constructs a health indicator, named HI-JS, using the self-organizing map (SOM) clustering and Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence methods. The effectiveness of HI-JS is validated using comprehensive evaluation criterion. A new bearings RUL prediction process is proposed using JS divergence and dynamic multi-time scale aggregation for bearings RUL prediction. The proposed approach is evaluated using XJTU-SY bearing datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the accuracy of RUL prediction of rolling element bearings.

articleTitle: Intelligent Scheduling Research and Application Based on PHM: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The manufacturing industry is transforming towards high-end, intelligent and digitalization. Intelligent scheduling is one of the key technologies to achieve the digital transformation of the manufacturing industry. The intelligent scheduling platform of the enterprise's intelligent manufacturing workshop can promote enterprises to improve production efficiency, reduce costs, improve product quality and enhance the controllability of the production process. This paper reviews the current research status of intelligent scheduling in production workshops from three perspectives: workshop personnel scheduling, flexible job workshop scheduling, and workshop intelligent scheduling platform. Human resources are important resources in production workshops, and achieving optimal matching of people and positions is an important way to improve enterprise production efficiency. Production workshop operation scheduling is to optimize the allocation of processing task sets in time for workshop processing equipment clusters under the premise of meeting some performance indicators. The specific implementation of intelligent scheduling in production workshops depends on the workshop intelligent scheduling platform, which is closely integrated with the Internet to achieve dynamic coordination and adaptive adjustment of manufacturing enterprises' production. With the development of new technologies such as big data, artificial intelligence, robots, prognostics and health management (PHM), there will be some new development trends in the research of intelligent scheduling in production workshops. This paper looks forward to the future development trend of intelligent scheduling from three perspectives: workshop personnel scheduling, flexible job workshop scheduling, and workshop intelligent scheduling platform. Additionally, as a future development trend, this paper also reviews the intelligent scheduling application based on PHM.

articleTitle: Dynamic Vision-Enabled Machine Condition Monitoring: A Point Cloud-Based Diagnostic Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Event-based cameras are an emerging type of Dynamic Vision Sensor. Unlike traditional standard cameras, they record the occurrence of brightness changes, which enables them to achieve low latency, high dynamic range, and high temporal resolution. To explore the application of contactless event data in machine fault diagnosis, this article draws inspiration from the similarity in data format between event data and 3D point cloud data. While point cloud data is widely employed in computer vision tasks, particularly in intelligent systems like autopilots and robots, its usage in industrial settings is scarce. This article presents one of the pioneering attempts in the current literature on using a 3D point cloud data algorithm to process event data for machine fault diagnosis. A geometric data structure is proposed to represent event information and a deep learning method on point cloud data is employed for classification to perform diagnosis tasks. The article conducts experiments on diagnosing rotating machine faults using event-based cameras. It has been extensively validated that utilizing point sets derived from dynamic vision data captured by event-based cameras can achieve high accuracy in fault diagnosis. Given their economic viability, installation flexibility, and data efficiency, event-based cameras emerge as a promising solution for non-contact monitoring of machine health conditions and fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Transformer-Based Time Series Prediction Model with Contrastive Learning for Nuclear Power System State Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) is currently the mainstream solution for the condition monitoring and maintenance of industrial systems. In PHM, the system condition is monitored by monitoring the operational status parameters of the system to diagnose equipment faults, predict the remaining useful life, etc. Utilizing sequential operational status parameters to complete prediction and classification tasks is usually modeled as a time series processing task. Therefore, a high-performance time series prediction model is crucial for PHM. This paper focuses on the use of time series prediction models to achieve the prediction of key state parameters of the nuclear power system. However, there are still some challenges when directly applying existing time series prediction models to industrial systems. First, obtaining operational data on the nuclear power system is relatively difficult, resulting in a small amount of training data, which causes many models to face the risk of insufficient training or overfitting. Second, most of the existing time series prediction models are composed of high- and low-frequency decoupling modules, while the operational data of nuclear power systems often have fewer high-frequency components, making it difficult for many existing SOTA models to achieve good results. In order to address these challenges, we have developed a Transformer-based time series prediction model with contrastive learning for monitoring the status of nuclear power systems. We evaluated the new model on three nuclear power simulation datasets and four power transformer datasets. The experimental results show that the new model's performance is superior to baseline models. We also proved the effectiveness of our improvement through ablation experiments.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Battery Health Estimation with Incomplete Charging Data and Spiking ResNet
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The accurate estimation of state of health (SOH) plays a crucial role in ensuring the safe operation of batteries. Most existing SOH estimation methods are based on complete charging or discharging data. However, in real-world applications, data are often derived from partial charging or discharging processes influenced by varying user habits, which brings great challenges to the accurate SOH estimation of batteries. In this article, a SOH estimation method based on incremental capacity (IC) curve reconstruction and spiking ResNet is proposed to deal with the SOH estimation issue using partial data. The monitoring data are preprocessed using differentiation and Gaussian filtering to obtain the IC curves. A nonparametric degradation model is constructed using functional principal component analysis (FPCA). Subsequently, the functional principal component (FPC) scores are estimated by the maximum likelihood estimation (PAMLE) algorithm to reconstruct the IC curves. Ultimately, the SOH can be estimated through the spiking ResNet. The proposed method is evaluated using the XJTU battery experimental data. The results demonstrate that the proposed method provides more accurate and reliable estimation results than other methods.

articleTitle: Structural Optimization of Turntable Frame Based on Improved Latin Hypercube Design and Hybrid Surrogate Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Structural optimization is an important part for engineering design. It involves optimizing the product or engineering structure by combining finite element analysis (FEA) with optimization algorithms. Based on the improved Latin hypercube design (LHD) and hybrid surrogate model, a structural optimization method is proposed to optimize the structure. It employs the successive local enumeration (SLE) method to improve LHD and obtain more comprehensive size parameter and sample space information. Based on the FEA results of the sample points, a hybrid surrogate model is established, and it involves polynomial response surface model (RSM), Kriging model, and radial basis function (RBF) neural network model. Thus, the simulation computation time is reduced and more accurate results are obtained. Moreover, the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) is used for multi-objective optimization of the size parameters, and the optimal parameter solution is gained based on the minimum Euclidean distance criterion. Case study of a two-axis turntable frame is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that after the optimization, the first order natural frequency of the turntable frame is reduced by 3.37%, meanwhile the mass is reduced by 8.87% and the maximum deformation is reduced by 19.42%. The results indicate that with minimal loss in the first order natural frequency, significant improvements can be achieved in the properties of mass and deformation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Abnormal Vibration and Sound in the High-Pressure Control Valve Due to Silencer Cracks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Failure of the high-pressure control valve will lead to unbalanced regulation of the steam inlet volume of the turbine, resulting in unplanned shutdown and serious economic losses. The high-pressure control valve of a nuclear power plant turbine unit showed abnormal vibration and sound, along with the presence of cracks at the bottom of silencer. The paper analyzed and compared the vibration data of normal and abnormal valve, obtaining the characteristic frequency of abnormal valves. The causes of abnormal vibration were studied through simulations of silencer model, including modal simulation and fluid-structure interaction simulation. Then a modal simulation of the gas column between the silencer and the positioning ring was used to analyze the cause of abnormal sound. The results showed that the silencer of the high-pressure control valve cracked at the bottom due to metal fatigue. The cracked silencer model undergone 3rd order resonance at small opening degrees and the cracked silencer model undergone 6th order resonance at large opening degrees (>35%), resulting in abnormal vibration. Abnormal vibration caused steam leakage, and then the steam excited the gas column between the silencer and the positioning ring to resonate, causing abnormal sound. Finally, according to the analysis results, replacing the silencer resolved the problem of abnormal vibration and sound.

articleTitle: Knowledge Extraction and Application of Railway Operation Equipment Fault Diagnosis Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Focusing on the issue where traditional fault diagnosis methods cannot effectively utilize the textual records of railway equipment faults and heavily rely on experts' experience, a knowledge graph-based fault analysis method for railway operation equipment is proposed. By designing preprocessing rules to process the text corpus to be annotated, and combining the attention mechanism (ATT) and bi-directional gated recurrent neural network (BiGRU) to complete the knowledge extraction, the knowledge graph of railway operation equipment faults is constructed. On this basis, a cause recommendation strategy combining query and reasoning is designed, which can give reasonable fault analysis suggestions based on the faults that have occurred. This research utilizes the dataset sourced from a railway administration, examines the effectiveness of the knowledge extraction method through experiments, and analyzes the feasibility of utilizing the constructed knowledge graph to assist in fault analysis through cause recommendation.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Method of Aircraft Sensor Based on Canonical Variate Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Aircrafts heavily rely on sensors for effective control. However, sensor faults are bound to occur over time. It is imperative to devise a dependable sensor fault detection technique for aircrafts. This study presents a data-driven strategy for aircraft fault detection using canonical variate analysis (CVA), a multivariate statistical technique. Through the utilization of CVA, the study establishes optimal correlations in aircraft flight data, facilitating accurate and efficient diagnosis of faults. The T2 statistic and squared prediction error (SPE) are put forward as indicators for detecting faults in this method. Compared to the traditional model-based Kalman filter (KF) fault detection method, this approach involves learning from actual data and using the learned models for decision-making, without the need for prior knowledge. The effectiveness of CVA in accurately identifying abrupt and incipient faults in inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors has been confirmed through comprehensive simulation and experimental verification. This method lays the foundation for active fault tolerance control of aircrafts and improves the overall reliability and safety of aircrafts.

articleTitle: Optimization of Multi-Level Nurse Scheduling: A Biorhythm-Based Fatigue Model Integrated with PFMEA for Enhancing Service Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper focuses on the optimization of multi-level nurse scheduling, addressing the issue that traditional methods often overlook nurse fatigue risks and their impact on service system reliability. An innovative solution is proposed, which involves the introduction of PFMEA (Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis) as a risk management tool, combined with biorhythm theory, to construct a biorhythm-based fatigue model for nurse scheduling. This model is integrated into the scheduling optimization process to achieve rational allocation of multi-level nurse resources. To assess risks and solve the complex scheduling problem, this study adopts the entropy-weighted PFMEA method for risk quantification and designs a hybrid improved algorithm that combines the advantages of NSGAII (Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II) and MOGWO (Multi-Objective Grey Wolf Optimizer). An empirical study was conducted in a county-level hospital to validate the effectiveness of the model. The results demonstrate that the model not only significantly optimizes the scheduling plan but also alleviates nurse fatigue, reduces risks, and ultimately enhances the reliability of the medical service system. This research brings new perspectives and methodologies to the field of multi-level nurse scheduling in medical services. Future studies can further explore diversified scheduling modes, more refined fatigue assessment methods, and intelligent scheduling algorithms to continuously improve the quality and efficiency of medical services.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Mode Analysis Method of Nuclear I&C Software Based on Time Automata
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: This paper presents a novel fault mode analysis method for nuclear instrumentation and control (I&C) software based on timed automata. The proposed approach addresses the limitations of traditional fault analysis techniques in handling complex, real-time systems by accurately capturing the dynamic characteristics and intricate interaction patterns of nuclear I&C software. Key contributions include: (1) development of a timed automata-based modeling framework tailored for nuclear I&C software; (2) design of a comprehensive fault mode library compatible with timed automata models; and (3) implementation of an automated fault mode analysis algorithm leveraging model checking techniques. The method's efficacy is demonstrated through a case study on a digital reactor protection system, specifically the Reactor Coolant Pump speed protection subsystem. Results show significant improvements in fault mode identification rates, particularly for time-related faults, and enhanced capabilities in quantitative analysis and dynamic behavior capture compared to traditional methods. This approach provides a more rigorous and systematic tool for improving the reliability and safety of digital I&C systems in nuclear power plants, with potential applications in other safety-critical domains.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis Technology of Inertial Navigation Systems on Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Inertial navigation systems play a crucial role in the aviation industry, and their safe operation is of paramount importance to the entire flight mission. The research on fault diagnosis of inertial navigation systems is becoming increasingly significant. This paper conducts an in-depth study on the fault diagnosis of strapdown inertial navigation systems in fault-tolerant integrated navigation systems. The paper thoroughly analyzes the fault modes and effects of strapdown inertial navigation systems, determines the system's composition structure, identifies possible fault causes and mitigation solutions, and proposes a fault diagnosis process. It conducts an in-depth analysis of the fault manifestations of relevant components and determines the forms of fault manifestations. Based on the fault manifestations, data collection and preprocessing are performed using simulation equipment and relevant datasets to obtain operational data of the inertial navigation system under various working conditions. This paper builds a model for diagnosing component faults in inertial navigation systems using deep learning methods. In terms of selecting the deep learning model, this paper constructs a Transformer model for fault diagnosis classification. After building the model, through validation and analysis of experimental data, this paper demonstrates the effectiveness and feasibility of the model used in fault diagnosis of strapdown inertial navigation systems, proving that the constructed model can diagnose faults in inertial navigation systems. Finally, the study is summarized, and future research directions in this field are discussed.

articleTitle: Ontology Construction of Fault Diagnosis Knowledge Graph for Civil Aircraft Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Maintenance of civil aircraft systems is crucial for ensuring air travel safety. However, managing a large volume of maintenance data can lead to inefficiencies in operation support work. Knowledge graphs are utilized to visualize maintenance manuals and historical fault diagnosis records. Therefore, this paper presents a novel ontology construction approach for fault diagnosis knowledge graphs in civil aircraft maintenance, focusing on event domain, fault domain, and product domain. The ontology construction process follows the “ontology seven-step method.” Finally, several applications, including information retrieval, intelligent question answering, and optimal route recommendation, are implemented using this knowledge graph.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearing Under Different Conditions Using Modified Inception and LSTM with Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Fault diagnosis of rolling bearing is very important for health prediction and maintenance of rotating machinery. However, the bearing operating conditions are complicated in the practical industrial environment, which is challenging to diagnose fault efficiently and accurately. In this paper, an end-to-end intelligent fault diagnosis method of modified inception structure cascades to Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) with Attention Mechanism (AM) is proposed. Firstly, the modified inception as the feature extraction module can effectively extract the multi-scale feature information from different fault vibration signals by using its multi-branch local sparsity, which can also improve the generalization of this model. Then, the feature information is input into the classification module composed of LSTM based on AM. It can further learn the temporal relevance of feature information. Meanwhile, the AM can adaptively map weights, which significantly enhances the memory ability of LSTM for important information and improves the robustness of this model. In addition, the internal working principle of the overall network is explained by the visual analysis of the key steps and results. Finally, the proposed method is verified by experimental results including single and compound fault bearing under different conditions. It is shown from the results that the proposed end-to-end intelligent fault diagnosis method can accurately identify different bearing fault types under different speeds or background noise.

articleTitle: Bottom Component Recognition Methods of Urban Rail Trains Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The challenge of accurately recognizing parts under urban rail trains (URT) due to their complex structure and varying scales is addressed in this study. A novel part recognition method based on an enhanced YOLOv5 model is proposed, integrating the convolutional block attention module (CBAM) and an optimized bounding box regression function. Adding CBAM to the YOLOv5 backbone improves the model's focus on crucial features, enhancing its ability to detect and locate components accurately. Furthermore, the bounding box regression function is refined using the extended intersection over union (EIoU) function, which enhances the speed, precision, and accuracy of prediction box regression and localization. A target detection dataset was created by photographing the underside of URT parts using a line array camera. Experimental results on this dataset demonstrate that the proposed method delivers outstanding performance, achieving 97.3% precision, 97.1 % recall, a high mean average precision (mAP) of 98.1 %, and a detection speed of 41.656 FPS.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning for Integrated Nested Digital-Physical Data in Product Performance Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the field of product performance prediction, the prediction accuracy of deep learning methods is limited by the scarcity of physical data. The integration of digital and physical data has been proposed to enrich the sample, but there is a problem of conditional shift between digital and physical data. Facing the above challenges, a transfer learning method for regression prediction based on conditional distribution embedding is proposed in this paper. Through the pre-training-fine-tuning of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model, a hybrid loss function is constructed to align the conditional distribution discrepancies across the digital and physical data and to preserve the global consistency of the conditional distributions in the target domain. Experimental results based on a test function confirm that this method can significantly improve the prediction accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: Blade Modal Parameter Identification Based on Fiber Strain Sensing and Fitting Circle Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The dynamic response characteristics of civil aircraft are closely related to aerodynamic load, rotor speed, flight attit ude and other parameters under specific flight conditions. Ther efore, real-time identification of rotor blade dynamic modal pa rameters is of great significance for evaluating flight conditions and ensuring. flight safety. Therefore, this paper proposes a ne w method of rotor blade modal parameter identification based on fiber optic strain sensing and fitting circle method. The fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensor is used to collect the blade vibratio n strain signal in real time, and the fitting circle method is combined to identify the modal parameters. The system frequency response error function matrix based on the strain response ch aracteristics is derived, and the fitting circle model including th e correlation coefficient of blade frequency response function is constructed. By solving the best fitting circle parameters, the i dentification of structural modal parameters is realized. On thi s basis, a composite blade modal parameter identification syste m based on quasi-distributed fiber strain sensing is constructed, and the vibration responses of 10 FBG sensors on the blade are collected under different working conditions. The natural freq uency and damping ratio of the blade are identified by the expe rimental method, and the corresponding modal pattern is recon structed. The research results break through the limitations of the normal-scale state parameter identification method, such as weak anti-noise interference, low resolution, false mode and di fficulty in order determination, which is helpful to improve the modal parameter identification accuracy and reduce the influe nce of noise.

articleTitle: Lightweight Mobile Phone Screen Flaw Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Aiming at the demand for detecting small defects on the surface of cell phone screens with highly reflective characteristics in industrial production, a lightweight detection algorithm for small defects on the surface of highly reflective media based on improved YOLOv8 (MGND-YOLOv8n) is proposed, which realizes a great reduction of computational volume and model parameters under the premise of guaranteeing the accuracy and effectively improves the detection speed. This algorithm employs the lightweight structure of MobileNetV3 to substitute the backbone structure of YOLOv8, thereby enhancing portability and realizing the lightweight network model. Additionally, GSConv and Slim-Neck structures are incorporated at the neck end of YOLOv8 to mitigate redundancy and duplicate information. To maintain the detection speed and reduce the complexity of the model, a detection head based on group normalization convolution is devised. Finally, the WIoU-v3 loss function is utilized to account for the quality imbalance of defective samples. Compared with CIoU, this effectively enhances the gradient gain distribution, improves the convergence speed and regression accuracy. Experimental results show that, compared with the original YOLOv8 algorithm, the proposed algorithm improves the average accuracy of mobile phone screen defect detection results by 1.7% at mAP@0.5, reduces the model parameters and computational load by 56.8% and 67.6% respectively, and the detection speed reaches 134.8FPS.

articleTitle: A Mask Disentanglement Domain Generalization Method for Bearings Remaining Useful Life Prediction Under Unknown Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Domain adaptation has proven to be a successful method for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) prognostic tasks in cross-domain scenarios. However, due to the reliance on target data, these methods are difficult to deploy to RUL prediction tasks under unknown operating conditions (OCs). Additionally, existing RUL prediction methods under unknown OCs try to learn domain-invariant features, ignoring domain-specific features that are beneficial for enhancing generalization to target tasks. To eliminate dependency on target data and consider label-relevant information in domain-specific features, a mask disentanglement domain generalization (MDDG) framework is proposed. Specifically, a binary mask is used to disentangle latent features into label-relevant and label-irrelevant features, instead of using multiple encoders. Then, an information theory-based loss is designed to ensure that label-relevant features contain sufficient degradation information, while label-irrelevant features have enough domain information. Finally, a pairing loss is developed to reduce the difference in label-relevant features between samples with similar labels from different domains, facilitating generalization to unknown target domains. Experiments conducted on a run-to-failure bearing dataset demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Reliability Evaluation Approach for Aircraft Hydraulic Tube System Based on Pulsating Stress Test Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the current aircraft system, the hydraulic system is mainly responsible for providing or transferring power to the operating system, power retracting system, braking system, etc., and plays a key role in the safe flight of the aircraft. Due to the huge system, limitation of test equipment, complicated engineering technology or other reasons, the objects of hydraulic tube pulsation stress test that must be carried out after the design and modification of the hydraulic system are individual tubes. Therefore, the research on the reliability of the whole hydraulic system is not sufficient. However, the system reliability assessment method can evaluate the reliability of the overall system by analyzing the failure data of components and subsystems, which has natural advantages to solve the above problems. Based on the existing pulsating stress test data of the hydraulic system tube, this paper uses the system reliability assessment method to evaluate the overall reliability of the hydraulic tube system, providing data support and decision-making basis for product design, improvement, finalization and production. Finally, the feasibility of the method is verified by example calculation.

articleTitle: A Few-Shot Fault Diagnosis Method for Train Transmission Systems Based on Spatial Median Prototypical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis methods based on few-shot learning are able to diagnose train transmission systems with scarce training samples accurately. However, the training samples may be mislabeled in engineering scenes, and the existing few-shot fault diagnosis methods lack robust learning strategies for partially mislabeled training samples, resulting in degradation of diagnosis accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a few-shot fault diagnosis method for train transmission systems based on spatial median prototypical networks. Firstly, according to prototypical networks, a prototype aggregation with mislabeling tolerance strategy is adopted, where the prototype deviation caused by the mislabeled support samples is alleviated by calculating the spatial median of the fault features instead of the mean of fault features in the prototype aggregation process. After that, a mislabeling suppression loss function is introduced to reduce the interference of mislabeled query samples on parameter updating by adopting a novel definition of the loss function. Finally, fault simulation experiments of subway train transmission systems are designed and conducted, and the experimental results show that even if the mislabeled samples are mixed in the limited training datasets, the proposed method is still able to diagnose the faults of train transmission systems accurately, and the diagnosis performance is better than that of the existing methods.

articleTitle: A Feature Pyramid Residual Network with Attention Mechanism for Wafer Map Mixed Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the semiconductor industry, wafer defect detection is facing unprecedented challenges as a key application of object detection. Lots of complex steps in the wafer manufacturing process can lead to defects and identifying these defect patterns accurately is critical to preventing defects and improving process reliability and product yields. With the complexity of the manufacturing process, the number of wafer map mixed defect has increased, which puts forward higher requirements for recognition accuracy. The existing deep learning-based defect recognition methods do not take into account the existence of multi-scale defects with different sizes when dealing with wafer map mixed defect, and the mixed diversity of wafer defect also limits the accuracy of the existing recognition methods. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a feature pyramid residual network (FPRN) with convolutional block attention module (CBAM) named FPRN-CBAM. The FPRN-CBAM model not only realizes multi-scale feature fusion for wafer map mixed defect detection (WMMDD), but also enhances the defect feature representation by adaptively assigning channels and spatial weights. To verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model, this paper uses the MixedWM38 dataset for experiments. The results show that the proposed model is effective in detecting multi-scale features of wafer maps, which leads to better performance in recognizing mixed defect patterns.

articleTitle: An In-Situ Method for Health Condition Monitoring of SiC Power MOSFETs Under Repetitive Short-Circuit Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the Silicon-Carbide (SiC) based power conversion system (PCS), SiC power MOSFET is one of the core devices in the system. Therefore, the health condition monitoring of SiC power MOSFETs is important. In this work, the variations of threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> ) and gate-source leakage current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gss</inf> ) are converted into the changing rate of drain-source voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds</inf> ), and the changing rate of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds</inf> is selected as the new aging-sensitive parameter. Then, a health condition monitoring method based on the principle of capacitive coupling is proposed. The method is completed by using a voltage sensor without any additional circuits, and the corresponding modeling is carried out for the SiC power MOSFETs. Besides, Short-Circuit (SC) stress is applied to degrade the devices, and the degradation behavior is investigated. Moreover, the health condition monitoring method has been simulated and experimentally verified in the Boost converter, the simulation and experimental results show that the changing rate of drain-source voltage of the devices in the Boost converter could be used to indicate the degree of degradation of SiC power MOSFETs. The work may be useful for degradation monitoring of the SiC power MOSFETs in PCS.

articleTitle: Reliability Modelling Method for Phased Mission System Considering Multi-Phase Continuous Backup Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: To achieve high reliability of the phased mission system (PMS), the phase backup strategy is always designed except for the redundant components. In the traditional phase backup strategy, only one phase is backed up at a time. However, in some PMS, continuous backup of multiple phases will occur, that is, if a task in a certain phase of the system fails, the system will go back to one or more phases prior to this phase, and re-execute these tasks in sequence. For this problem, a reliability modelling method of PMS considering multi-phase continuous backup strategy is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the subsystem composition of a UAV and its mission phases under multi-phase continuous backup strategy are analyzed. Secondly, a new model based on binary decision diagram model for phased mission system (PMS-BDD) is developed to model the mission reliability of the UAV considering multi-phase continuous backup strategy. Thirdly, according to the accelerated failure model and Poisson process, the analytical expression of mission reliability of the UAV in the case of random shock is derived. Finally, a case study on a UAV's reconnaissance strike mission is used to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Optimization Method with Multiple Objectives for the Emergency Maintenance Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: A timely emergency maintenance operation can prevent the failure problem from getting worse. And it can eliminate potential safety hazards and ensure the safety of operators and the equipment. A two-stage optimization method with multiple objectives for the emergency maintenance process is proposed. Firstly, a Graphical Evaluation and Review Technique (GERT) model is established to describe and evaluate the emergency maintenance process. Expected expressions of maintenance time and maintenance effectiveness are derived based on the GERT model, which are set as multi-objective optimization functions. The tradeoff between the optimal maintenance time and maintenance effectiveness is realized by the multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) algorithm. Based on the obtained Pareto optimal solution sets through MOPSO algorithm, the maintenance time and maintenance effectiveness are re-optimized with the goal of the minimum system performance loss to determine exact optimization results. The proposed method is demonstrated by taking the emergency maintenance process optimization of the subsea tree as a case.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Bearings Based on Game Theory Feature Selection and Channel Attention-Enhanced TCN
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: The prediction of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) for rolling bearings is a critical step in the Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) of rotating machinery. However, RUL prediction continues to face challenges, such as the difficulty in extracting vibration-sensitive features of rolling bearings from condition monitoring signals containing substantial redundant information, and the neglect of bearings' multi-stage degradation characteristics in RUL prediction, resulting in reduced accuracy of prediction methods. In response to these challenges, this study proposes a novel data-driven approach. Firstly, a dynamic weight determination method based on game theory combination weighting is implemented to construct comprehensive evaluation indicators, thereby identifying feature sets sensitive to the degradation process. Secondly, a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) integrated with the Squeeze-and-Excitation Network (SEN) attention mechanism is employed for multi-stage life prediction. The incorporation of SEN not only enhances the model's ability to capture complex temporal patterns but also improves its adaptability and robustness. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using publicly available bearing datasets.

articleTitle: A Method for Identifying Loose State of Bolt Groups in Composite Lapped Panels Based on Fiber Optic Strain Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: In the service process of aerospace composite lapped panels, the bolted connection structures may become loose due to the action of vibration and fatigue loads. Real-time monitoring of the bolt tightening state is of great significance for ensuring the reliability and safety of the lapped structure. To this end, this paper develops a method for identifying the loosening state of a group of bolts based on strain modal parameters, and proposes four quantification indices for the loosening state of bolts, which are based on the differences and relative change rates of strain modes of different orders. By constructing a threshold for identifying the loosening state of bolts based on strain modal parameters, precise identification of the loosening state of multiple bolts is achieved. A sensitivity evaluation index for loosening identification is defined, and the identification effects of bolt loosening states are presented based on four indices, including the differences and relative change rates of strain modes of different orders. On this basis, a monitor and identification system for the loosening state of the bolt group in composite lapped panels was constructed based on quasi-distributed fiber optic strain sensing. This system overcomes the difficulty of synchronous monitor and identification of the loosening state of multiple bolt connections on the lapped panel. The research outcomes can provide technical support for identification of bolt group loosening states during the manufacturing, assembly, and service stages of aerospace equipment, aiding their maintenance and inspection.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method for Check Valve Based on Stochastic Subspace Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Swing check valve plays a key role in preventing countercurrent in complex pipeline systems such as nuclear power plant. Aiming at the problem that swing check valve in loop devices is prone to stall and other faults during long-term operation and difficult to monitor, a fault diagnosis method based on stochastic subspace identification is proposed. The method can calculate and process the acceleration response data of check valve in real time. After calculating the modal parameters, the deviation from the standard modal parameters is calculated to realize the fault diagnosis and detection of the check valve. The feasibility of the proposed method is verified by simulation analysis from explicit dynamics and modal aspects respectively. Finally, the method is verified by experiments. The test results show that the check valve with stuck fault can be effectively monitored and identified by the method during the test, and the method has certain guiding significance for the fault detection of the valve without periodic characteristics in the loop.

articleTitle: Cross Varying-Speed Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Multi-Sensor Information Fusion and Domain Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Beijing)
abstract: Current researches in deep transfer learning for fault diagnosis predominantly assume the constant-speed operating condition. However, in real-world industrial scenarios, dynamical production environments often result in time-varying speed conditions. Therefore, this study proposes a novel cross-domain diagnostic approach integrating energy weighted signal fusion (EWSF) with a domain adaptation feature enhancement network (DAFEN). Firstly, the EWSF technique amalgamates data from diverse sensors, amplifying the key information within signals. Subsequently, a global-local feature enhancement module (GLFEM) is developed to capture the invariant features across various domains. Finally, an integrated DAFEN with GLFEM is designed to achieve cross-domain diagnosis under time-varying speed conditions. The proposed method was implemented and verified on planetary gearbox dataset. Experimental results show that the proposed EWSF-DAFEN method outperformed comparative methods, achieving an impressive average accuracy of 96.24% across seven transfer diagnosis tasks, thereby proving its robust domain adaptation and cross-domain fault diagnostic capability.
